original: You force yourself to remember who you currently are.
translation: 你强迫自己记住你现在是谁。

original: A newfound lucidity
translation: 新发现的清醒

original: Painful memories seep away like bad dreams dissolved in dawn. Fond memories vanish too.
translation: 痛苦的回忆如溶解在黎明中的恶梦一样逐渐消失。温情的回忆也随之消逝了。

original: Relocation
translation: 重新安置

original:
In one of Piranesi's cold stone rooms, you discover a strangely familiar red-and-gold dollhouse. Lifting the roof, you find that one of the dolls has your face. 

It would be easy to reach inside and grab it. You could smash it, or put it in one of Piranei's damp cobwebbed corners.
translation:
在皮拉内西的一间冰冷的石屋里，你发现了一座奇怪而又熟悉的红金色玩偶屋。掀开屋顶，你发现其中一个玩偶长着你的脸。

你很容易就能伸手进去把它抓出来。你可以把它砸碎，或者把它放在皮拉内西那些潮湿布满蛛网的角落里。

original: From gold fittings to damp stone walls
translation: 从金黄陈设到潮湿石墙

original: Hotel? What hotel? Sometimes they called the old gaol a hotel, but only in jest.
translation: 酒店？什么酒店？有时他们称旧监狱为酒店，但那只是个玩笑。

original: Never mind all that
translation: 无视这一切

original: You force yourself to remember who you currently are.
translation: 你强迫自己记住你现在是谁。

original: Indiscretions, forgotten
translation: 忘却污点

original: You no longer take any pride in your notoriety, nor feel any shame.
translation: 你不再为自己的恶名感到骄傲，也不再为之感到羞耻。

original: Revision
translation: 修订

original:
You come across a bookshelf. Upon it: a thick layer of dust, a fountain pen, and a single book. You recognise it. Your old diary, from before you commanded a train.

When you open it, the ink crumbles away at a brush of your fingernail. It would take no effort at all to scrub out these old words and add new ones.
translation:
你遇到一个书架。上面有一层厚厚的灰尘，一支钢笔，和一本书。你认出了它。那是在你在指挥火车前写的旧日记。

当你打开它时，只要用指甲一划，墨迹便会碎裂。抹掉旧字，加上新字，一点也不费力。

original: From infamy to prestige
translation: 从声名狼藉到声名鹊起

original: Scandal? No, you must be misremembering. You did great things, and your reputation is pristine.
translation: 丑闻？不，你一定是记错了。你做了伟大的事情，你的声誉是纯洁的。

original: Never mind all that
translation: 无视这一切

original: You force yourself to remember who you currently are.
translation: 你强迫自己记住你现在是谁。

original: Indiscretions, forgotten
translation: 忘却污点

original: You no longer take any pride in your notoriety, nor feel any shame.
translation: 你不再为自己的恶名感到骄傲，也不再为之感到羞耻。

original: Revision
translation: 修订

original:
You come across a bookshelf. Upon it: a thick layer of dust, a fountain pen, and a single book. You recognise it. Your old diary, from before you commanded a train.

When you open it, the ink crumbles away at a brush of your fingernail. It would take no effort at all to scrub out these old words and add new ones.
translation:
你遇到一个书架。上面有一层厚厚的灰尘，一支钢笔，和一本书。你认出了它。那是在你在指挥火车前写的旧日记。

当你打开它时，只要用指甲一划，墨迹便会碎裂。抹掉旧字，加上新字，一点也不费力。

original: From locks of hair to locks on doors
translation: 从发丝的锁结到门关的锁结

original: No debauchery for you. Just gruel, and a damp stone cell.
translation: 放荡不再。只有稀粥和潮湿的石牢。

original: Never mind all that
translation: 无视这一切

original: You force yourself to remember who you currently are.
translation: 你强迫自己记住你现在是谁。

original: Substitution
translation: 替代

original:
You stroll beside the Reformer, past colossal stone heads and delicate marble figures. When you ask him to be your scapegoat, he offers you a pained smile.

"I can help more people as a Chaplain than as a prisoner. Why should I take your place?"
translation:
你经过硕大的石头头像和精致的大理石塑像，走到了改过者身边。当你请求他成为你的替罪羊时，他向你露出痛苦的微笑。

“作为牧师时，我能够帮助的人比作为囚犯时要多。我为什么要代替你呢？”

original: Convince him
translation: 说服他

original: The goodness of his heart?
translation: 出于他心底的善良？

original: A Defeated Sigh
translation: 被打败的叹息

original:
You beg, you bargain, you promise to devote your life to good deeds. The Reformer shakes his head, but you don't let up. By the time you're finished pleading, he is sitting with his head bowed.

"Very well," he says finally. "But you don't know what you're doing. Without me, this place will be left to the care of the other three, whose efforts are misguided at best. And Piranesi will change me again. I dread to think..." He trails off.

Without another word, he guides you to the exit. The lamp falls from your wrist, and he shackles it to his own. "Go before I change my mind," he says.

[The Gallant Reformer is now imprisoned!]
translation:
你乞求，你讨价还价，你承诺将你的生命投入到善行中。改过者摇了摇头，但你并没有松口。当你的恳求结束时，他已经低头坐在了地上。

“很好，”他最后说，“但你不知道你在做什么。没有我，这个地方会被留给其他三个人打理，他们的努力从最好的角度来看也是完全用错了地方。而皮拉内西将再次改变我。我不敢想……”他的话音渐渐淡去。

他没有再说话，而是把你带到了出口。灯从你的手腕上掉下来，他把它铐在自己的手腕上。“在我改变主意之前，快走吧！”他说。

[无畏的改过者入狱了！]

original: No Luck
translation: 不走运

original: You beg, you bargain, you plead, but the Reformer just smiles and tells you to stop making a fool of yourself. He was a prisoner once before, and look at all the good it did him.
translation: 你乞求，你讨价还价，你恳求，但改过者只是笑笑，告诉你不要再丢人现眼了。他曾经当过囚犯，看看这给他带来了多少好处。

original: Use his secret to convince him
translation: 用他的秘密来说服他

original: He was once a notorious villain. Has he changed so much?
translation: 他曾经是一个臭名昭著的恶棍。他有这么大的变化吗？

original: A Return to the Old Ways
translation: 重返旧路

original:
Your words hang in the air like a cloud of poison. The Reformer shakes his head, a strange light in his eyes.

"It is so tiring to be good," he says finally. "I remember very little from my old life, but I know I didn't have to wrestle with all this guilt." He stares at a half-eroded statue. "Perhaps Piranesi will change me back. Perhaps I've done enough good for one lifetime."

Without another word, he guides you to the exit. The lamp falls from your wrist, and he shackles it to his own. His smile is sad and terrible.

[The Gallant Reformer is now imprisoned!]
translation:
你的话像一团毒云一样悬在空气中。改过者摇摇头，眼底闪过一道奇怪的光。

“做好人太累了，”他最后说，“我对过去的生活知之甚少，但我知道我不必与所有这些内疚搏斗。”他盯着一尊半被侵蚀的雕像，“也许皮拉内西会把我变回来。也许我这辈子做的好事已经够多了。”

他没有再说话，而是把你带到了出口。灯从你的手腕上掉下来，他把它铐在自己的手腕上。他的微笑是悲凉而可怖。

[无畏的改过者入狱了！]

original: A Stern Rebuke
translation: 严声斥责

original: "Don't you dare!" The Reformer draws himself to his full height, grey eyebrows bristling fiercely. "Don't mention my old self again. That man is dead, and lives on only as a shadow in my dreams."
translation: “你敢！”无畏的改过者挺直身子，猛地竖起了灰色眉毛。“别再提以前的我了。那个人已经死了，现下只是活在我梦里的一个影子。”

original: Appeal to your friendship
translation: 提及你们的友谊

original: You've built a close rapport with the Reformer. Won't he help you in your hour of need?
translation: 你和改过者建立了密切的关系。在你需要的时候，他会不会帮助你呢？

original: A Defeated Sigh
translation: 被打败的叹息

original:
You beg, you bargain, you recall the good times you've spent together. The Reformer shakes his head, but you don't let up. By the time you're finished pleading, he sits with his head bowed.

"Very well," he says finally. "For the sake of friendship. Remember me."

Without another word, he guides you to the exit. The lamp falls from your wrist, and he shackles it to his own. "Go before I change my mind," he says.

[The Gallant Reformer is now imprisoned!]
translation:
你乞求，你讨价还价，你提起起你们一起度过的美好时光。改过者摇了摇头，但你并没有松口。当你的恳求结束时，他已经低头坐在了地上。

“很好，”他最后说，“以友谊的名义。记住我。”

他没有再说话，而是把你带到了出口。灯从你的手腕上掉下来，他把它铐在自己的手腕上。“在我改变主意之前，快走吧！”他说。

[无畏的改过者入狱了！]

original: No Luck
translation: 不走运

original: You beg, you bargain, you plead, but the Reformer just shakes his head sadly. He was a prisoner once before, and has no desire to revisit the experience. Not even for a friend.
translation: 你乞求，你讨价还价，你恳求，但改过者只是悲伤地摇摇头。他已经被囚禁过一次，并且不想再经历第二次。即使是为了朋友也不行。

original: Turn away from the Reformer
translation: 转身离开改过者

original: There's nothing he can do for you.
translation: 他不能为你做什么。

original: A Grave Mistake
translation: 要命的错误

original: [qvd:135568(Grave)]
translation: [qvd:135568(Grave)]

original: Approach the corpses
translation: 接近尸体

original: They are key to whatever befell the Boatman.
translation: 他们是了解船夫号遭遇的关键。

original: A greeting, of sorts
translation: 某种程度上，是一种问候

original: The leader extends one bony hand, its limb shaking from the weight of yet-unsloughed flesh.
translation: 首领伸出一只骨手，它的肢体在未脱落的肉的重量下颤抖。

original: Introduce yourself
translation: 介绍自己

original: It's only polite.
translation: 遵守礼节。

original:
The corpse nods stiffly. Its fingers close around your own. There is an uncomfortable moment where you almost leave with more fingers than you started with, but eventually, and with many a courteous "Excuse me!", you extract yourselves. 

"We're glad you didn't run away," the skeleton says.
translation:
尸体僵硬地点点头。它的手指紧抓住你的手指。有一瞬间，几乎把它的指头拔下来的感觉让你有些不适，但最终，在许多声礼貌的“抱歉！”中，你们彼此都脱了身。

“我们很高兴你没有逃跑，”骷髅说。

original: Pull off the ridiculous corpse mask
translation: 扯下那可笑的尸体面具

original: Enough of this farce! Walking corpses? Staged tableaux? This theatrical display may fool lesser minds, but not you.
translation: 闹剧该结束了！行走的尸体？舞台布景？这种戏剧表演可能会骗过蠢人，但不会骗过你。

original:
The leader lowers his rotting head. The flesh is chill as meat left on the butcher's block overnight. Aha! You grab two handfuls and tear— 

Flesh sloughs away like mouldering wallpaper, revealing polished bone, white as snow. "Are you done?" the corpse says. 

He pauses while he ascertains that you're not about to run away. "Would you like a brandy?"
translation:
首领低下了他腐烂的头。它的血肉寒冷，如同在砧板上放置了一夜。啊哈！你抓起两把肉，把它撕开——

肉体像腐烂的墙纸一样脱落，露出抛光的雪白骨头。“你还有别的事吗？”尸体问道。

当确定你不会逃跑时，他停了下来。“来点白兰地？”

original: Flee!
translation: 快逃！

original: This engine has been claimed by the dead. Let them keep it.
translation: 这台机车已被死者占据。让他们留着它吧。

original: Away!
translation: 离开！

original:
Away from the mocking sunken faces, and indifferent hollow eyes. One hand, bone shrouded in flaps of skin, reaches out as you pass by – in supplication? Or to grab you?

Back through the freezing carriages, back past the shattered window and the empty cabins, back through the creaking door, and away into the heat and light of your own engine.
translation:
逃离那些嘲弄的凹陷面孔和冷漠的空洞眼窝。一只皮包骨头的手在你经过时伸了出来——是在恳求？还是想抓你？

穿过冰冷的车厢，穿过破碎的窗户和空荡荡的客舱，穿过吱吱作响的门，走进你自己发动机的热和光中。

original: Hear the Deceased Stoker out
translation: 听活死人司炉把话说完

original: He has more to say.
translation: 他有更多的话要说。

original: Articulate, for a dead man
translation: 对于一个死人来说，口齿伶俐

original:
"I should apologise," he says. "We've not had any visitors since the mutiny. Couldn't predict how you'd react. Driving you off with a haunting seemed safest."

"Almost had you," a decaying lady cackles. The fruit in her hat has fused with the exposed parts of her cranium. 

The Stoker clears his crumbling throat. "While our bodies were being transported, the captain steered us through a carelessness in time. Things have gotten tangled, you see. As far as our minds are concerned, we haven't died, but our bodies beg to differ. Vociferously. The last thing I remember from when I was alive is saying farewell to my husband, then heading to the station." 

He looks down at the captain in her coffin. "She's getting agitated again. We've been very decent, considering they tried to throw us into the incinerator the moment we climbed out of our boxes! Anyway, we thought we might face the same treatment elsewhere, so we set out into the wild.  But here we are, stuck without fuel. We'd appreciate help."
translation:
“我应该道歉，”他说。“那次哗变以后，我们再也没有任何访客了。无法预测你会有什么反应。用鬼魂来驱赶你似乎是最稳妥的选择。”

“差点就吓跑你了，”一位腐朽的女士咯咯笑着说道。她帽子上的水果已经与暴露出来的头骨部分融合在一起。

司炉清了清他那破碎的喉咙。“当我们的身体被运送时，车长带领我们穿越了一个时间的漏洞。事情变得错综复杂了，你知道。就我们的意识而言，我们并没有死去，但我们的身体不同意，很强烈的那种。我还记得活着时最后一件事是向我的丈夫告别，然后前往车站。”

他低头看着棺材里的车长。“她又开始激动了。我们已经相当文明体面了，考虑到他们试图在我们一从箱子里爬出来时就把我们扔进焚化炉！无论如何，我们担心其他地方也会对我们采取同样的待遇，所以我们决定深入高荒原。但我们现在被困在这里，没有燃料。我们希望能得到帮助。”

original: Open the coffins
translation: 打开棺材

original: Ignore the protestations of your crew.
translation: 无视你列车员的抗议。

original: Prised open
translation: 被撬开

original:
With the aid of a burly signaller, you raise the lid of the nearest. A piteous groan emerges as you do.

The lid clatters to the ground, revealing the coffin's occupant. A living woman, in the silver-trimmed uniform of the Necropolis Line. Her captain's rank insignia gleams. She is gagged. From what you can see of her face, the skin around her mouth is coated in something brown. It looks like dried food. 

Your crew set to opening the other coffins. Similar discoveries are made. 

The captain struggles in her bonds, and moans from behind her gag.
translation:
在一位魁梧的信号员的帮助下，你抬起了最近的一个棺材盖。随着盖子被抬起，传来一阵引人同情的呻吟声。

盖子哐当一声掉在地上，露出了棺材里的乘客。是一位穿着带有陵墓运输银边制服的的女性，她的车长军衔标志闪闪发光。她被堵住了嘴，从能看到的脸部部分来看，她嘴巴周围的皮肤覆盖着一层棕色的东西，看起来像是干了的食物。

你的列车员们开始打开其他棺材，发现了类似的情况。

这位车长在束缚中挣扎，并且从堵住嘴的东西后面发出低沉的呻吟声。

original: Explore the hold
translation: 探索货舱

original: There are signs of a fight.
translation: 有打斗的痕迹。

original: Black as death
translation: 黑如死神

original: You move through the hold, which is as large as a wealthy family's mausoleum, casting your light before you. Shadows flee, revealing chains holding some of the coffins closed, scuff marks on the floor, a few shreds of black and silver cloth. An insistent scratching comes from a coffin. Knocking from another. Your signaller startles, and stumbles – falling face first onto a coffin, which rocks angrily. The lid slides off to reveal the Boatman's captain: gagged, bound and still very much alive.
translation: 你穿过这个和富家墓室大小相当的货舱，手中的灯光驱散阴影，照亮前路。借着光，你看到几口棺材上绑着锁链、地上有多道凌乱的磨痕，黑色与银色的布片零落四散。 突然，从一口棺材中传来急促的刮擦声，另一口棺材内则传来了敲击声，吓得你的信号员踉跄了几步，脸朝下绊倒在棺材上。那棺材猛烈地晃动起来，棺盖滑落，露出了船夫号的车长：她嘴巴被堵，浑身被缚，但用力挣扎。

original: Look at the figures
translation: 看看那些身影。

original: Who are they? What do they want?
translation: 他们是谁？他们想要什么？

original: An unsettling crowd
translation: 引人不安的人群

original:
You raise your torch, illuminating the figures in the door. This provokes shrieks from your crew.

Sallow-skinned, hollow-eyed, decaying corpses are blocking your escape. Bloody ribcages, broken skulls, exposed bone and sloughing flesh: cadavers.
translation:
你举起火把，照亮了门口的那些身影。这引起了船员们的尖叫声。

脸色蜡黄、眼窝深陷、腐烂的尸体挡住了你们的逃生之路。血淋淋的胸腔、破碎的头骨、暴露的骨头和脱落的血肉：死尸。

original: Reach for your weapon
translation: 伸手拿你的武器

original: Walking corpses! They cannot mean well.
translation: 会动的死尸！他们绝无可能是好意。

original: You reach for your pistol. The cadavers take a step back. "Please!" the nearest rasps, a tall tattered man in a stoker's uniform. "I'm not sure these bodies could survive any more damage."
translation: 你伸手去拿手枪。那些死尸往后退了一步。“求你了！”最近的一个沙哑地恳求道，那是一个穿着司炉工制服的高大男尸。“我不确定这些躯体还能承受多少伤害。”

original: Pray
translation: 祈祷

original: What good are weapons against the walking dead?
translation: 面对行尸走肉，武器有什么用？

original: Distressingly, the cadavers join in, mumbling, rasping and otherwise mangling the words. When you finish, the leader, a tall tattered man in a stoker's uniform, thanks you. "Very grateful to you for leading us in that, Captain."
translation: 令人不安的，那些死尸也加入了进来，含糊不清地、沙哑地，甚至破碎地吐出字句。当你结束时，他们的首领，那个穿着司炉工制服的高大破烂男子，感谢你说：“非常感谢你带领我们做了这些，车长。”

original: The Inconvenient Aunt
translation: 令人困扰的姨妈

original:
She has taken over one of your nicer cabins, which she has ruthlessly redecorated. There is a preponderance of ugly ornaments balanced precariously on tiny tables. Hideous antimacassars adorn every available surface. 

Your Aunt occupies a felt armchair in the centre of the horror, where she spends her time either knitting or solving truly mind-boggling cryptic crosswords.
translation:
她霸占了你一间不错的舱位，还无情地重新装修了一遍。小桌子上摇摇欲坠的摆满了不少丑陋的装饰品。难看的护头巾装饰着每一处空间。

你的姨妈坐在那恐怖区域中心处的一把毡绒扶手椅上，她在那里编织毛线或是解决难度惊人的神秘填字游戏。

original: Converse with your Inconvenient Aunt
translation: 与令人困扰的姨妈交谈

original: "I'm rather busy!" she insists. Perhaps if you tell her something ghoulish she'll pay attention to you.
translation: “我很忙！”她强调。也许告诉她一些可怕残忍的事情，她会转而关心你。

original: An evening's entertainment
translation: 一个晚上的娱乐

original:
"Good lord!  Are you all right?" She immediately bakes you a batch of scones. She doesn't even comment on the order in which you apply the jam and the cream. 

"I know what will cheer you up," she says briskly. "I've been invited to a little soiree by Bunty." She pauses. "An old schoolfriend. I think she's Head of the Deniable Constables now. You'll come with me, won't you? It'll take your mind off things."

She considers for a moment. "I must warn you. It's a very particular evening. Old enmities put aside, that sort of thing. It's at Carillon."
translation:
“天哪！你没事吧？”她立即给你烤了一些烤饼。她甚至没有对你涂抹果酱和奶油的顺序发表任何意见。

“我知道什么东西能让你振作起来，”她轻快地说道，“邦蒂邀请我去参加一个小宴会。”她停顿了一下，“一个老同学。我想她现在是秘密警署的负责人。你会和我一起去的，对不对？这能让你忘掉那些事情。”

她考虑了一会儿，“我必须事先警告你，这是一个非常特殊的夜晚。抛开旧有的恩怨情仇，诸如此类。这是在钟琴区。”

original: Question your Aunt
translation: 询问你的姨妈

original: What was all that about St Dunstan's? What got her so shaken up at Carillon?
translation: 关于圣邓斯坦的那些事是怎么回事？是什么让她在钟琴区受到如此大的震动？

original: In Her Majesty's Service
translation: 为女王陛下服务

original: "When I was a gal, I used to do a bit of spying for the Crown. Now, I've been out of the trade for years, but I couldn't help but overhear an intriguing conversation. People rarely pay attention to ladies of my age." She gives you a look, as though daring you to disagree. "They said Revolutionaries helped our government conquer Albion! They mentioned a secret rendezvous at St Dunstan's, between four representatives: a New Sequencer, a revolutionary, and two members of Her Majesty's Government! I have to get to the bottom of this. It is my duty!" She tilts her chin defiantly. "I've a friend at Port Prosper who owes me a favour. And we can get lunch!"
translation: “当我还是个小妮子的时候，曾经为王室做了一些间谍工作。现在，我已经离开这个行业很多年了，但我还是忍不住偷听了一段有趣的对话。一般人很少注意到在我这个年龄段的女士。”她看了你一眼，仿佛是让你不敢有异议。 “他们说革命者帮助我们的政府征服了阿尔比恩！他们提到了一个在圣邓斯坦的秘密集会，有四个代表：一个新秩序者，一个革命家，还有两个女王陛下的政府成员！我必须把这件事查个水落石出，这是我的职责！”她轻蔑地仰起下巴。“我在兴荣港有个朋友，他欠我一个人情。而且我们可以吃午饭！”

original: Quiz your Aunt
translation: 盘问你的姨妈

original: What has she gotten involved in? And what's this with the Christmas card?
translation: 她卷入了什么事情？这张圣诞贺卡又是怎么回事？

original: The Calendar Council
translation: 日历会

original:
"One tick, deary. Just looking for— Aha!" The clink of glass. Your Aunt rises from an open suitcase clutching a dusty bottle of brandy. 

"We've got to get to Pan, in Eleutheria. That's where February is. Though she wasn't February when I knew her. She was my opposite number back in— But you want answers.

"February's on the Calendar Council. The Revolutionary leadership. The Christmas card'll get us into Winter's Reside." Your Aunt brandishes the bottle. "She has a fondness for brandy. I've been saving this for if I ran into her again. It should get us into her good graces. She'll be able to tell us what went on at St Dunstan's."
translation:
“稍等一下，亲爱的。我在找——啊哈！”玻璃杯的叮当声响起。你的姨妈从打开的行李箱旁站起身，手里拿着瓶布满灰尘的白兰地。

“我们得去潘城，在厄琉忒里亚。二月就在那里。虽然我刚认识她时，她还不是二月。我们那时是对头，但要想知道答案，就只能找她了。”

“日历会是革命军的领导机构，二月就是其中一员。有了圣诞贺卡，我们就能进入冬日之居。”姨妈挥舞着瓶子继续讲道：“她对白兰地情有独钟，所以我一直留着这酒，就怕我俩有一天会重逢。她应该会喜欢这酒，然后告诉我们在圣邓斯坦教堂里发生过什么。”

original: Help your Aunt go through February's papers
translation: 帮你的姨妈翻阅二月的文件

original: The secrets of St Dunstan's Rendezvous are locked behind a nigh impenetrable cipher.
translation: 圣邓斯坦集会的秘密被锁在一个几乎无法攻破的密码后面。

original: The Revolution betrayed
translation: 被出卖的革命

original:
Piles of pages are strewn across her cabin. "I've been impersonating February in some correspondence to get more information," your Aunt says in explanation. "It's not like she's going to object."

Working together, you discover the key to the cipher: various calendars – from the Roman to the Revolutionary. From the documents, you learn that February knew that the final design for the bomb was held by Her Majesty's Privy Counsellor. He died and is now interred in the Most Serene Mausoleum.

"If we could find those designs, we'd know for certain what our government agreed to," your Aunt says.
translation:
成堆的书页散落在她的舱室。“我在一些信件中假冒二月，以获取更多信符的信息，”你的姨妈解释说，“她又不会反对。”

你们一起工作，发现了密码的关键：从罗马时代到革命时代的各种日历。从这些文件中，你了解到二月知道炸弹的最终设计是由女王陛下的枢密院顾问掌握的。他死了，现在被埋在圣宁墓里。

“如果我们能找到这些设计，我们就能确定我们的政府同意了什么，”你的姨妈说。

original: Talk to your Aunt about the Unclear Bomb
translation: 与你的姨妈谈论晦暗炸弹

original: You found it hidden in Her Majesty's Privy Counsellor's Tomb.
translation: 你发现它藏在女王陛下枢密院顾问的墓中。

original: An Audience
translation: 一个听众

original:
Your Aunt looks up from an ancient, battered etiquette book. "This is from my schooldays," she says with a wistful smile. 

Her focus sharpens. "We need to know why London colluded with the Revolutionaries to build this dreadful weapon and then didn't use it. There were four people at the Rendezvous. Two – three now – are dead. There's only one person who can give us the answers we need: Her Renewed Majesty."

Your Aunt barrels on. "There's an old protocol we could take advantage of. If we had a Royal Dispensation, we could use the Privilege of an Answer to get an audience. The Sovereign is behoven to answer one question truthfully."
translation:
你的姨妈从一本古老的、破损的礼仪书中抬起头来。“这是我学生时代的东西，”她带着怀念的微笑说。

她的注意力更加集中。“我们需要知道为什么伦敦与革命者勾结，制造这种可怕的武器，然后却不使用它。在汇合点有四个人。其中有两个人——现在是三个——死了。只有一个人可以给我们提供我们需要的答案：新生的女王陛下”

你的姨妈继续说着。“我们可以利用一个古老的协议。如果我们有皇家特许状，我们可以利用回答的特权来获得接见。君主有义务如实回答一个问题。”

original: Talk to your Aunt
translation: 与你的姨妈交谈

original:
She's been very quiet since meeting the Queen.
[This will transform your Inconvenient Aunt into Your Spymaster Aunt, a Quartermaster who increases your Iron by 10 and your Affiliation: Establishment by 2.]
translation:
自从见到女王后，她一直很安静。
[这会让令人困扰的姨妈变成你的间谍头目姨妈，一位可使你的钢铁+10，人脉：权贵+2的军需官。]

original: Her Majesty's Woman
translation: 女王陛下的女人

original:
You catch your Aunt burning papers in the boiler room. "Care for tea?" she asks, leading you to her cabin. She gets out her best service.

"I was relieved to speak to the Queen. Our Sovereign's prescience alone kept us from being in thrall to the Revolutionaries." A lump of sugar settles in her teacup. 

"It seems the Albion government has been lax! Getting into messes! And worse, shoddiness when attempting to cover them up!" Her eyes gleam behind her spectacles. "I shall have to come out of retirement. Her Majesty needs me. Though – I'll still have time to help you out here, of course."

[You can appoint Your Spymaster Aunt to be your Quartermaster when you are docked in port.]
translation:
你发现你的姨妈在锅炉房里焚烧文件。她问道：“想喝茶吗？”她把你领到她的小屋。她拿出了她最好的茶。

“和女王的交谈让我如释重负。仅凭我们君主的先见之明，就让我们免于革命者的迷惑。” 一块糖落入她的茶杯。

“看来阿尔比恩政府已经松懈了！陷入混乱！更糟糕的是，在试图掩盖它们的时候，还那么粗心大意！”她的眼睛在眼镜后面闪闪发光。“我不得不离开退休生活。女王陛下需要我。当然，我仍会有时间来这里帮助你。”

[当你在港口停靠时，你可以任命你的间谍头目姨妈为你的军需官。]

original: Talk to your Aunt
translation: 与你的姨妈交谈

original:
She's been very quiet since meeting the Queen.
[This will transform your Inconvenient Aunt into Your Revolutionary Aunt, a Quartermaster who increases your Veils by 10 and your Affiliation: Villainy by 2.]
translation:
自从见到女王后，她一直很安静。
[这会让令人困扰的姨妈变成你的革命者姨妈，一位可使你的面纱+10，人脉：恶棍+2的军需官。]

original: The shortest month
translation: 最短的一个月

original:
Your Aunt is sealing letters into envelopes. "There is work to be done!" she cries, applying a stamp with the force of someone hammering a nail into a fence post. 

"I've been thinking about our meeting with Her Majesty. What she said. Our government colluded with the Revolutionaries and has been lying to us all for years! To say nothing of Her Majesty's ambitions." She sighs a deep and weary sigh.

"The truth must out. I will continue as February. I shall be tireless against this tyranny." She smiles, ferociously. "And I'll continue to help you out, of course! I am still your Aunt after all."

[You can appoint Your Revolutionary Aunt to be your Quartermaster when you are docked in port.]
translation:
你的姨妈正在给信加封。她喊道：“有工作要做！”她用敲打钉子的力气在地址栏上盖了一个章。

“我一直在想我们与女王陛下的会面。她说的话。我们的政府与革命者勾结，多年来一直在对我们所有人撒谎！更别提女王陛下的抱负了。”她深深地、疲惫地叹了口气。

“真相必须查明。我会继续假扮二月。我会不懈地反对这种暴政。”她笑了，面容狰狞，“当然，我还会继续帮助你！毕竟我还是你的姨妈。”

[当你在港口停靠时，你可以任命你的革命者姨妈为你的军需官。]

original: Attempt a translation
translation: 试着翻译一下

original: See if you can decipher the Correspondence scored into the Throne of Hours.
translation: 看看你是否能破译被记入时间王座的信符。

original: See what your Aunt is up to
translation: 看看你的姨妈在做什么

original: A smell of baking wafts through your locomotive.
translation: 一股烤饼的味道在你的机车上萦绕。

original: Uninvited
translation: 现在不欢迎你

original: It emerges that your Aunt is holding a tea party for those of your crew plagued with bad dreams. You're not invited. "It's nothing personal, dear. They just won't feel able to speak freely if their captain can hear. They know they can always trust Aunty to keep a secret." She closes the door.
translation: 你的姨妈正在为那些被恶梦困扰的列车员举办茶会。你没有被邀请。“这不是针对你，亲爱的。他们只是觉得如果他们的车长能听到，他们就没法畅所欲言。他们知道可以相信姨妈总会保守秘密的。”她关上了门。

original: A Secondment: Listen to Aunty's suggestion
translation: 借调：听取姨妈的建议

original: She's been baking up a storm. This usually means she wants something.
translation: 她一直在疯狂地烤着东西。这通常意味着她需要什么。

original: Possible employment for an Aunt
translation: 姨妈或许能做的工作

original:
"Just an idle thought," she says, presenting you with a new batch of sourdough loaves. She frowns at the consistency of the bread, as though she expects it to get its act together sharpish.

"But if you wish to make use of my full arsenal of talents, you might want to grant me shore leave at the Most Serene Mausoleum." Her eyes gleam behind her horn-rimmed spectacles. "I have ideas. But if you think I'm more valuable aboard your engine, that's up to you."

[Your Aunt will be able to generate Barrels of Unseasoned Hours for you while seconded at the Most Serene Mausoleum.]
translation:
“我也就这么一说啊，”她说着，向你展示了一批新的酵母面包。她皱着眉观察着面包的整体，好像她希望它能迅速地振作起来。

“但是，如果想利用我的全部才能，你得让我在圣宁墓下车。”她的眼睛在角质框眼镜后面闪闪发光。“我有些想法。但如果你认为我在你的机车上更有价值，那就由你决定。”

[你的姨妈借调至圣宁墓时，能为你生产桶装的未加工的时间。]

original: Approaching the Parzifal
translation: 驶近帕西法尔号

original:
The engine drifts unhappily through the sky. Its hull has been split by an eruption of corpse-white fungus from inside. The name 'Parzifal' can be made out in brass letters on its side. 

"The first engine through the Avid Horizon," a navigator whispers, "London's pride. She was captained by Lt Commander Percy Blythe, and her mission was to chart new horizons beyond Albion. But she never came back."
translation:
机车在天野中缓缓漂荡，模样凄楚。尸白色真菌撕裂车体，自内部疯长出来。侧舷上还能辨出用黄铜拼成的名字：“帕西法尔号”。

一位领航员轻声叹道：“第一辆穿越渴求之地平线的机车啊，伦敦的骄傲。这车由珀西·布莱斯上尉负责指挥，本要去绘制阿尔比恩之外地区的航图，却再也没能返航。”

original: Board the Parzifal
translation: 登上帕西法尔号

original: What happened to the first engine in the High Wilderness? Its doors are sealed, its lights dim. It drifts in the currents, mangled by fungal extrusions.
translation: 第一台抵达天野的机车上发生了什么？帕西法尔号在风中飘荡，车门禁闭，车灯昏暗，车体被真菌挤压得支离破碎。

original:
Bolt-cutters and pry-bars are required to break the outer door. Its locking mechanism is antiquated and slickened with an oily substance.

You wrench the door open, and are immediately greeted with a cloud of yellowing spores. Your vision blurs, just as your navigator torches them, igniting the air with burning fungus. A few gaslights flicker on the walls. The scratchy sounds of a gramophone can be heard.
translation:
要用螺栓切割器和撬棍才能打破外门。它的锁具很陈旧，而且沾有油状物质。

你扳开门，立刻就有一团发黄的孢子迎面而来。你的领航员拿出火炬，利用空气引燃真菌时，你的视线模糊了。几盏煤气灯在墙上闪烁。能听到留声机的刺耳声音。

original: Return to the Parzifal
translation: 返回帕西法尔号上

original: You have unfinished business with the Pride of London.
translation: 帕西法尔号是伦敦的骄傲，你在此车上还有未竟之事。

original: Back amongst the fruiting carriages, where the walls sprout terrible blossoms. Back to the hateful sound of the gramophone, and the sweet scent of rot, like sanctity defiled.
translation: 回到那遍布真菌，墙壁上涌现可怖花簇的车厢。回到留声机发出可恨噪音里，以及神圣被亵渎时会散发的，腐烂的甜美气味里。

original: Attempt to board the Parzifal
translation: 尝试登上帕西法尔号

original: Is it worth looking back?
translation: 这里值得回访吗？

original: Empty, all empty
translation: 空无一物

original: The fungus-strewn engine is empty; silent as the grave it has become. Whatever walks here now, does so alone and unmourned. There is nothing more for you to find.
translation: 长满真菌的车厢空无一物；一片寂静，如同它已成为的坟墓。现在无论是谁在这里行走，都是孤独的，无人哀悼。你在这里找不到别的东西了。

original: Wreck of the Parzifal
translation: 帕西法尔号的残骸

original: [qvd:135754(Parzifal)]
translation: [qvd:135754(Parzifal)]

original: Enter the captain's cabin
translation: 进入车长室

original: In the first designs for London's engines, the captain always roomed towards the back of the train, for their protection.
translation: 在伦敦机车的初版设计中，为了保护车长，他们的房间往往被安排在车尾。

original:
Plush seats surround a decaying paper map, placed on a mahogany table. Drinks, some floating with mildew, have been poured in glasses around the table. Maps hang from sprouting fronds like peeling wallpaper. Spores float gently through the room. 

Logbooks lie scattered about the table. None date from after 1897. The engine's destination was to be Traitor's Wood. The last entry regards a stop at Hybras, which they named Hy-Brasil. Something was brought on board.

The captain's bunk has collapsed in a pile of rotten wood and infected bedsheets, wet with fungal growths.
translation:
长毛绒座椅中央是一张红木桌子，上面放着破烂的纸质地图。饮料，其中一些漂浮着霉菌，装在桌子边缘的玻璃杯里。地图像剥落的墙纸一样挂在抽条的卷叶上。孢子在房间里轻轻地漂浮着。

航行日志散落在桌上，所有记录在1897年以后就此终止。机车的目的地是叛徒之林。最后一条记录提到了在海波拉的一个站点，他们将其命名为海-波拉西。有东西被带到了列车上。

车长的床铺已经崩解成了一堆腐烂的木头和发霉的床单，潮乎乎的，还长满了真菌。

original: Investigate the armoury
translation: 调查军械库

original: An explorer engine like the Parzifal would have been stocked for all eventualities.
translation: 像帕西法尔号这样的探索型机车会为任何可能出现的情况做好准备。

original:
The solid iron walls of the armoury are stained and rotted with sporing bodies.  Lockers hang open, revealing decaying and antiquated sky-suits. The old design, with thermal chest-plate and brass buttons for fastenings. Several of your crew coo appreciatively, but back away when a prodding of one suit reveals a fruiting colony of golden-black mushrooms has sprouted within.

Amongst the outdated (and unused) weaponry you uncover a trove of novels. Fanciful stuff, but all concerned with the possibilities of space-travel, and the interaction between modern man and the alien.
translation:
军械室坚实的铁墙上糊满了腐烂的尸体，气味刺鼻。储物柜被打开，露出了里面破烂的旧式潜天装。老式的设计，有着胸前的保温板和铜质扣子。你的几个列车员发出赞赏的咕哝，但在发现其中一件衣服里面结满了金黑色的蘑菇时，他们又退了回去。

在这些过时（和未使用）的武器中，你发现了一袋小说。幻想题材，但主题都是太空旅行的可能性，以及现代人和外星人的接触。

original: Breach the fungus
translation: 打破真菌屏障

original: Shivering spasms of festering fungus separate the front of the train from the rest. The only way forward is through.
translation: 溃烂的真菌的痉挛着将列车其他部分与头部分开，继续前进的唯一方法是穿过菌丛。

original:
You organise your hardiest stokers into a rota, slowly but steadily widening the gap between the pallid walls of quivering fungal flesh. The smell is direful, as are the ominous bulges protruding from the mushroom bulk. 

Thanks to your capable direction, however, a wide path is cleared straight through the fungus, bisecting it like two lungs separated by the trachea. You pass through, unharmed.
translation:
你组织你手下最得力的炮手轮流开火，缓慢而稳步地扩大菌肉苍白菌壁之间的缝隙。气味令人作呕，蘑菇上不祥的凸起也同样令人不安。

尽管如此，在你的指挥下，一条宽阔的道路笔直地穿过真菌丛，如同气管分开两片肺叶。你毫发无损地走了过去。

original:
Sabres serve to hack away the plump, bulging intrusions. It peels away like flesh carved from a roasted pig. The smell is considerably worse, however. 

The work is slow going. These twitching sheathes of fungus are of enormous size and depth. An American stoker remembers the redwood trees of his youth. Eventually, enough of a path is cleared to allow you to progress. It's a tight squeeze between the walls of livid flesh, allowing you to see the bulges within up close. Bulges the same shape and size as you. 

And then you are through.
translation:
用军刀砍下那些肿胀隆起的入侵真菌，它像烤猪身上的肉一样片片剥落。然而，可以想见，气味相当糟糕。

工作进展缓慢。这些抽搐的真菌肉壁尺寸和深度都相当巨大，一个美国司炉回忆起了他年轻时见过的红木。终于，足以通行的道路被清理出来，使你能够继续前进。跻身色彩鲜艳的肉壁之间，你能够近距离地看到里面的隆起。隆起的形状和大小与你相同。

然后你到了另一头。

original: Explore the crew cabins
translation: 探索宿营舱

original: In locomotives as old as this, the crew were always assigned bunks near the engine room.
translation: 在像这样古老的机车中，列车员总是被分配到靠近锅炉室的铺位上。

original:
The sounds of the gramophone are louder here. Battered metal and tormented wood-panelling comprise the confines in which the crew dwelled. Chubby toadstools, round as pastries, dot the cramped bunkbeds. 

Mementos of home are scattered about the fruiting debris. Slim volumes of Arnold and Blake, vials of honey, and engravings of simple domestic scenes can be found under every bunk. You also uncover a little tally-chart on a folded up bit of paper. It seems the crew were organising a whip-round for their commander's retirement present. They'd settled on a plot of land on Port Prosper.
translation:
留声机的声音在这里更加响亮，残破的金属和木板组成了列车员们的生活空间。肥大的蘑菇像面团一样点缀在狭窄的双层床表面。

这堆残骸中散落着列车员们故乡的纪念品。每张床铺下都能找到阿诺德和布莱克的系列小说、小瓶蜂蜜和简单的家庭场景雕塑。你打开一张折叠的纸，发现是个统计表，看来他们正在为车长退休仪式组织一次抽奖活动。他们在兴荣港停靠。

original: Traverse the sporing carriage
translation: 穿过孢子遍布的车厢

original: Fruiting sacs send clouds of vitriolic orange into the air.  Passing through will be hazardous to the health. The engine room is just beyond.
translation: 孢囊向空气中喷出腐蚀性的橙色气体，走进去绝对有害健康。引擎室就在车厢后面。

original:
You go alone. Your crew disappear behind you, lost in a haze of orange and gold. Above, sacs of sporing fungus encrusted to the metalwork begin to erupt. Showers of spore and viscous liquids render the terrain still more hazardous. 

You feel a peculiar sensation; your hands tingle, as though wishing to reach out, to touch the fungus, as though for one more drink. You increase your speed.

At last, you leap over a final hissing sac of fungal eggs, and find yourself before the engine room door.
translation:
你独自深入。你的列车员在身后消失，融入一片橙金色的迷雾之中。上方，附着在金属上的孢子囊开始爆裂。孢子和粘稠液体如雨般落下，令地形更加险峻。

你泛起一种奇特的感觉。你的手在发抖，仿佛在渴望触摸真菌，就像渴望着再喝一杯酒。你加快了脚步。

最后，你跃过了最后一个嘶嘶作响的菌卵，发现自己站在引擎室门前。

original:
You go alone. Your crew disappear behind you, lost in a haze of orange and gold. Above, sacs of sporing fungus encrusted to the metalwork begin to erupt. Showers of spore and viscous liquids render the terrain still more hazardous. 

You feel a peculiar sensation; your hands tingle, as though wishing to reach out, to touch the fungus, as though for one more drink. You increase your speed. 

There is a cry behind you. You turn, to see one of your crew, a particularly distractible signaller, has entered the miasma after you. Her hands are in a mound of virulent gold fungus. Then, so is the rest of her. 

The scene is lost to another shower of spores. You press on, towards the engine room.
translation:
你独自深入。你的列车员在身后消失，融入一片橙金色的迷雾之中。上方，附着在金属上的孢子囊开始爆裂。孢子和粘稠液体如雨般落下，令地形更加险峻。

你泛起一种奇特的感觉。你的手在发抖，仿佛在渴望触摸真菌，就像渴望着再喝一杯酒。你加快了脚步。

身后响起尖叫。你转身，看到一名特别不专心的信号员也跟着你进入了瘴雾。她的双手陷进了剧毒的金色真菌中，很快全身也被吞没了。

最后，你跃过了最后一个嘶嘶作响的菌卵，发现自己站在引擎室门前。

original: Entrancing fungus
translation: 迷人的真菌

original:
You go alone. Your crew disappear behind you, lost in a haze of orange and gold. Above, sacs of sporing fungus encrusted to the metalwork begin to erupt. Showers of spore and viscous liquids render the terrain still more hazardous. 

You feel a peculiar sensation; your hands tingle, as though wishing to reach out, to touch the fungus, as though for one more drink. You increase your speed. 

There is a cry behind you. You turn, to see one of your crew, a particularly distractible signaller, has entered the miasma after you. Her hands hover over a mound of virulent gold fungus, as though transfixed.
translation:
你独自深入。你的列车员在身后消失，迷失在一片橙金色的朦胧之中。在上方，包覆在金属物件上的孢子菌囊开始喷射。孢子和粘稠液体喷洒而下，使地形更加危险。

你泛起一种奇特的感觉；你的手在发抖，仿佛在渴望触摸真菌，就像想再喝一杯。你加快脚步。

身后响起了尖叫声。你转身，看到一名特别不专心的信号员也跟着你进入了瘴雾。她用双手抚摸着剧毒的金色真菌，好像被迷住了。

original: Go back for her
translation: 回去找她

original: Perhaps there's time.
translation: 也许还有时间。

original:
You call out, risking spores entering your mouth, and begin to run. Your signaller flinches and draws back just as a fungus pops, emitting an iridescent cloud. 

You see, briefly, an image of an old marshy place, bedecked with sprawling fungus. A large tower of wobbling mushroom. A word enters your head. Mother. 

You come to with your signaller crouched over you. You send her back to safety. You're fine. You're fine. You press on.
translation:
你冒着孢子进入嘴里的危险喊了一声，然后开始奔跑。信号员收回了手，就在这时，一个菌囊爆炸了，释放出五彩缤纷的气体。

你短暂地看到了一个古老的沼泽地的图像，里面长满了蔓延的真菌。一座巨大的，摇摆不定的蘑菇塔。一个词进入你的脑海：母亲。

你醒来的时候，信号员正蹲在身边。你把她送回了安全地带。你没事。继续前进。

original: Leave her
translation: 让她自生自灭

original: She has disobeyed orders. If she endangers herself, that might be a lesson to your crew.
translation: 她违抗了命令。如果她陷入危险，也算给你的列车员好好上了一课。

original:
You push on. There is a brief scream behind you, and when you look back, she is gone. The golden fungus looks a little larger, and bulges unpleasantly. 

You run on, towards the engine room, before the cloud of spores can do any further damage to you.
translation:
你继续前进。身后传来一声短促的尖叫，当你回头时，她已经不见了。金色的真菌看起来更大了一些，并且令人不快地鼓胀起来。

在孢子云造成任何更多伤害之前，你继续向引擎室跑去。

original: Enter the Engine Room
translation: 进入引擎室

original: The thick steel door is scored with bulletholes, and is held in place by tendrils of ropy white fungus.
translation: 厚厚的钢门上遍布弹孔，被白色真菌的卷须固定在原地。

original:
As you approach, you notice the damage done to the walls, riddled with bullets. Old stains on the carpet. An attack was mounted on the engine room. 

You can hear music loud and clear from inside. An eery green light pours through the hinges, like floodwater. You push open the door.
translation:
走近大门时，你注意到墙上遍布弹孔。地毯上有着旧渍，引擎室遭遇了敌袭。

你可以听到门内传来响亮而清晰的乐声，阴森的绿光像洪水一样从门缝涌出。你推开了门。

original: The Remnant of Percy Blythe
translation: 珀西·布莱斯的遗物

original: [qvd:135754(Percy)]
translation: [qvd:135754(Percy)]

original: Investigate the engine room
translation: 调查引擎室

original: What happened here?
translation: 这里发生了什么？

original:
The corpses bear bullet wounds. They are unmarred by fungus, decaying in peace. Amongst the rank insignia, you spot a first officer, a chief engineer and a conductor. All died violent deaths. There are far too few to amount to the full crew.

The boiler – a battered, antiquated, wheezing contraption –  stands silent, and broken. Strips of iron hang in front of it, as though it had suffered an explosion. Inside, you find fungus amidst the ashes; clumps and clusters of tendrils that sprout from the charcoal. When burnt, the spores would have infected the whole engine.
translation:
尸体上有枪伤。它们未被真菌破坏，不受打扰地腐烂。在众多肩章中，你认出了一名大副、一名轮机长和一名粘土人列车主管，全都死于非命。数量远远低于列车员总数。

锅炉破旧不堪，型号过时，喘着粗气，一动不动，已经损坏了。锅炉前面悬挂着铁条，似乎曾经发生过爆炸。你在锅炉内部的灰烬中发现了真菌；木炭里冒出一丛丛、一簇簇的触须。如果被点燃，孢子会感染整架机车。

original: Examine the captain's corpse
translation: 检查车长的尸体

original: Here lies all that remains of Lt Commander Percy Blythe.
translation: 这里陈列着珀西·布莱斯上尉的全部遗物。

original:
The corpse of the finest officer of his generation hangs from the wall, suspended by loops of pale fronds. His skin is sallow, and strands of golden fungus crawl beneath it. His eyes open.

Percy Blythe looks down on you. Blue-fruiting mushrooms speckle his beard. Next to him, the gramophone crackles out dreary anthems of years past. His mouth opens too wide as he speaks; his jaw cracks.
translation:
他那一代最优秀的军官的尸体挂在墙上，被一圈圈苍白的叶子悬挂着。他的皮肤苍白，下面爬满了一缕缕金色的真菌。他的眼睛睁开了。

珀西·布莱斯俯视着你。蓝色的蘑菇在他的胡须上留下了斑点。在他旁边，留声机噼里啪啦地播放着过去几年的沉闷的颂歌。他说话的时候嘴巴张得太大了；他的下巴裂开了。

original: Listen to Lt Commander Percy Blythe
translation: 听珀西·布莱斯上尉说话

original: Somehow, he is alive.
translation: 不知何故，他还活着。

original:
He groans. His mouth opens impossibly wide, and a cloud of yellow spores emerge. "I am all that's left." An oily liquid begins to drip from his left eye. "I am a Child of the Grave-Garden." 

The voice alters, becoming more clipped, more static, like that of the voices on the gramophone. "I am Lt Commander Percy Blythe, captain of the Parzifal. My task was to explore the Wilderness, and return home with new discoveries." He groans, as though weeping. "I am all that remains. I want to go home."
translation:
他呻吟着。他的嘴巴张得大得不可思议，一团黄色的孢子冒了出来。“只剩下我了，” 一种油腻的液体开始从他的左眼滴落，“我是坟墓花园的孩子。”

声音变了，变得更加紧凑，有更多的杂音，就像留声机上的声音一样。“我是珀西·布莱斯上尉，帕西法尔号的车长。我的任务是探索荒野，并带着新的发现返回家园。”他呻吟着，仿佛在哭泣，“只剩下我了。我想回家。”

original: Ask him what happened here
translation: 询问他这里发生了什么

original: How did the Parzifal end up in this condition?
translation: 帕西法尔号怎么会落到这种地步？

original:
"We met the Children on Hybras. We sought to know each other. Wanted to go to the wood. Wanted to see what was kept from us." Percy is drooling as he speaks.

The gramophone clicks, as yet another patriotic dirge begins to play. Percy Blythe struggles in his bonds, pulling himself up to stand a little straighter. "We made contact on Hybras. The fungus was so bright, so beautiful." 

His eyes shine gold. "I brought it aboard, God forgive me. I wanted the crew to see. To know." 

Oil leaks from those hollow eyes. "I'm sorry. I'm so sorry. Some came willing. Others refused to join us. We had to—" He breaks off into silence, staring away into the middle distance.
translation:
“我们遇到了海波拉的孩子们。我们试图了解对方。想去森林里看看。想看看有什么东西被瞒着我们。 ”珀西一边说着，一边流着口水。

留声机咔咔作响，又一首爱国的悲歌开始播放。珀西·布莱斯在束缚中挣扎着，把自己拉起来，站得更直一些。“我们在海波拉建立了联系。真菌是如此明亮，如此美丽。”

他的眼中金光闪烁。“我把它带上了车，上帝原谅我。我想让列车员们去看，去了解它们。”

珀西凹陷的双眼中漏出了油。“我很抱歉。我真的很抱歉。有些人愿意来。其他人拒绝加入我们。我们不得不……”他陷入了沉默，凝视着远方。

original: What happened to him?
translation: 他身上发生了什么？

original: How can he be alive?
translation: 他怎么可能还活着？

original: Self-pity
translation: 自怨自艾

original: Percy Blythe launches into a long, meandering, slurred story of children and gardens, of a cruel king who needed but did not love his subjects, despite their love for him, of knowledge denied and growth checked. Of tyranny and freedom, of grief and betrayal and longing. The music bursts into sudden life. Percy jerks, and fixes you with an infected eye. "I was stupid. I thought we would be welcome here. And we were, we were welcomed. We were loved. The Children, the Verdance, they wanted us." He begins to sob. It is a sad, squelching sound.
translation: 珀西·布莱斯讲述了一个冗长的、曲折的、含糊不清的故事，讲述了孩子和花园，讲述了一个残暴的国王，残暴的国王需要却并不爱他的臣民，尽管他们爱他，知识被拒绝和成长受阻的故事。 音乐突然生动起来。珀西猛地一颤，用被真菌感染的眼睛盯着你。“我太傻了。我以为我们会受到欢迎的。而且我们确实是，我们受到了欢迎。我们被爱着。孩子们，绿意，他们是想要我们的。”他开始抽泣，发出一种悲伤而沉闷的声音。

original: Console him
translation: 安慰他

original: Something of the man remains.
translation: 这个男人身上还保留了一些东西。

original: You approach gingerly, fishing for a handkerchief in your pocket. Reaching up, you begin to dab at the oily tears that scour the Lt. Commander's face. Beneath the grime, you can see Percy's flesh is remarkably well preserved, save for the vibrant tendrils of golden fungus running beneath the skin. "Thank you," he whispers.
translation: 你小心翼翼地走近他，从口袋里摸出一块手帕。你伸出手，擦拭上尉脸上的油性泪痕。在污垢之下，你可以看到珀西的肉体保存得异常完好，除了在皮下涌动的金色真菌和触须。“谢谢你，”他轻声说。

original: Keep your distance
translation: 保持距离

original: You're not going near his noxious secretions.
translation: 你不打算靠近他的有毒分泌物。

original: The oily burbling goes on for some time. The Lt. Commander becomes rapidly incoherent. Sometimes he weeps for 'Mother', other times for London. He believes himself disgraced twice-over. Eventually, the embarrassing affair comes to a stop, as Percy Blythe is left blowing clouds of spores from his mouth, his eyes vacant.
translation: 油腻的咕哝声持续了一段时间。上尉迅速变得语无伦次。有时他为“母亲”哭泣，有时为伦敦。他觉得自己已经两次颜面尽失了。这尴尬的场景终于到头了，珀西-布莱斯从口中喷出孢子云，眼神空洞。

original: What does he want now?
translation: 他现在想要什么？

original: Can he even go home?
translation: 他还能回家吗？

original:
Lt Commander Percy Blythe lets out a low moan, and slumps forward. The chains of fungus adjust to accommodate this despair. 

"Home." He slurs, like a drunk man demanding another drink. "On Hybras. Mother spored us there. She set out her children across the stars to learn. The Traitor's Wood. We were forbidden from entering there, but now its king is dead. But this craft failed before we could arrive..." 

The body jerks, as though shocked. Percy's face rises to face you. "London," he rasps. "London."
translation:
珀西·布莱斯上尉发出低低的呻吟，然后向前倒下。他身上真菌锁链迅速调整了重心。

“我的家，”他含糊地说，就像一个醉汉要求再来一杯，“在海波拉。母亲在那里孕育了我们。她让她的孩子们穿越星辰去学习。叛徒之林。我们被禁止进入那里，但现在它的国王已经死了。但是这艘机车在我们到达之前就失败了……”

他的抽搐了一下，仿佛受到了电击。珀西的脸转向你。“伦敦，”他嘶哑地说。“伦敦。”

original: Decide his fate
translation: 决定他的命运

original:
This cannot continue.
[This will bring the story of the Parzifal to a conclusion.]
translation:
不能再这么继续下去了。
[这将为帕西法尔号的故事画上句号。]

original:
Lt Commander Percy Blythe, decorated hero of London's forces, first captain through the Avid Horizon, gazes at you, slack-jawed and unseeing. 

"Please," he rasps. "Take me home. Or finish this." He twitches, "We just wanted to know what was kept from us in Traitor's Wood. Why did our king not love his children?"
translation:
珀西·布莱斯上尉，伦敦部队的功勋英雄，通过渴求之地平线的第一任车长，凝视着你，下巴松弛，眼神空洞。

“求你了，”他咆哮着说，“带我回家。或者结束这一切。”他抽搐了一下，“我们只是想知道在叛徒森林在瞒着的是什么东西。为什么我们的国王不爱他的孩子？”

original: Burn it all down
translation: 烧尽一切

original: No one need ever know what happened here. It might be mercy.
translation: 没有人需要知道这里发生过什么。这可能是种仁慈。

original:
The remnant of Percy Blythe does not appear to register your response. His head bobs with the tilting of the engine. You back away from the door, and quickly away through the rotting carriages of the Parzifal.

Your crew do not need telling twice. With torches and pistols, you roam the fruiting carriages, igniting plump walls of fungus wherever you find them. You work from back to front, until the locomotive blazes like fireworks at the Proms. Soon, the engine will be little more than a smouldering husk. And somewhere in the conflagration burns Percy Blythe, but not for long. 

You flee the smoking wreck of the Parzifal, having purged it of its infection.
translation:
珀西·布莱斯的残体似乎并没有察觉到你的回应。他的头随着机车的倾斜而晃动。你从门前退开，迅速穿过帕西法尔号腐烂的车厢。

你的列车员不需要三申五令。带着火把和手枪，你们在结满孢子的车厢里穿行，点燃无论在哪里发现的鼓胀的真菌墙。你们从车后来到车前，直到火车像舞会上的焰火一样燃烧起来。很快，机车就会变成一具冒烟的躯壳。珀西·布莱斯就在这场大火中的哪个地方燃烧着，但他不会燃烧太久。

你逃离了冒烟的帕西法尔号的残骸，清除了它的感染。

original: Can the Parzifal still fly?
translation: 帕西法尔号还能飞行吗？

original: The answer is almost certainly no, but there's no harm in asking.
translation: 答案几乎肯定是否定的，但问一下也无妨。

original: "No," the Lt Commander hisses, his eyes rolling in his head. "Sabotage. Mutiny. Ignorance. No fuel. The Children too greedy, spread too fast. Like fire. The engine is broken. The crew all gone. I am alone." His head lolls as though his neck were broken.
translation: “不行，”上尉嘶吼道，眼睛在眼眶里滚动。“破坏。叛变。无知。没有燃料。孩子们太贪婪了，扩张得太快了。像火一样。机车坏了。列车员都走了。只剩我一个。”他的头耷拉着，仿佛脖子被折断了。

original: Take Percy Blythe to Hybras
translation: 带珀西·布莱斯去海波拉

original: Return him to 'Mother'.
translation: 把他还给“母亲”。

original:
The remnant of Percy Blythe does not appear to register your response. His head bobs with the tilting of the locomotive. You begin cutting the body down. It is a task only made more difficult by the discovery that most of the far wall is, in fact, a rubbery sort of mushroom, whose weak yellow flesh is entirely embedded in Blythe's back. 

You are forced to cut down a whole section of the wall, exposing the metal shell of the Parzifal, and carry Blythe out upon it. On board your engine, he mutters and twitches, as though diminished by the separation. You leave the Parzifal drifting alone in the sky.
translation:
珀西·布莱斯的残体似乎并没有察觉到你的回应。他的头随着机车的倾斜而晃动。你开始把他的身体从车中切下。在你发现大部分远处的墙壁其实是一种橡胶状的蘑菇后，这任务变得更加困难，脆弱的黄色血肉完全嵌进了布莱斯的背部。

你不得不砍下一整段墙，露出帕西法尔号的金属外壳，然后连着它与布莱斯一起送出来。在你的机车上，他喃喃自语，抽搐着，仿佛因为分离而变得渺小。你放任帕西法尔号在天空中独自飘荡。

original: Return Percy Blythe to London
translation: 带珀西-布莱斯去伦敦

original: Bring him home.
translation: 把他带回家。

original: Mercy?
translation: 仁慈？

original:
The remnant of Percy Blythe does not appear to register your response. His head bobs with the tilting of the engine. You cup his head gently, to avoid plunging your hand through the soft, rotten flesh of his neck. The chains of fungus quiver as you set to freeing him.

His hand reaches for yours, and his gold-flecked eyes meet yours. "An end. Please," he rasps. "London... I want... remember as I was."
translation:
珀西·布莱斯的残体似乎并没有察觉到你的回应。他的头随着机车的倾斜而晃动。你轻轻地抱住他的头，以免双手穿过他脖子上柔软的烂肉。当你准备释放他时，真菌的锁链开始发抖。

他的手伸向你的手，他那双泛着金光的眼睛与你的目光相遇。“结束。求你了，”他喘着粗气说，“伦敦……我想……记住我以前的样子。”

original: Grant him an end
translation: 为其了断

original: Bring home his corpse
translation: 把他的尸体带回家

original:
A small spatter of red and a longer drip of black follows. The corpse sinks to the floor, as though abandoned by the fungus. His body has left a deep impression in the yellow mushroom that covers the wall. 

You bear the fallen captain of the Parzifal back to your engine, where his corpse is covered with an old flag. His last voyage is almost at an end.
translation:
一小片红色的喷溅和更长的黑色滴落随之而来。尸体沉到了地上，仿佛被真菌抛弃了。他的身体已在覆盖墙壁的黄色蘑菇上留下了深深的印痕。

你带着倒下的帕西法尔号车长回到你的机车，他的尸体上盖着一面旧旗。他的最后一次航行几乎已经结束了。

original: Spare him
translation: 从真菌中释放他

original: Bring him home alive. Perhaps he might yet be saved.
translation: 把他活着带回家。也许他还有救。

original:
The light leaves his eyes, and his head lolls back. He speaks not another word to you, as you untangle him from the frondulent chains that bind him. 

Eventually, and after some deft work with a hacksaw to free him from the spongy flesh at his back, Lt. Commander Percy Blythe is free. You guide him, clinging and ruined, through the sporing carriages and to the safety of your engine.
translation:
光线离开他的眼睛，他的头向后仰去。当你把他从捆绑他的蓬松锁链上解开时，他没有再对你说一句话。

最终，在用钢锯巧妙地将他从背部的海绵状血肉中解放出来后，珀西·布莱斯上尉获得了自由。你引导着执着而破败的他，穿过孢子弥漫的车厢，来到你机车中的安全地带。

original: Take Percy Blythe to Traitor's Wood
translation: 把珀西·布莱斯带到叛徒之林。

original: Let him complete his last mission.
translation: 让他完成最后的任务。

original:
The remnant of Percy Blythe does not appear to register your response. His head bobs with the tilting of the locomotive. You begin cutting the body down. It is a task only made more difficult by the discovery that most of the far wall is, in fact, a rubbery sort of mushroom, whose weak yellow flesh is entirely embedded in Blythe's back. 

You are forced to cut down a whole section of the wall, exposing the metal shell of the Parzifal, and carry Blythe out upon it. On board your engine, he mutters and twitches, as though diminished by the separation. You leave the Parzifal drifting alone in the sky.
translation:
珀西·布莱斯的残体似乎并没有察觉到你的回应。他的头随着机车的倾斜而晃动。你开始把他的身体从车中切下。在你发现大部分远处的墙壁其实是一种橡胶状的蘑菇后，这任务变得更加困难，脆弱的黄色血肉完全嵌进了布莱斯的背部。

你不得不砍下一整段墙，露出帕西法尔号的金属外壳，然后连着它与布莱斯一起送出来。在你的机车上，他喃喃自语，抽搐着，仿佛因为分离而变得渺小。你放任帕西法尔号在天空中独自飘荡。

original: The Vigilant Nightingale
translation: 机警的夜莺

original: This broken down engine has been comprehensively gutted to serve as the Ringbreakers' home and base. Filthy hammocks stretch between metal bars, most full of snoring urchins. Others sit around decorating tea-tray armour with bright paints, or sparring playfully with wooden sticks.
translation: 这台破旧机车的内部已被彻底改造，现作为破戒者们的避风港和大本营。脏兮兮的吊床挂在金属栏杆之间，大多躺着呼呼大睡的顽童。几个没睡的则围坐在一起，要么拿着颜料给茶盘拼成的盔甲上色，要么举着木棍打打闹闹。

original: Visit the Captain's cabin
translation: 前往指挥室

original: The door leads to one of the few rooms that hasn't been gutted. A series of names have been scratched into it and then scratched out. The only one still readable says SIGRID.
translation: 少数几间舱室仍保持原貌，这扇门便通向其中一间。门上刻有一连串名字，后来又被划掉。其中，只有“西格丽德”仍可辨认。

original: Knock Knock
translation: 叩叩叩

original: "Enter!" barks a high-pitched voice – Sigrid Spitesdottir, Valkyrie of the Ringbreakers and the closest thing this port has to law.
translation: “进来！”里面传来尖锐的嗓音。那是西格丽德·斯派茨多蒂尔，破戒者的女武神，也是此地秩序的维护者。

original: Knock Knock
translation: 叩叩叩

original: "Just a sec!" A good thirty seconds pass. "Who's there?"
translation: “稍等！”半分钟后，话音又响起，“是谁？”

original: Announce yourself by name
translation: 自报家门

original: The dignity of the Captain's cabin must be maintained.
translation: 要进入指挥室，必须遵循礼仪。

original: A pause. "Come in then."
translation: 她顿了一下，说：“那进来吧。”

original: "Isadore"
translation: "我是伊萨多尔"

original: A most fiendish ruse!
translation: 这诡计太狡猾了！

original:
A pause. "Isadore who?"

Sigrid's silence as you add "Isadore open or not?" is strong enough to peel the skin from your bones.
translation:
她顿了一下，问：“哪个伊萨多尔？”

你接着说：“我是伊萨多尔，你开不开门？”西格丽德心中默忖。这沉默压得你透不过气，像是要活生生把你剥了皮。

original: "Viola"
translation: “我是薇奥拉”

original: A classic pretence for the ages...
translation: 一个经久不衰的经典谎言……

original:
"What? Viola who?"

Sigrid's expression as you enter with a satisfied "Viola sudden don't you know who I am?" suggests that you are at most one poorly chosen sentence away from being hurled into the marsh.
translation:
“啥？哪个薇奥拉？”

你一边得意洋洋地进门，一边甩出一句：“薇奥拉登场，你居然不认得我了？”而西格丽德满脸狐疑，显然，再说错一个字，你就得被扔进沼泽里了。

original: Train with the Urchins
translation: 和顽童们一起训练

original: Their equipment may smack of the schoolyard, but they take their fighting seriously.
translation: 纵使手里的家伙相当简陋，他们动起手来可不马虎。

original: A triumphant victory
translation: 大胜

original: You wield your broom proudly, fending off attacks with ease and returning them as stern but educational bops to the Ringbreakers' heads. By the end, they reluctantly agree that for a grown-up, you're not entirely rubbish. (Maybe a bit lucky.) A certain silence falls. They seem to be expecting something...
translation: 你自信满满地挥舞着扫把，轻松挡下一次又一次的攻击，又还了手，不轻不重地敲了几下他们的小脑瓜，算是寓教于打。战斗结束后，他们虽然面带不甘，但还是承认：你这臭大人，倒也不完全是个草包。（也可能只是你这次运气好。） 随后，沉默悄然降临。破戒者们一齐望向你，似乎在等你做些什么……

original: Bellow "HOJOHOTO!"
translation: 大喊“嘿吼嘿哈！”

original: A stirring battle-cry.
translation: 战吼过后，人群骚动。

original: The urchins snigger to themselves. That probably wasn't what they had in mind.
translation: 顽童们暗自窃笑，你的吼法和他们料想的不一样。

original: Bellow "HOJOTOHO!"
translation: 大喊“嘿吼哈嘿！”

original: A triumphant battle-cry.
translation: 战吼传来，人心振奋。

original: "HOJOTOHO!" they chorus in response. You sense you have earned no small amount of respect here.
translation: 他们齐声回应：“嘿吼哈嘿！”。你感到自己备受尊重。

original: Bellow "HOTOHOJO!"
translation: 大喊“嘿哈嘿吼！”

original: A deafening battle-cry.
translation: 战吼出口，震耳欲聋。

original: The urchins snigger to themselves. That probably wasn't what they had in mind.
translation: 顽童们暗自窃笑，你的吼法和他们料想的不一样。

original: A sweeping defeat
translation: 大败

original: The Ringbreakers come at you with much speed and little mercy. Though they only wield regular broomsticks – no sharp objects on these ones, for training purposes – they still hurt. Several minutes of being smacked around the legs later, you are forced to yield.
translation: 破戒者们一拥而上，来势汹汹，毫不手软。他们手中手里挥舞的，不过是些普普通通的扫把（用于训练的扫把没有加装锐器），可抽在腿上，照样疼得钻心。你就这样被他们围攻，几分钟后，只得败下阵来。

original: Return to the Market
translation: 返回市场

original: The Ringbreaker guards half-heartedly salute as you depart.
translation: 离开时，破戒者守卫向你敬礼，但相当敷衍。

original: Visit the 'brig'
translation: 前往“禁闭室”

original: A series of iron bars have been welded into the stern, ready to hold anyone who might do the port harm.
translation: 车尾焊了一排铁栏杆作为牢房，随时关押会危害本地安全的人。

original: Prisoners of Sigrid
translation: 西格丽德的阶下囚

original: A mix of angry, doleful and drunk eyes stare back at you from the darkness. All the prisoners have been stripped to their underthings. The Ringbreakers do their best to keep them happy by regularly throwing them boiled sweets. It doesn't appear to be working.
translation: 黑暗中，一双双眼睛盯着你，有的怨恨，有的伤感，有的则醉意朦胧。所有囚犯都被扒光衣服，只剩下内衣。破戒者们每过一段时间就扔去些硬糖，想让囚犯们心情好点，但似乎于事无补。

original: Sigrid Spitesdottir
translation: 西格丽德·斯派茨多蒂尔

original: Despite being the youngest Ringbreaker to be declared Valkyrie, Sigrid has the glare of a seasoned general and the scars to back it up. She sits sternly behind a mahogany desk almost as tall as she is, carefully engrossed in a copy of Sun Tzu's The Art Of War. It is a show of military diligence only slightly undercut by it being upside down.
translation: 在所有被封为女武神的破戒者中，西格丽德年纪最轻，但其眼神却有如久经沙场的老将，身上的几道伤疤也足以为她背书。她危坐在和她一般高的桃花心木书桌后，全神贯注地阅读着《孙子兵法》，似在领悟用兵之道。只不过，她把书拿反了，略显滑稽。

original: Ask about the Ringbreakers
translation: 询问什么是破戒者

original: Why are Urchins acting like the constabulary in this port?
translation: 为什么这里的顽童像本地的警察一般？

original: "Someone's gotta, right?"
translation: "总得有人维持秩序吧，对不？"

original:
Sigrid's face is a mixture of pride in her job and irritation at being questioned. "Don't just be thinkin' we're a bunch of kids. You hear of the Valkyrie? Greatest warrior in Old London she was. Yeah, well, in her name we kicked out the old bugger what brought us to the Wilderness to clean out his chimneys or whatever, an' now we've a home. Can't blame us for wantin' to protect it, right? Even if it is a bit damp in bits."

"Course," she adds, "Can't stay here forever. Rule One of the Ringbreakers. When you're old enough, that's when it's time to go out and find fortune out there, and find others to fill their places. All welcome. Just got to swear by our code and they're welcome to grab a hammock. Least, long as they don't fart too much in their sleep."
translation:
遭你质疑，西格丽德既有点骄傲，又有点烦躁：“可别把我们当小孩看。你听说过女武神吧？旧伦敦最顶尖的女战士。我们就是打着她的名号，把那个把我们骗到天野来清烟囱的老混蛋赶了出去，现在这里就是我们的地盘。就算地方有点潮，我们也想护住这地。”

她又补了几句：“当然啦，也不能一辈子窝在这儿。破戒者的第一条规矩——年纪够了，就得出门闯一闯，闯出前程，也给新来的腾地方。来者不拒，只要肯发誓守咱们的规矩，就能来放个吊床住下。只要他们睡着别放太臭的屁就行。”

original: Ask about the Monastery
translation: 问及修道院

original: It dominates the port, but stands apart from it.
translation: 修道院主宰着这里，但又与之独立。

original: Midnight
translation: 午夜所在

original: "Never been in meself," Sigrid admits. "Them Bohemian types in town are said to know a way, but it 'aint through the front door. Anyway. Without the tea from the place, we'd not have much of a home. Reckon we'll keep defending it. A Valkyrie don't need thanking."
translation: 西格丽德承认道：“我自己从没进去过，据说镇上的那帮波西米亚派艺术家知道该怎么进去，反正不是走前门。不管怎么说，要是没有那里的茶，我们也不会有这么个家。估摸着我们会继续守护‘午夜茶’，这是女武神该做的。”

original: Leave Sigrid to her business
translation: 不再打扰西格丽德

original: She has plenty to be getting on with.
translation: 她还有很多事情要忙。

original: Ask about the War of Midnight
translation: 询问什么是午夜之战

original: What's going on between her crew and the attackers?
translation: 她的手下和来袭者之间有什么纠葛？

original: No time for tea
translation: 长话短说

original: Sigrid's face darkens. "Shouldn't have let that Amblerley Murgatroyd get her boots dry after striding into port. We know it's her trying to destroy the Midnight Tea so everyone'll buy daddy's old scrapings instead, but she's tricksy. And with them Clay Men of hers always around, we can't go 'accidentally' pushing her off into the marsh. But we'll get her. Oh yeah."
translation: 西格丽德脸色一沉：“早知道就不该让安布利·穆加托德在这立足。我们都清楚，是她在暗地里搞鬼，想让‘午夜茶’彻底垮掉，好让大家去买她爹的那些陈年烂茶，但这女人狡猾得很。再加上她那几个粘土人随时跟着，我们也不好‘不小心’把她推到沼泽里。不过她别得意太早，我们迟早收拾她，哼。”

original: Ask about Midnight's Favour
translation: 询问什么是午夜甄选

original: She must know about the brew that made this port's name.
translation: 这个地方因此闻名，她肯定知道这种茶饮。

original: A shrug
translation: 她耸了耸肩

original: "Yeah, like them snooty Bohemian types'd let us try the stuff." Sigrid shrugs. "No big problem. Nothing wrong with juice, not 'less you drink it after brushing your teeth. Just don't brush 'em, that's what I say. Prob'ly bad for 'em anyway, working 'em over like that."
translation: “哼，说的好像那帮高高在上的艺术家会让我们试他们那茶一样。”西格丽德耸耸肩。“不过也无所谓啦，喝果汁也没啥不好，只要你不是刷完牙再喝就行。要我说，干脆别刷，老这么刷牙，八成也对牙不好。”

original: Ask about the state of the port
translation: 问及港口的状况

original: What will happen now that the monastery is no more?
translation: 修道院现已不复存在，接下来会怎么样？

original: Defeated
translation: 无精打采

original: "Like I knows," mutters Sigrid. "Some bloody Valkyrie I was. Reckon most of these folks'll move over to Pan or somewhere. Maybe we'll join 'em. Maybe we'll stick around. Make something of the place still. May not be my problem once the gang gets voting."
translation: 西格丽德嘟囔着，“你问我我问谁去，我他妈一直是个女武神。估摸着这儿的人大多都会搬去潘城那边或者别的地儿。可能我们也会跟着去，或许干脆留下来，把这地方整出点名堂来。反正等帮派选完头儿，大概也轮不到我来操心了。”

original: Ask about the War of Midnight
translation: 询问什么是午夜之战

original: Sigrid and her Ringbreakers don't seem to be basking in their victory.
translation: 西格丽德和手下的破戒者似乎没有沉浸在胜利的喜悦中。

original: An endless struggle
translation: 斗争不止

original: "Eternal vigilance, innit?" Sigrid sits back in her chair, fingers steepled. For just a moment though, her face breaks into a childish giggle. "But did you see old Murgy's face when she fell in the mud? Classic."
translation: “得一直警觉着，懂不？”西格莉德往椅背一靠，十指相抵，装出副大人模样。但转瞬，她就忍不住笑出声，像个真正的孩子似的咯咯直乐：“你看到老穆吉掉进泥里的那张脸没？笑死我了！”

original: Steal Sigrid's chocolate supply
translation: 偷走西格丽德的巧克力

original: She must keep it in her desk drawer. This should be easy.
translation: 她肯定把巧克力放在抽屉里了，不难偷走。

original: The chocolate heist
translation: “巧克力大劫案”

original: You distract Sigrid and slip a hand into her desk drawer. As promised, there are several half-melted bars of chocolate. She won't notice one of them going missing. The hungry Urchin from the market is suitably grateful, digging up some supplies.
translation: 你分散了西格莉德的注意力，悄悄把手伸进她的抽屉。正如顽童所讲，抽屉里果然藏着几块半融的巧克力。少一块，她也不会察觉。市场上那个挨饿的顽童满怀感激，翻出些补给送给你。

original: Sticky fingers
translation: 手脚不干净

original: You distract Sigrid, or so it seems. As your fingers slip into her drawer, however, she turns and slams it shut on your knuckles. "Thieves get bleeds," she snaps. "Leave it alone."
translation: 你以为自己成功分散了西格丽德的注意力。指尖刚碰到抽屉里的巧克力，她却猛地一转身，“啪”地一下合上抽屉，夹住你的半只手。她冷冷地说：“想偷窃，就流血，别打我糖的主意。”

original: Murgatroyd's Taste of Albion
translation: 穆氏阿尔比恩风味茶摊

original: Although one of the more professional looking barrows in the market, the Murgatroyd family's special tea blends have gained little traction. Proprietress Amberley Murgatroyd glares at you from behind a slender cigarette holder, twitching at the inconvenience of your presence.
translation: 尽管看起来是市场上的靠谱摊位，所售的穆氏特制拼配茶却不受欢迎。店主安布利·穆加托德咬着纤细的烟嘴，冲你冷眼一瞥：你的光临令她不胜其烦。

original: Purchase a caddy of tea
translation: 购买一罐茶叶

original: At these prices, it is no wonder the stall is so quiet.
translation: 价格这么高，怪不得没人光顾。

original: A poor deal is struck
translation: 一笔不划算的交易

original: Amberley takes the money and calls for one of her Clay Men. He scoops out the tea into its caddy using his bare hands, and seals it tight with a blob of wax.
translation: 安布利接了钱，叫来个粘土人手下帮忙。粘土人徒手将茶叶装进罐里，又用蜡封好口。

original: Enquire about the 'family business'
translation: 询问其“家族产业”的情况

original: The Murgatroyd company is known for more than tea and crackers. There is little you cannot learn at their salons, for the right price.
translation: 穆加托德公司的特产可不止茶和饼干。只要价格合适，在他们的沙龙里几乎没有打听不到的事。

original: A more specialised branch of the family tree
translation: 家族中的专业茶贩

original:
Amberley looks at you with disdain. "Oh, please. Even if I had time for Father's spymaster games, exactly how much do you think one overhears on the edge of nowhere?" 

She takes a long, pointed drag from her cigarette. "Honestly, if you must waste someone's time with such nonsense, go annoy my sister Melusine. I think we stashed her somewhere in the Reach. Her and her ridiculous inventions. Yes. I'm sure she's nothing better to do than listen to you."
translation:
安布利满脸不屑地看着你：“得了吧。就算我有空替父亲玩那些间谍把戏，经营情报生意，你觉得我在这穷乡僻壤边上，能偷听到什么天大的秘密？”

她深吸一口烟，平复心情，继续讲道：“说实话，要是你非要烦谁，不如去烦我妹妹梅露齐娜。我记得我们把她，跟她那堆稀奇古怪的发明一起扔在了外野的某个地方。对，她应该挺闲的，有的是时间听你胡扯。”

original: Speak with Amberley Murgatroyd
translation: 与安布利·穆加托德交谈

original: There aren't many fellow Albioners this far into Eleutheria.
translation: 这里是厄琉忒里亚的腹地，阿尔比恩的老乡可不多见。

original: A short chat
translation: 随便聊两句

original: "Are you here to buy?" Amberley glances around, looking for a distraction. "If you're not here to buy, I don't know why you're here. Unless..." She sizes you up. "Perhaps..."
translation: “你是来买茶的吗？”安布利四下里看看，心不在焉地说：“要是不买茶，我真不知道你为什么来这。除非……”她仔细打量着你，继续说着，“或许……”

original: Perhaps?
translation: 或许什么？

original: That sounds like an opportunity in the offing.
translation: 听起来似乎有机可乘。

original: Amberley lights a fresh cigarette. "I'm sure you've heard of Midnight's Favour. It's all anyone wants around here. Well, I have plans to deal with that. Were you to assist me when the moment presents itself, well, I would be most grateful. In a most profitable way for us both."
translation: 安布利又点了根烟，说道：“你应该听说过午夜甄选吧，这里人人都想要这东西。嗯，我这边有点安排，如果你在时机成熟时能帮我一把，那我感激不尽，当然，咱俩都会有利可图。”

original: Not interested
translation: 不感兴趣

original: This doesn't sound like your kind of business.
translation: 这听起来不像是你会参与的事情。

original: Amberley shrugs and returns to her cigarette. "Be that way, then. Either buy some tea or leave me alone."
translation: 安布利耸了耸肩，又抽起烟来，她说道：“既然如此，你要么买点茶，要么别烦我。”

original: Return to the market
translation: 返回市场

original: There are many more stalls to visit.
translation: 还有很多摊位可以逛。

original: Speak with Amberley Murgatroyd
translation: 与安布利·穆加托德交谈

original: Her business has picked up considerably of late.
translation: 她的生意最近明显好转了。

original: Past Midnight
translation: 午夜过后

original: "Yes, yes, a definite improvement." Amberley lights a cigarette. "I should be away from here in no time, just as soon as Father finds out. Any day now, I'm sure." She blows a long stream of smoke into the air. "I cannot wait to see my little sister's face when I finally take the company's reins, and run it properly."
translation: “是的，没错，最近生意的确好了不少。”安布利点燃了根烟。“我相信用不了不久，只要父亲注意到这边的起色，我应该就能离开这里。说不定就是哪一天。”她吐出一长缕烟雾，继续说道：“当我最终接手公司并经营得井井有条时，妹妹会有什么表情，我都等不及想看了。”

original: Purchase a caddy of tea
translation: 购买一罐茶叶

original: The price seems to have gone up recently. The ink on the sign is still wet.
translation: 售价似乎刚刚才改高，标签上的墨水都还没干。

original: Supply and demand
translation: 有求必有应

original: Amberley takes the money and calls for one of her Clay Men. He scoops out the tea into its caddy using his bare hands, and seals it tight with a blob of wax.
translation: 安布利接了钱，叫来个粘土人手下帮忙。粘土人徒手将茶叶装进罐里，又用蜡封好口。

original: Ask about Sigrid and the Urchins
translation: 问及西格丽德和顽童们

original: The Urchins seem young to be in a position of authority.
translation: 顽童们还太小了，没什么地位。

original: Fingers squeezed white around a cigarette holder
translation: 紧握烟嘴，手指发白

original: "That little scrot and her infernal playmates." Amberley shakes her head. "I'd blame the parents if she'd had any. No discipline. A few damn good spankings never did me any harm. Today's youth could do with getting to know the back end of a slipper. Just look at my sister Melusine."
translation: “那个小混蛋和她那些讨厌的小跟班们啊，”安布利摇摇头，继续抱怨：“要是她真有父有母，我倒是能有人可怪。这小孩缺乏管教，肆无忌惮。我小时候挨了几顿好打，现在不也没事儿。如今的小青年啊，个个该好好见识见识拖鞋底儿。我妹妹梅露齐娜就是个欠管教的主儿。”

original: Ask about Midnight's Favour
translation: 询问什么是午夜甄选

original: Even if it is the competition, she must know about it.
translation: 虽然是竞品，她应该也有所了解。

original: A sore spot
translation: 哪壶不开提哪壶

original: "Oh, we are not worthy of Midnight's Favour," Amberley snaps, her tone suggesting that she's parroting someone else. "Haven't touched the stuff. Can't wait to get back to Albion and never hear about it again. When I'm running the business—" She catches herself. "Well. I'll have my sights set rather higher than beverages."
translation: “哎呀，小店哪配得上午夜甄选这种好货。”安布利冷笑一声，听起来像是鹦鹉学舌。“从来没碰过那玩意儿。我恨不得马上回到阿尔比恩，再也不想听别人提起午夜甄选。等我接手公司——”她尴尬地戛然而止，一转话锋，“唔，我的眼界可不会局限在区区饮品上。”

original: Pay to let the Clay Conductor spend time with Amberley's assistants
translation: 付钱让粘土人列车主管与安布利的粘土人手下们待一会

original: He is eager to speak to the Clay Men in her employ.
translation: 他急切地想与安布利的粘土人手下交谈。

original: Echoing across the marsh
translation: 回荡在沼泽之上

original:
"Just don't let him give them any ideas," Amberley tells you. The Clay Conductor requests that they sing for him.The other Clay Men look reluctant, embarrassed even, but one with shale skin steps forward. "It has been too long. But we should still sing." 

Following his lead, the Clay Men launch into a mournful, hollow aria that resonates within your rib cage. Even Amberley Murgatroyd shivers as the last notes die away. 

The Clay Conductor is quiet for a long minute. At last, he gives his verdict. "No." He stomps away, back towards your engine.
translation:
“千万别让他说什么坏点子。”安布利对你说。粘土人列车主管请求他们为他唱歌。其他粘土人看起来很不情愿，甚至有些尴尬，但其中一个有着页岩皮肤的粘土人走上前。“已经太久了。但我们应该还能唱。”

在它的带领下，粘土人开始了一段哀伤而空灵的咏叹调，那声音在你的胸腔内回响。即使是安布利·穆加托德，在最后一个音符消逝时也不禁打了个寒战。

粘土人列车主管沉默了许久。终于，他给出了评价：“不。”然后他走开了，回到你们的机车那边，脚步沉重。

original: Echoing across the marsh
translation: 回荡在沼泽之上

original: The Midnight Garden
translation: 午夜花园

original: The noise of the market slowly fades as you follow the rickety wooden steps down to the marsh. Bohemians calling themselves Midnight Connoisseurs have built a wooden pagoda overlooking the monastery to savour the taste of the leaves that grow within.
translation: 随着你沿着摇摇欲坠的木梯走下沼泽地，市场的喧嚣声逐渐淡去。一群自称为“午夜鉴赏家”的波西米亚派艺术家在这里建了一座俯瞰修道院的木质楼阁，以便品味那些在修道院内生长的茶叶。

original: Attend a tea ceremony
translation: 参加茶道仪式

original: Midnight Connoisseurs are extremely choosy about who gets to savour the tea here.
translation: “午夜鉴赏家”对在此品茶的人选极为挑剔。

original: An honoured guest
translation: 贵客驾到

original: The ritual comes easily to you. It begins with a cup of mere hot water, sipped to clear the taste-buds. Midnight Connoisseurs bring forth a bowl of embers on which to heat the ceremonial bronze kettle. You wait, eyes averted from the kettle so that it may boil, while your host prepares the implements. The silver spoon. The receptacle of milk, to be turned down politely in accordance with both taste and tradition. A small chocolate biscuit, perched aside the saucer, to be greeted with the classic mantra 'ooh, lovely', and devoured in no fewer than three bites that leave behind no trace of crumb.
translation: 这个仪式对你来说轻车熟路。它从一杯纯净的热水开始，慢慢啜饮以清洁味蕾。午夜鉴赏家们端来一碗炭火，用以加热那精致的青铜茶壶。你静静地等待，目光避开茶壶，让它能够顺利沸腾，而主人则在准备各种器具。银质的勺子。盛着牛奶的小容器——出于口味和传统礼貌地婉拒。旁边碟子上放着一块小巧的巧克力饼干，按照经典的说法要赞叹一声“哦，真好”，然后在不多于三口内吃完，不留下任何碎屑。

original: Ask the Midnight Connoisseurs about the tea
translation: 向午夜鉴赏家问及茶

original: How good can it be to be worth so much trouble?
translation: 到底多好的茶，才值得这么兴师动众？

original: A gasp of shock
translation: 震惊到吸气

original: You would even ask? In this place? So close to its presence? The Midnight Connoisseurs stare at you coldly from behind their tea-cups.
translation: 你竟然会问这样的问题？在这个地方？离午夜甄选如此之近？午夜鉴赏家们从茶杯后面冷冷地盯着你。

original: Attend another tea ceremony
translation: 再参加茶道仪式

original: The experience was quite something, last time.
translation: 上次的茶道体验确有一番滋味。

original: A once in a lifetime opportunity
translation: 千载难逢的机会

original: The Midnight Connoisseurs seem shocked at your request. Few enough get to sample their precious tea once. Nobody gets to have seconds.
translation: 午夜茶鉴赏家们听后大为震惊，那珍贵的茶，能尝一次的已是寥寥无几，还没人尝过第二次。

original: Return to the market
translation: 返回市场

original: The rest of the port awaits down below.
translation: 本地的其余部分位于下方地区。

original: Attend a tea ceremony
translation: 参加茶道仪式

original: Midnight Connoisseurs are extremely choosy about who gets to savour the tea here.
translation: “午夜鉴赏家”对在此品茶的人选极为挑剔。

original: An honoured guest
translation: 贵客驾到

original: The ritual comes easily to you. It begins with a cup of mere hot water, sipped to clear the taste-buds. Midnight Connoisseurs bring forth a bowl of embers on which to heat the ceremonial bronze kettle. You wait, eyes averted from the kettle so that it may boil, while your host prepares the implements. The silver spoon. The receptacle of milk, to be turned down politely in accordance with both taste and tradition. A small chocolate biscuit, perched aside the saucer, to be greeted with the classic mantra 'ooh, lovely', and devoured in no fewer than three bites that leave behind no trace of crumb.
translation: 这个仪式对你来说轻车熟路。它从一杯纯净的热水开始，慢慢啜饮以清洁味蕾。午夜鉴赏家们端来一碗炭火，用以加热那精致的青铜茶壶。你静静地等待，目光避开茶壶，让它能够顺利沸腾，而主人则在准备各种器具。银质的勺子。盛着牛奶的小容器——出于口味和传统礼貌地婉拒。旁边碟子上放着一块小巧的巧克力饼干，按照经典的说法要赞叹一声“哦，真好”，然后在不多于三口内吃完，不留下任何碎屑。

original: The Court of Tea and Spices
translation: 茶与香料宫

original: Clouds of rich scents hang in the air. Though the market is small, it is bustling with both London and native Eleutherian traders. Each cramped stall and barrow is piled high with the region's finest tea leaves, opiates, salts and spices.
translation: 空气中弥漫着浓郁的香气。尽管市场不大，但这里熙熙攘攘，既有来自伦敦的商人，也有厄琉忒里亚当地的商贩。每个拥挤的小摊和手推车上都堆满了该地区最优质的茶叶、鸦片、盐和香料。

original: Browse the tea barrows
translation: 茶摊闲逛

original: Many of the spice merchants have tattoos on their left cheek, denoting what they sell. The Londoners present have yet to adopt the tradition.
translation: 许多香料商人在左脸颊上纹以图案，标识自己出售的商品。而伦敦来的商人尚未采纳这一传统。

original: Endless varieties
translation: 琳琅满目

original: Although this port is mostly famed for its homegrown Midnight's Favour, it is quickly becoming a trade hub for every flavour and blend of tea you could possibly wish for. Customers don't brew them, but bite into the leaves and lick samples off their fingers.
translation: 尽管这个车站主要以本地出产的“午夜甄选”而闻名，但此地正迅速成为一个汇聚各类风味和拼配茶的贸易中心。顾客们并不冲泡茶叶，而是直接咬下茶叶，用手指舔舐品尝。

original: Visit Murgatroyd's Taste of Albion
translation: 造访穆氏阿尔比恩风味茶摊

original: Even out here, you can get a mug of Murgatroyd's finest.
translation: 即使在此荒凉之地，你也能享受到一杯穆加托德店里最上等的茶。

original: Visit the Midnight Garden
translation: 造访午夜花园

original: Steps lead up to a wooden temple, landscaped with flowers and gravel. Not just anyone is welcome. Mere money will not grease the wheels.
translation: 台阶通向一座木制寺庙，周围精心布置了花卉和砾石。这里并非人人皆可入内，金钱也无法轻易打通关节。

original: Purchase some tea in bulk
translation: 购买一批茶叶

original: This would be a good place to stock up, especially if you can haggle.
translation: 这里非常适合补充库存，特别是如果你能讨价还价的话。

original: Fighting down the price
translation: 打压价格

original: You do your best to trade with the merchants, and agree a fairer price. Slightly fairer or much fairer, you can only guess and hope.
translation: 你尽力与商人周旋，商定一个比较公平的价格。至于这是略微公平还是非常公平，你只能要么猜，要么想了。

original: Return to the Market
translation: 返回市场

original: Away from the sickly smells of tea and the cloying scent of incense.
translation: 远离那令人不适的茶香和甜腻的熏香气味。

original: Ask about Midnight's Favour
translation: 询问什么是午夜甄选

original: Stories say it is blacker than night, and tastes even deeper.
translation: 传说，它比夜更黑，比夜更浓。

original: The rarest of delicacies
translation: 稀世佳品

original: Your enquiries draw little but averted eyes and apologies that they 'are not worthy of Midnight's Favour'. The select few who trade in it consider it far too precious to simply sell.
translation: 你的询问只换来游离的目光和“他们不配得到‘午夜甄选’”的道歉。那些少数经营这种商品的人认为此茶太过珍贵，不能随便出售。

original: Visit the Midnight Garden
translation: 造访午夜花园

original: The Midnight Connoisseurs agree that helping to rid the port of Amberley Murgatroyd is worth entrance to their little salon.
translation: 午夜鉴赏家们一致认为，帮助将安布利·穆加托德赶出港口的人有资格进入他们小型沙龙。

original: Visit the Midnight Garden
translation: 造访午夜花园

original: What remains of it now that Midnight's Favour is no more, at least.
translation: 至少现在“午夜恩宠”已经不复存在，它剩下的东西也寥寥无几了。

original: An abandoned memory
translation: 一个被抛弃的记忆

original: The stairs lead up to what used to be a quiet wooden pagoda where the Midnight Connoisseurs held their tea ceremonies. Now, nothing remains but a few strewn mats, broken cups, and the sight of the Halved glaring down from on high. You take a look around for anything of use and, finding nothing but spilled tea, take your leave.
translation: 楼梯通向曾经是午夜鉴赏家举行茶道仪式的宁静木质楼阁。如今，这里只剩下几片散落的草席、破碎的杯子，以及半分者从高处俯视下来的一双冷峻的眼睛。你环顾四周，寻找任何有用的东西，但除了洒在地上的茶水一无所获，走吧。

original: Speak to a Grumbling Urchin
translation: 与一个抱怨的顽童交谈

original: He slouches more than most of them, chewing on an old twig.
translation: 他比其他人更驼背，嘴里嚼着一根旧树枝。

original: Quest for Chocolate
translation: 巧克力任务

original: "Just bored of rations, okay," He spits out the twig. "Ol' Sigrid keeps all the chocolate round here locked up in the Nightingale." He grins. "Maybe you could sneak some of it out of that desk of hers. Could make it worth your while..."
translation: “只是厌倦了配给物资，行了吧。”他吐出了嘴里的树枝。“老西格丽德把所有的巧克力都锁在‘夜莺’里。”他笑着说道，“也许你可以从她的桌子里面偷一些出来。这对你我都有好处……”

original: Search for Clay Men for the Clay Conductor
translation: 为粘土人列车主管寻找粘土人

original: Amberley Murgatroyd has been thrown out of Achlys, but perhaps some of her staff stayed on. A few coins should get the market sellers talking.
translation: 安布利·穆加托德已经被驱逐出了埃克吕斯，但也许她的一些员工留了下来。几枚硬币应该能让市场上的商贩们开口。

original: Echoing across the marsh
translation: 回荡在沼泽之上

original:
Your coin buys a number of loose tongues. The Clay Men it transpires have been sheltering in the ruins of the Taste of Albion. Everyone has been too awkward to attempt a reconciliation, but your coin convinces the Clay Men to at least come out into the market.

The Clay Conductor requests that they sing for him.The other Clay Men look reluctant, embarrassed even, but one with shale skin steps forward. "It has been too long. But we should still sing." 

Following his lead, the Clay Men launch into a mournful, hollow aria that resonates within your rib cage. The crowd of market sellers shiver as the last notes die away. 

The Clay Conductor is quiet for a long minute. At last, he gives his verdict. "No." He stomps away, back towards your engine.
translation:
你的几枚硬币买来了不少松动的舌头。原来，粘土人们一直在“阿尔比昂风味”的废墟中避难。大家都碍于情面，不愿和解，但你的硬币至少说服了粘土人走出店门，来到集市上。

粘土人列车主管请求他们为他唱歌。其他粘土人看起来很不情愿，甚至有些尴尬，但其中一个有着页岩皮肤的粘土人走上前。“已经太久了。但我们应该还能唱。”

在它的带领下，粘土人开始了一段哀伤而空灵的咏叹调，那声音在你的胸腔内回响。即使是那些熙熙攘攘的市场摊贩们，在最后一个音符消逝时也不禁打了个寒战。

粘土人列车主管沉默了许久。终于，他给出了评价：“不。”然后他走开了，回到你们的机车那边，脚步沉重。

original: The Ruined Monastery
translation: 修道院遗址

original: Petrified veins run down the side of this ancient structure. Two giant featureless doors block the crumbling entrance, far too large for any human to open. The metal is unfamiliar, but resilient. Unfortunately the same cannot be said of the monastery itself. [qvd:135933(MonasteryStatus)]
translation: 古老的建筑一侧布满了石化的脉络。两扇庞大却朴实的大门挡住了破败的入口，它们如此巨大，得远非任何人类能够打开。这种金属看似陌生但却坚韧无比。遗憾的是，修道院本身没有这么坚固。[qvd:135933(MonasteryStatus)]

original: Return to the Market
translation: 返回市场

original: There is nothing to be done here at the moment.
translation: 此刻这里没有什么可做的。

original: Demand entrance
translation: 要求进入

original: They say the Monastery opens only for those undergoing great torment. Rumours are less clear on exactly how 'they' know this.
translation: 他们说，修道院只为那些正在经受巨大折磨的人开放。关于“他们”是如何知道这一点的，传言却语焉不详。

original: Silence
translation: 沉默

original: The doors do not open. However, from above, a vine languorously extends downwards to where you wait. Its leaves peel away, forming a cup filled with slightly brown, bitter tasting cold water. One sip and the world begins to spin. Darken. Fall.
translation: 大门并未打开。然而，从上方，一株藤蔓慵懒地垂下，来到你等待的地方。它的叶子剥落，形成一个杯子，里面盛满了微褐色、略带苦味的冷水。仅仅一口，世界就开始旋转、变暗，最后陷入一片黑暗。

original: Speak with an Impatient Penitent
translation: 与一个不耐烦的忏悔者交谈

original: He beats his fists against the doors, getting nothing but bloody knuckles for his trouble.
translation: 他用拳头捶打大门，但最终只落得血迹斑斑的指关节，徒劳无功。

original: A lost love
translation: 失落的爱人

original: "You." He blinks tears from his eyes. "You're a captain, right? You've got the look about you. Maybe you can help. My husband, he was never the same after he came back from the zee with that tattoo. The eye. That blasted eye, it drew him here, I'm sure of it."
translation: “是你。” 他眨了眨眼中的泪水。“你是位车长，不是吗？我看得出来。或许你可以帮帮忙。我的丈夫，自他带着那个纹身从地下海泽回来后，就再也不是原来那个人了。那只眼睛。那只该死的眼睛，它把他引到这里来了，我敢肯定。”

original: The House of Silks
translation: 丝绸之家

original: The curtains part with a sickly sweet breath of incense. Velvet wraps the inside of the hut like a fine chocolate box, with silk curtains delicately hanging down to provide translucent privacy for guests. Behind, the shadows of wealthy traders lie in the embrace of soft, well-plumped cushions, gently sipping from bronze hookah pipes until their eyes and troubles are somewhere else entirely.
translation: 窗帘拉开，散发出令人作呕的甜香。天鹅绒像一个精致的巧克力盒一样覆盖着小屋的内部，丝绸窗帘精致地垂下，为客人提供半透明的隐私。在后面，富商的影子躺在柔软、丰满的垫子的怀抱中，轻轻地啜饮着青铜水烟，直到他们的眼睛和烦恼完全移到别处。

original: Request an audience with Mr Pipes
translation: 请求与烟管先生会面

original: The hooded proprietor keeps to itself at the back of the House. A particularly large hookah pipe delivers smoke into the darkness of its cloak. A gramophone beside it quietly plays a Bach concerto.
translation: 戴兜帽的老板一直躲在房子的后面。一个特别大的水烟筒将烟雾送入其斗篷的黑暗中。旁边的留声机静静地播放着巴赫的协奏曲。

original: An apologetic refusal
translation: 带歉意的拒绝

original: A serving boy returns, bowing apologetically. Mr Pipes is relaxing and has no interest in either chitter or chatter. If you have business, you may present it to one of the staff. Otherwise, his master encourages you to avail yourself of the facilities.
translation: 一个侍童回来了，带着歉意鞠了一躬，告诉你：烟管先生正在放松，暂无会面的雅兴。如果你有事，可以转告工作人员；如果没有事，他的主人邀请你试试店里的水烟。

original: Present the Seal of Mr Barleycorn to Mr Pipes
translation: 向烟管先生展示麦寸先生的印章

original: This should get the master of the house's attention.
translation: 这应该能引起屋主的注意。

original: A moment's silence
translation: 片刻的静默

original: A serving girl takes the wax seal to her snoozing master and whispers something into its cloak. A moment passes and she returns, with a certain amount of trepidation. "My master trusts that this is what you require. May it do you some good, or at least no harm."
translation: 一个侍女把蜡封印章拿给她打瞌睡的主人，又对着它的斗篷里面低声说了些什么。过了一会儿，她回来了，带着几分惶恐。“我的主人相信这是您需要的东西。愿它对您有好处，或者至少没有伤害。”

original: Sit down with a hookah pipe
translation: 坐下来，拿起水烟管

original: The cushions are soft. The honeyed incense is sweet.
translation: 坐垫柔软。蜜香甘甜。

original: Smoke and relaxation
translation: 烟雾和放松
