translation: 使用一个古老的杀手诡计，你摆脱了那些怒目而视的头颅的注意。那个看起来像你阿姨的头清了清嗓子（鉴于她的生理结构，这是一个成就）。“我的同事的身份并不重要。重要的是观点。绝对的论调对于这次讨论没有帮助。”

original: Lend the beleaguered head your sight
translation: 将你的视力借给受困的头

original:
You represent a fresh pair of eyes. And, admittedly, not much else at the moment.
[If you fail, you will lose some Mirrors.]
translation:
你代表一双新鲜的眼睛。而且，说实在的，目前也不能代表更多东西了。
[如果失败，你会失去一些镜子。]

original: Standing her ground
translation: 站在她的立场上

original: "Quite right." The head that looks like your aunt agrees. "My associate's identity isn't important. Their point is. Absolutes aren't a helpful frame for this discussion."
translation: “不错。”那个看起来像你阿姨的头附和道。“我的同事的身份并不重要。重要的是观点。绝对的论调对于这次讨论没有帮助。”

original: Borrowing your eyes
translation: 借用你的眼睛

original:
"Yes, I think that's what I need," the head that looks like your aunt mumbles. Vines crawl around your face. You feel their frondules unfurl, pushing their way insistently under your eyelids. A sharp pain. 

"Thank you, that's helpful." She turns her attention back to the other heads. "My associate's identity isn't important. Their point is. Absolutes aren't a helpful frame for this discussion."
translation:
“是的，我想这就是我需要的。”那个看起来像你阿姨的头颅喃喃道。藤蔓爬上你的脸。你感到它们的叶子展开了，坚持不懈地向你的眼皮底下推进。一阵剧痛。

“谢谢你，这很有帮助。”她把注意力转回到其他的头颅上。“我的同事的身份并不重要。重要的是观点。绝对的论调对于这次讨论没有帮助。”

original: Present a counterpoint
translation: 提出反驳意见

original:
The Heart-Catchers are here to advise, not to decide. This one has done so as well as it was able.
[This course is reliable, but costs a Moment of Inspiration.]
translation:
捕心花在此提供建议，而不是做出决定。这株捕心花已经尽其所能地做到了这一点。
[这种做法比较可靠，但需要花费一个瞬间的灵感。]

original: Close enough
translation: 足够了

original: The head nods in its cradle of vines. "This is so. We have never given advice we knew to be false. We have not wasted our cognition on matters of no significance. We have, of course, been wrong, and will be so again. But that has to be acceptable. We don't have the privilege of certainty: we are counsellors, not priests."
translation: 头颅在藤蔓的摇篮当中点了点头。“就是这样。我们从未给出过自己认为虚假的建议。我们从未为微不足道的小事浪费过脑力。当然，我们犯过错误，而且未来还会再犯。不过你应当接受这一点。我们并没有必然的特权；我们是顾问，不是主教。”

original: Lend the last healthy head your ambition
translation: 将你的野心借给最后的健康的头

original:
And let her make a counter-claim to the accusations of her persecutors.
[If you fail, you will lose some Iron.]
translation:
并让她对迫害她的人的指控提出反驳。
[如果失败，你会失去一些钢铁。]

original: Determination
translation: 决心

original:
She falters in her initial points; you encourage her to be bold in them. She rallies.

"We have never given advice we knew to be false. We have not wasted our cognition on matters of no significance. We have, of course, been wrong, and will be so again. But that has to be acceptable. We don't have the privilege of certainty: we are counsellors, not priests."
translation:
她最初的观点动摇了，而你鼓励她大胆地把它说出口。她振作起来。

“我们从来不会给出明知是错误的建议，我们不会把自己的认知浪费在不重要的事情上。当然，我们曾经犯过错，也会再次犯错。但我们必须接受这件事。我们没有确定事物的特权：我们是顾问，不是牧师。”

original: The sacrifice
translation: 祭品

original:
She falters in her initial points. Your encouragement is insufficient. "Forgive me," she says, and you feel briars writhe about you. The thorns dig deep, and drink of you. As she feeds on your confidence, she rallies.

"We have never given advice we knew to be false. We have not wasted our cognition on matters of no significance. We have, of course, been wrong, and will be so again. But that has to be acceptable. We don't have the privilege of certainty: we are counsellors, not priests."
translation:
她最初的观点动摇了。你的鼓励收效甚微。“原谅我，”她说，你感觉到荆棘在你周围扭动。尖刺深深地扎入你的身体，吸食着你。当她汲取你的信心时，她振作了起来。

“我们从来不会给出明知是错误的建议，我们不会把自己的认知浪费在不重要的事情上。当然，我们曾经犯过错，也会再次犯错。但我们必须接受这件事。我们没有确定事物的特权：我们是顾问，不是牧师。”

original: Listen to her response
translation: 听听她的回答

original: You have helped her as much as you could. Now you find out if it was enough.
translation: 你已经尽你所能地帮助了她。现在看看这是否足够。

original: Sometimes, a stalemate is enough
translation: 有时候，平局便已足够

original:
"I believe it more than I don't," she answers. "Marginally. And that will have to do."

A couple of the other heads nod, convinced. The pinch-faced head is one of them. "Perhaps it will," he says. The green tinge has faded from his cheeks. 

The majority of the heads are still poisoned. The Heart-Catcher is not cured. But maybe it can manage.

Some time later, during the Hour of Knots, the Green-Fingered Old Warhorse retrieves your head. There is another bloody and elaborate rite in the lamp-lit grove. With a complex series of stitches, your head is restored to your shoulders. You are left with a persistent itch, though, around the base of your neck. It will endure to the end of your days.
translation:
“我对这一观点的相信多于不相信，”她回答，“只是稍微多一点。但这样就够了。”

另外几颗头颅也点点头，表示相信。一个面色苍白的头也是其中之一。“也许够了，”他说。绿色的色彩已经从他的脸颊上褪去。

大多数头仍然中毒。捕心树并没有被治愈。但也许它可以自己处理好这一切。

一段时间后，在缠结之时，擅长园艺的老兵取回了你的头。在灯火通明的小树林里，还有另一场血腥而繁琐的仪式。通过许多复杂的缝合，你的头回到了你的肩上。不过，你的脖子根部留下了持续的瘙痒。它将持续到你生命的尽头。

original: Listen to her response
translation: 听听她的回答

original: You have helped her as much as you could. Now you find out if it was enough.
translation: 你已经尽你所能地帮助了她。现在看看这是否足够。

original: An ending
translation: 结局

original: "No," she admits, and you watch the poison crawl greenly along the veins in her face. She and the other heads turn to regard you. "Now," she says, "let's talk about you." At some point, when the heads lapse into a short, brooding silence, the Green-Fingered Old Warhorse is beside you. Is he on a ladder? "Alas," he is saying, "that leaves you as the final fruit of the tree. Or the closest we've got. You're all that's keeping the poison from reaching the heartwood. We're looking for another willing to undergo the rite, but you'll just have to hold out as long as you can." The will not be another, not in time. Your fellow heads begin to stir from their thoughts. You can feel the dull ache of the poison. [Your captain has met their end.]
translation: “不，”她说道，然后你看见绿色的毒液沿着她脸上的血管慢慢爬动。 她和其他的头颅都转过来看着你。“现在，”她说，“让我们谈谈你的事。” 在某个时候，当这些头陷入短暂的、沉思的静默时，擅长园艺的老兵来到了你身边。他是站在一个梯子上吗？ “唉，”他说，“你得成为树上的最后一个果实。或者说仅剩的几个果实之一。你是唯一能阻止毒药到达心材的人。我们正在寻找另一个愿意接受仪式的人，但你必须尽可能地坚持下去。” 不会有另一个人了，来不及了。其他的头开始行动起来。你能感觉到毒药的钝痛。 [你的车长走向了末路。]

original: The Nepenthine Ritual
translation: 支离仪式

original:
First, you are asked to inhale mists from a copper bowl. "Vapours from the Achlean marsh," the Old Warhorse explains. "It's for the best." Your world disjoints. Events separate into isolated moments, each untroubled by sensation or emotion.

A lamp-lit grove, ringed by veiled gardeners. 

The heads of a Heart-Catcher looking down at you, speaking with tongues of fire.

The Old Warhorse advancing with a set of garden shears...
translation:
首先，你被要求从铜碗中吸入雾气。“来自埃克利沼泽的蒸气，”老兵解释道，“以防万一。”你的世界支离破碎。事件被分割为孤立的时刻，每个时刻都不受感觉或情绪的困扰。

灯火通明的小树林，周围环绕着蒙着面纱的园丁。

捕心花的头颅俯视着你，用火舌说话。

老兵拿着一把花园剪刀走上前……

original: Object
translation: 反对

original:
This was a terrible idea.
[You will be able to try again in the future.]
translation:
这是个糟糕透顶的主意。
[将来你可以再度尝试。]

original: Spared
translation: 幸免于难

original: The shears pause, withdraw, and slowly close. How disappointed they seem, when the firelight winks out on their edge. Later, your perception of events reassembles itself. You feel things again, things like horror and a splitting headache. The Old Warhorse's expression is neutral. "If you change your mind – again – tell us."
translation: 剪子停下来，退了回去，然后慢慢合上。当火光在它们的刀锋上闪烁时，它们看上去多么失望啊。 随后，你的现实意识重新组合起来。你再次感受到一些东西，比如恐惧和欲裂头痛。老兵表情平静，“如果你再次改变了主意，请告诉我们。”

original: Observe how the firelight gleams upon the blades
translation: 观察在剪刀的刀身上跃动的火光

original: Let what will be, be.
translation: 随它去吧。

original: Among the branches
translation: 在树枝间

original:
A sharp sound, like tailor's scissors. A period of darkness. Then you are being carried, facing backwards. You can't see where you're going, but you can see what's left behind: a body, slumped among the roots of a Heart-Catcher. It does not look back at you. It cannot.

Then you are lifted up and set among the branches of another Heart-Catcher. Around you dangle a gallery of stern heads. The nearest is unsmiling, distinguished, and reminds you of your aunt. This is the head you are here to help. The others cluster about it like vultures. Their cheeks are veined with green poison.
translation:
一声锐响，就像裁缝的剪刀。一时黑暗。然后你被人抬着，背对前方。你看不到你要去的地方，但你能看到后面留下的东西：一具尸体，倒在捕心树的根部之间。它没有回望你。它已无法这么做。

然后你被举起，放置在另一株捕心树的树枝之中。在你的周围，悬挂着一大堆面色严肃的头颅。离你最近的一个不苟言笑，卓然不群，让你想起了你的姨妈。这就是你在这里要帮助的头。其他的像秃鹰一样聚集在它周围。它们的脸颊上有绿色的毒纹。

original: The London Embassy
translation: 伦敦大使馆

original: The Ambassador greets you in his study. Instead of a fire burning in the hearth, there is an electrical heater that smells faintly of burning hair. Everything else is comfortingly old-fashioned, from the creaking leather of the armchairs, to the vintage of brandy in the drinks cabinet.
translation: 大使在他的书房里迎接你。炉膛里没有火，取而代之的是有一股烧焦毛发味道的电暖炉。除此之外从扶手椅吱吱作响的皮革沙发，到饮料柜中陈年的白兰地，全都是令人感到舒适的老式风格，

original: Warn the Ambassador of the Bespectacled Official
translation: 向大使警告那位戴眼镜的事务官

original: A foreign agent contacted you. He should be told.
translation: 一个外国特工联系了你。应该告诉他。

original: A familiar story
translation: 一个熟悉的故事

original:
The Ambassador is entirely unsurprised. "Oh, don't worry. His lot in the Rose-Without-Thorns try that with everyone. 

"Between you and me, I think it's mostly just their way of showing us that their people are always watching ours. A blasted nuisance, but we can't complain. If more of them came to London, we'd be doing the exact same thing."
translation:
大使完全不感到惊讶。“哦，别担心。他在‘无刺玫瑰’的那批人对每个人都会这样做。”

“私下里，我认为这主要是他们向我们展示他们的人一直在监视我们的方式。真是令人讨厌，但我们没什么好抱怨的。如果有更多的人来伦敦，我们也会做同样的事情。”

original: Ask how you might help the Embassy
translation: 询问你可以如何协助大使馆

original: Perhaps the Ambassador has some special requests.
translation: 也许大使有一些特殊的请求。

original: The House of Rods and Chains
translation: 链杆之屋

original: The Ambassador swirls the brandy in his glass. "London is entirely open with her Empyreal allies. That being said, if we had illicit eyes in the field, I imagine they would have had difficulty getting reliable reports from the House of Rods and Chains. A shame. I have money put aside for exactly that kind of information." [dir:b14c0b6b-839c-4311-bfd5-518edeea28ad].
translation: 大使在他的酒杯里搅动白兰地。“伦敦对她的上国盟友完全开放。话虽如此，如果我们在外地有非法的眼线，我想他们很难从链杆之屋里得到可靠的报告。真遗憾。我专门留出了一些钱来获取这类信息。” [dir:b14c0b6b-839c-4311-bfd5-518edeea28ad]。

original: Ask how you might help the Embassy
translation: 询问你可以如何协助大使馆

original: Perhaps the Ambassador has some special requests.
translation: 也许大使有一些特殊的请求。

original: Piranesi
translation: 皮拉内西

original:
The Ambassador warms his hands on the electric fire. "Ah, yes, the prisoners of Piranesi. We keep an eye on who goes in. The real question is: who comes out? Yesterday's enemies can so quickly be turned to tomorrow's friends. Or vice versa, of course. We prefer having advance warning."

[dir:06401842-00d7-463c-8d6b-6fdd41b2edae].
translation:
大使在电炉上暖他的手。“啊，是的，皮拉内西的囚犯。我们一直关注着谁进去了。真正的问题是：谁出来了？昨天的敌人可以很快变成明天的朋友。当然，反之亦然。我们希望能预先收到警告。”

[dir:06401842-00d7-463c-8d6b-6fdd41b2edae]。

original: Ask how you might help the Embassy
translation: 询问你可以如何协助大使馆

original: Perhaps the Ambassador has some special requests.
translation: 也许大使有一些特殊的请求。

original: Achlys
translation: 埃克吕斯

original:
The Ambassador shows you a map of Eleutheria, so vague that it may as well fill the uncharted areas with warning of dragons. He taps on a small circle.

"Achlys. Lots of our people headed there recently. For the tea, I believe, but that might be code for something else. A shame we can't take a closer look without showing our hosts that we've taken an interest." He tops up his brandy glass.

[dir:9e91ea8e-3f0f-4a25-a400-2f451d91da81].
translation:
大使向你展示厄琉忒里亚的地图，这张地图非常模糊，就像在未知区域上贴满了危险警告一样。他敲了敲一个小圆圈。

“埃克吕斯。我们很多人最近都去了那里。我相信是为了喝茶，但那可能是做其他事情的代号。遗憾的是，我们不能仔细打听，否则会向我们的东家表示我们对此感兴趣。”他给他的白兰地酒杯倒满了酒。

[dir:9e91ea8e-3f0f-4a25-a400-2f451d91da81]。

original: Ask how you might help the Embassy
translation: 询问你可以如何协助大使馆

original: Perhaps the Ambassador has some special requests.
translation: 也许大使有一些特殊的请求。

original: Caduceus
translation: 商神宫

original:
The Ambassador drains his glass. "Never did trust devils. All that buzzing around. Goodness only knows what they're up to at Caduceus. Horrible place. Could be anything. Want a drink?" He leaves the other request implied.

[dir:44773c30-e3dd-4ce4-a8bd-fec7b55bb463].
translation:
大使把杯中酒液一饮而尽。“永远不要相信魔鬼。他们总是在周围嗡个不停。天知道他们究竟在商神宫做些什么。可怕的地方。任何事都有可能发生。想喝一杯吗？”他暗示着其他请求。

[dir:44773c30-e3dd-4ce4-a8bd-fec7b55bb463]。

original: Deliver intelligence on the House of Rods and Chains
translation: 提供有关链杆之屋的情报

original:
It's only spying if the Eagle finds out about it.
[Delivering Intelligence to the Ambassador will raise your standing with the London Embassy and lower it with the Eagle.]
translation:
被鹰国发现的才叫间谍活动。
[向大使提供情报将提高你在伦敦大使馆的地位，并降低你在鹰国的地位。]

original: A quiet exchange
translation: 一次安静的交换

original: The Ambassador does not, of course, take any documents from you. Nor does the clerk who hands you your reward. As you leave, however, [qvd:135155(KnownSwitch)] Bespectacled Official does watch you from a distance. His polite smile is thin.
translation: 大使当然不会从你那里拿任何文件。那个付给你报酬的职员也不会。然而，当你离开时，[qvd:135155(KnownSwitch)]戴眼镜的事务官确实在远处看着你。他礼貌性的微笑显得很淡薄。

original: Deliver intelligence on Piranesi
translation: 提供有关皮拉内西的情报

original:
It's only spying if the Eagle finds out about it.
[Delivering Intelligence to the Ambassador will raise your standing with the London Embassy and lower it with the Eagle.]
translation:
被鹰国发现的才叫间谍活动。
[向大使提供情报将提高你在伦敦大使馆的地位，并降低你在鹰国的地位。]

被鹰国发现的才叫间谍活动。

translation: 大使当然不会从你那里拿任何文件。那个付给你报酬的职员也不会。然而，当你离开时，[qvd:135155(KnownSwitch)]戴眼镜的事务官确实在远处看着你。他礼貌性的微笑显得很淡薄。

original: Smuggle Artefacts into the Empyrean
translation: 将文物偷运进苍天上国

original:
"Empyrean electricity is fascinating," says the Ambassador. "Fascinating, but dangerous. We must tip the technological balance in our favour."
[This will trade three Otherworldly Artefacts for a Moment of Inspiration.]
translation:
“苍天上国的电力技术很迷人，”大使说。“迷人而危险。我们必须让技术的天平倾向我们这边。”
[这将用三个异界遗物换取一个瞬间的灵感。]

original: Advancements in technology
translation: 技术进步

original: The Ambassador's clerk leads you to an unregistered basement, where a layer of soot marks the failure of many attempts to replicate the Eagle's advanced electrical technologies. "Our head researcher suspected the Rose-Without-Thorns kept slipping us sabotaged devices," he says, and points at an oddly human-shaped silhouette on the walls. "Hopefully their replacement will be more careful."
translation: 大使的办事员把你带到一个未经登记的地下室，那里的一层煤烟标志着多次复制上国先进电气技术的失败尝试。“我们的首席研究员怀疑无刺玫瑰一直以来交给我们的都是有问题的设备，”他说，并指了指墙上一个奇怪的人形剪影，“希望替补人员能更小心一点。”

original: Smuggle Secrets into the Empyrean
translation: 将秘密偷运进苍天上国

original:
"What have you heard, I wonder," says the Ambassador. "I know a certain someone who would be most grateful to find out."
[This will trade three Savage Secrets for a Cryptic Benefactor.]
translation:
“我想知道你听到了什么”，大使说，“我认识一个人，他最想知道的就是这个。”
[这将用三个残酷的秘密换取一个隐秘的人脉。]

original: A diplomatic soiree
translation: 外交晚会

original: Your service sees you invited to a dinner that night, where representatives of the London Embassy and their rivals in the Rose-Without-Thorns share drinks and barbed civility. "You can almost see the daggers behind their backs, can't you?" says a figure behind you. "Let me pour you a drink and give you a name you might find useful."
translation: 你的业绩让你被邀请参加当晚的宴会，在那里，伦敦大使馆的代表和他们在无刺玫瑰的对手在餐桌上举杯共饮，互相攻讦。“是不是都快看见他们笑里的刀子了？”你身后的一个人说，“让我敬你一杯，再送你一个名字，说不定他能帮到你。”

original: The Wreck of the Berrenger
translation: 贝伦格号的残骸

original:
[qvd:138177(berrenger_description)]

[qvd:138177(berrenger_description2)]
translation:
[qvd:138177(berrenger_description)]



[qvd:138177(berrenger_description2)]

original: Choose the Mask of the Supplicant
translation: 选择求道者的面具

original:
"The Supplicant's job is to talk," says the Founder, fastening the mask of a hideously-toothed angler fish over your face. "And, perhaps, entice." 
[This mask gives opportunities to deliver lectures.]
translation:
“求道者的工作是言语，”创始人说，把一张长着骇人牙齿的鮟鱇鱼面具戴到你的脸上，“或许还有引诱。”
[此面具使你能够发表讲演。]

original: The Supplicant
translation: 求道者

original:
A miniature lantern dangles from your new mask, swinging back and forth between your eyes. 

"The Supplicant gives speeches in the Forum," says the Founder. "Thanks to the mask, a person's reputation or lack thereof doesn't matter here. Just stand and talk and if you're saying something worthwhile, perhaps you'll attract an audience."
translation:
一盏微型灯笼悬挂在你的新面具上，在你的两眼之间前后摆动。

“求道者在论坛上发表演讲，”创始人说道，“由于戴着面具，美誉或恶名在此处全无用处。只要站在那里说就行，如果说出有价值的东西，你也许能吸引到观众。”

original: Choose the Mask of the Aspirant
translation: 选择有志者的面具

original:
A sculpted silver rose, blank, eyeless, mouthless. "The Aspirant listens," says the Founder. "And blossoms."
[This mask gives opportunities to listen to lectures.]
translation:
一朵雕制而成的银色玫瑰，面容空洞，无眼无嘴。“有志者聆听，”创办者说道，“且盛放。”
[此面具使你能够聆听讲演。]

original: The Aspirant
translation: 有志者

original:
As the mask slips over your face you realise that it is ingeniously designed so that you can see perfectly between the folds of the silver petals.

"The Aspirant's role is to absorb," says the Founder. "Go to the Library and read a book, or go to the Forum and enjoy yourself. Stay quiet. Grow."
translation:
当面具滑过脸部时，你发现它设计得十分精巧，让你的目光可以完美地自银色花瓣的褶皱中穿过。

“有志者的职责是吸收，”创始人说道，“去图书馆读书，或是去论坛享受讲演。保持静默。成长。”

original: Choose the Mask of the Scintillant
translation: 选择闪烁者的面具

original:
A woman's face, wreathed in glorious flames. "The Scintillant learns through experimentation," says the Founder. "Putting aside concern for the safety of others or themselves."
[This mask gives opportunities to conduct experiments.]
translation:
一个女人的面庞，笼罩在耀眼的火焰中。“闪烁者通过实验来学习，”创始人说道，“全然不顾他人或自身的安全。”
[此面具使你能进行实验。]

original: The Scintillant
translation: 闪烁者

original:
The flames on the mask are orange-yellow tissue which rustles as you move your head. 

"The Scintillant's purpose is to visit the Laboratories and take part in the experiments," says the Founder, clapping you on the back. "Good luck! Last time I went to the Laboratories I lost a finger."
translation:
面具上的火焰由橙黄色的薄纸拼成，当你移动头部时，它发出沙沙声。

“闪烁者的目的是拜访实验室，参与实验，”创始人拍拍你的肩膀，说道，“祝你好运！上次去实验室时，我丢了一根手指。”

original: Choose the Mask of the Recalcitrant
translation: 选择顽抗者的面具

original:
A snarling face halfway between bulldog and gargoyle. "A difficult role," cautions the Founder. "A squabbler. Recommended for those who've spent time as an Aspirant."
[This mask gives opportunities to debate.]
translation:
一张介于斗牛犬和石像鬼之间的狰狞面庞。“这是一个困难的角色，”创始人警告道。“一个争吵者。推荐给那些曾经做过一段时间有志者的人。”
[此面具使你能够进行争论。]

original: The Recalcitrant
translation: 顽抗者

original:
The mask is oddly uncomfortable, digging into your skin, cutting off the blood to your ears. You peer out through a wall of gruesome fangs.

"Go to the Forum or the Debating Halls, and raise hell," says the Founder. "Ask impertinent questions. Hit close to home. The mask allows you to speak loudly and truthfully without losing friends."
translation:
面具戴起来很奇怪，很不舒服，它深深地扎进你的皮肤，阻断了流向你耳朵的血液。你透过重重阴森獠牙向外张望。

“去论坛或辩论厅大肆批判，”创始人说道，“提出一些无礼的问题。直击要害。面具能让你大声说出真相，而不会失去朋友。”

original: Speak to the Unassailable Founder
translation: 与无懈可击的创始人交谈

original: Before you don a mask, you have questions. Who is she? How did the Berrenger end up out here?
translation: 在戴上面具之前，你有一些疑问。她是谁？贝伦格号怎么会出现在这里？

original: Questions, Questions
translation: 疑问重重

original:
How did a London dreadnought end up wrecked in Eleutheria, crowded with devotees of the Liberation of Night? The Founder waves a gloved finger disapprovingly.

"I can't go prattling my secrets to just anyone, can I? Join our community, put your trust in us, and I'll extend some trust in return."
translation:
一台伦敦无畏机车怎么会在满是黑夜解放信徒的厄琉忒里亚撞毁？创始人不以为然地挥了挥戴着手套的手。

“我不能随便向任何人吐露我的秘密，不是吗？加入我们的社区，信任我们，然后我们就会回报你的信任。”

original: Leave the Berrenger
translation: 离开贝伦格号

original: The anarchists gather at the railings to wave you goodbye.
translation: 无政府主义者们聚集在栏杆前向你挥手告别。

original: Your face, returned
translation: 你的脸回来了

original: Your crew express a measure of relief at leaving behind the Berrenger's babble, its crowds, its ceaseless bustle. Not to mention that riotous smell of rust and sweat and gunpowder. As the unremittent darkness swallows your train again, their relief turns to dismay. Maybe the Berrenger wasn't so bad, they say. Maybe you could turn around?
translation: 你的列车员对摆脱贝伦格号上的谈话、人群与永无休止的喧闹的打算感到如释重负。更不用说远离那里浓郁的铁锈味、汗水味和火药味了。 当无尽的黑暗再次吞噬你的火车时，他们的轻松变成了沮丧。他们说，也许贝伦格号没那么糟。也许你可以掉转车头？

original: Seek out the Diabolical Contriver
translation: 寻找魔鬼发明家

original: She is said to be working on an experimental engine somewhere on the Berrenger.
translation: 据说她正在贝伦格上开发某个实验性引擎。

original: Visit the Diabolical Contriver
translation: 拜访魔鬼发明家

original: You are known to her. Her guard, a burly, huffing goat-demon, will let you pass.
translation: 她认得你。她的守卫，一个魁梧的、气息粗重的山羊魔鬼，会让你通过。

original: Collect the Devourer of Distance from the Diabolical Contriver
translation: 为魔鬼发明家收集路距食客

original: The Devourer, when not in use, somehow returns to the place where it was brought to life.
translation: 在不行动的时候，路距食客不知为何会回到它被赋予生命的地方。

original: Reunited
translation: 重聚

original:
The Contriver is at work on a looming church of an engine, brassy and bristling with pistons. She waves you towards a corner of the hold. 

The Devourer sits there, clattering to itself under a tarpaulin. You pull the sheet away, and the Devourer falls silent, so as not to frighten you. But as you order your crew to carry it to your locomotive, it can't keep itself from ticking, eagerly.
translation:
发明家正在制作一台巨大的黄铜色发动机，上面活塞密布。她挥手示意你前往货舱的一角。

“吞噬者”就在那里，在防水布下发出咔嗒咔嗒的声音。你拉开罩布，“吞噬者”便安静下来，就好像不想惊吓到你一样。但当你命令列车员将它抬到机车上时，它又开始响起急切的滴答声。

original: A Teeming Wreck
translation: 喧嚷的残骸

original: The Berrenger's rusting innards have been hollowed. The walls and floors of a dozen interlocking corridors have been methodically stripped away, carving a vast hive-like atrium draped with ladders and criss-crossed with rope bridges. Anarchists bustle back and forth between a circle of iron doors below. The largest are labelled "LABORATORIES," "FORUM," and "HALL OF DEBATE." [qvd:137669(berrenger_description)][qvd:137666(berrenger_description)][qvd:137668(berrenger_description)][qvd:137667(berrenger_description)]
translation: 贝伦格号生锈的内腔已被掏空。十几条相互连接的走廊的墙壁和地板被有条不紊地剥离，形成一个巨大的蜂巢状中庭，里面布满梯子，绳索桥纵横交错。 无政府主义者在底层圆形排列的一圈铁门之间忙碌地走来走去。最大的门前面标着“实验室”、“论坛”和“辩论厅”。 [qvd:137669(berrenger_description)][qvd:137666(berrenger_description)][qvd:137668(berrenger_description)][qvd:137667(berrenger_description)]

original: Head to the Forum
translation: 前往论坛

original: A stream of Aspirants, Supplicants and Recalcitrants are barrelling through the double-doors.
translation: 一群有志者、求道者和顽抗者正穿过双重闸门涌过来。

original: Head to the Forum
translation: 前往论坛

original: A stream of Aspirants and Recalcitrants are barrelling through the double-doors.
translation: 一群有志者和顽抗者正穿过双重闸门涌过来。

original: Head to the Forum
translation: 前往论坛

original: A stream of Aspirants and Recalcitrants are barrelling through the double-doors.
translation: 一群有志者和顽抗者正穿过双重闸门涌过来。

original: Make your way to the Laboratories
translation: 前往实验室

original: A crude orange mask-symbol has been painted above the door. Next to it, someone has scrawled 'DANGER! Science occurs within!'
translation: 门上画了一个粗糙的橙色面具符号。在它的旁边，有人写着“危险！此处有科学！”

original: The Hall of Debate
translation: 辩论厅

original: Recalcitrants barge in like ants invading a rival nest. Some wit has painted over the door: "Abandon the slippery slope all ye who enter here."
translation: 顽抗者像蚂蚁入侵敌巢一样闯进辩论厅。某个智者在门上写了一行字：“入此门者，当弃绝一切滑坡谬误。”

original: Approach the Unassailable Founder
translation: 走近无懈可击的创始人

original: Strike up a conversation, or perhaps swap your mask.
translation: 进行交谈，或者交换你的面具。

original: Leave the Berrenger
translation: 离开贝伦格号

original: You hook your mask by the door on the way out.
translation: 你离开时把面具挂在了门边。

original: Your face, returned
translation: 你的脸回来了

original: Your crew express a measure of relief at leaving behind the Berrenger's babble, its crowds, its ceaseless bustle. Not to mention that riotous smell of rust and sweat and gunpowder. As the unremittent darkness swallows your train again, the crew's relief turns to dismay. Maybe the Berrenger wasn't so bad, they say. Maybe you could turn around?
translation: 你的列车员对摆脱贝伦格号上的谈话、人群与永无休止的喧闹的打算感到如释重负。更不用说远离那里浓郁的铁锈味、汗水味和火药味了。 当无尽的黑暗再次吞噬你的火车时，列车员的轻松变成了沮丧。他们说，也许贝伦格号没那么糟。也许你可以掉转车头？

original: Approaching the Berrenger
translation: 驶近贝伦格号

original: A vast wreck, larger than any other locomotive you've seen. Armour rattles in the wind. An Albion flag flies, tattered almost beyond recognition. The hull is cracked like an egg, a charred and tangled engine exposed to the air. The Berrenger, reads the nameplate, though some wag has appended a question mark. As you approach, you see figures scrambling behind guardrails; revolutionary slogans graffitied across every rusted surface. The Berrenger is still very much occupied.
translation: 一个巨大的残骸，比你见过的任何其他机车都要大。装甲在风中吱呀作响。一面阿尔比恩的旗帜飘扬着，破烂得几乎无法辨认。车体像鸡蛋一样裂开了，一个烧焦的、纠缠在一起的发动机暴露在空气中。 贝伦格号，铭牌上写着，尽管某个爱开玩笑的人在上面加了一个问号。当你走近时，你看到一些人在护栏后面争先恐后，革命的口号被涂抹在每一个生锈的表面。 贝伦格号里面仍然很拥挤。

original: Board the Berrenger
translation: 登上贝伦格号

original: A dozen figures in heavy coats hang from the side of the wreck, waving joyously as your engine docks.
translation: 十几个人穿着厚重的外套挂在残骸的一侧，当你的机车停靠时，他们高兴地挥手致意。

original: A masked welcome
translation: 蒙面的欢迎

original: You step into the Berrenger's halls, to a swelling crowd and a babble of cheery greetings. Every one is wearing a mask. The crowd parts; a woman glides to your side. Her scarlet leather jacket gleams with buckles and vestigial straps; her face is hidden behind a mask in the shape of a screeching bat's face. "Glad to have you aboard," says the Unassailable Founder, shaking your hand.
translation: 你走进贝伦格号的大厅，眼前是涌动的人群和一片欢呼雀跃的问候声。每个人都戴着面具。 人群分开，一个女人溜到你身边。她猩红色皮夹克上的搭扣和残留的带子闪闪发光；她的脸藏在一个尖叫的蝙蝠脸形状的面具后面。 “很高兴你能在来这里，”无懈可击的创始人说着，与你握手。

original: Board the Berrenger
translation: 登上贝伦格号

original: A dozen figures in heavy coats hang from the side of the wreck, waving joyously as your engine docks.
translation: 十几个人穿着厚重的外套挂在残骸的一侧，当你的机车停靠时，他们高兴地挥手致意。

original: A masked welcome
translation: 蒙面的欢迎

original: You step into the Berrenger's halls, to a swelling crowd and a babble of cheery greetings. Every one is wearing a mask. "Welcome back," says the Unassailable Founder, shaking your hand.
translation: 你走进贝伦格号的大厅，眼前是涌动的人群和一片欢呼雀跃的问候声。每个人都戴着面具。 “欢迎回来，”无懈可击的创始人说着与你握手。

original: The Forum
translation: 论坛

original:
The Forum greets you with a cacophony of competing voices and the acrid stench of gunpowder. This was once the dreadnought's vast storage-room, and now munitions crates have been stacked and shoved together to create a semi-circle of stages. Hopefully no one lights a cigarette.

The stages are occupied by Supplicants, voices raised.
translation:
论坛里迎面是刺耳的争论声与刺鼻的火药味。这里曾经是无畏机车的巨大储藏室，现在这里的弹药箱垒成了一个半圆形的讲台。希望不会有人在这里点烟。

讲台上挤满了求道者。众声喧哗。

original: Deliver a lecture on the origins of the Cantankeri
translation: 发表有关顽固虱之起源的讲演

original:
You climb atop a stack of crates and set out your diagrams.
[qvd:137723(founder_description)]
translation:
你爬到一叠箱子上，摆出你的图表。
[qvd:137723(founder_description)]

original: The Origins of the Cantankeri
translation: 顽固虱之起源

original:
With great authority, you take your audience through the diagrams one by one: carapace, antennae, drill (which alone requires six different cross-sections to explain).

You swap biology for geology. The carapace is igneous rock; the crystals scattered throughout indicate rapidly-frozen lava. To have been encased in this kind of stone, the Cantankeri must be truly ancient – and whatever world they came from, it was in the process of freezing over.

By the time you finish your lecture, your audience is huge and rapt. Aspirants raise their hands with polite questions; Recalcitrants slink away, unable to spot weakness.

You are given several overflowing gift-hampers by impressed audience-members.

[You cannot deliver another lecture for 15 days.]
translation:
你以权威的口吻带领观众逐一浏览图表：甲壳、触角、钻头（仅解释这一部分就需要六个不同的横截面图）。


你采用地质学方法分析，而非生物学。甲壳是火成岩：散布各处的晶体表明它是骤然冻结的熔岩。顽固虱能被这种石头包裹，说明它们一定非常古老——而且无论他们来自哪个疆域，那里都曾被冰封。


当你结束演讲时，面前已聚集起一大堆全神贯注的听众。有志者举手提出礼貌的问题；顽抗者则无法找出你的漏洞，悄悄地溜走了。

[15天后你才能再度发表讲演。]

original: Deliver a lecture on the place-behind-glass
translation: 发表有关玻璃后面的讲演

original:
The results of your mirror-research are sure to attract an audience.
[qvd:137723(founder_description)]
translation:
你对镜子的研究肯定会吸引观众。
[qvd:137723(founder_description)]

original: Your findings
translation: 你的发现

original:
You begin your lecture by warning your audience that you've been tampering in things which humanity was not meant to know, and that therefore the results still need to be reliably replicated.

Cribbing from your copious notes, you deliver a lecture on the intricacies and vagaries of the Is-Not. The correct way to climb inside a mirror; the means by which a traveller can dream a palace; speculations on why the barrier between Is and Is-Not has become so much less permeable in recent years.

Your audience swells, many of them furiously taking notes. When your talk is complete, you find yourself mobbed with questions.
translation:
你在演讲开始时就警告听众，你一直在触碰一些人类本不该知道的事物，因此结果仍然需要以更可靠的手段复现。

根据自己丰富的笔记，你发表了一场关于“无何有之物”的复杂性和善变性的讲演。爬入镜中的正确方法；旅行者梦见宫殿的方法；关于为什么近年来“有”与“无何有”之间的障碍变得如此难以逾越的推测。

你的听众越来越多，大多都疯狂地记着笔记。演讲结束后，你发现自己被一堆问题包围了。

original: Deliver a lecture on the Extinguishments
translation: 发表有关熄处的讲演

original:
Out in the furious emptiness, there are places that have never known light or heat.
[qvd:137723(founder_description)]
translation:
在狂搅的虚空中，有一些从未见过光和热的地方。
[qvd:137723(founder_description)]

original: The Extinguishments
translation: 熄处

original:
Your approach is academic, your tone matter-of-fact, but the Aspirants listen as though to a ghost story. There are places of darkness in Eleutheria, you tell them, a darkness so total it devours even the memory of light. Your audience whispers and swells.

What does such emptiness conceal? Unlit trains that plunged into the darkness hoping to commit crimes beyond the sight of any god. Disgraced servitors, hiding for millennia from otherwise-omniscient masters.

At the end of your lecture, your audience are too subdued to ask questions. The spectres of an Extinguishment seems to hang in the air above you, fascinating and repellent in equal measure.
translation:
你秉承着学术研究方法与实事求是语气，但有志者像在听鬼故事一样听着你的讲演。你告诉他们，厄琉忒里亚有一片阴暗得足以吞噬记忆中光明的暗处。听众们窃窃私语，情绪高涨。

如此空虚是为了掩盖什么？熄灭灯光的火车冲入黑暗，企图犯下任何神明都无法看见的罪行。蒙羞的仆从，在此处躲避无所不知的主人数千年。

在你的讲演结束时，你的听众已经被震慑得无法提问。熄处的幽魂们似乎悬在你们上空，既令人着迷，又令人厌恶。

original: Tell a story from your travels
translation: 讲一个你的旅行故事

original: It's not precisely a lecture, but as a Supplicant, you can speak about whatever you wish. The right audience will find you.
translation: 这并不完全是一场讲演，但作为求道者，你可以讲任何你想讲的东西。正确的听众会找到你。

original: A decent story
translation: 一个不错的故事

original: You climb onto an unoccupied stack of bomb-crates and launch into a reliable favourite from your stable of anecdotes. You attract a small but excitable audience, who gasp and cheer at all the appropriate moments. When you reach the conclusion, they applaud more than politeness necessitates.
translation: 你爬上一堆无人看管的炸弹箱，然后从收藏的趣闻轶事中挑选出最吸引人的话题。你吸引了一小群兴奋的观众，他们在适当的时刻发出惊叹和欢呼。当你讲完时，他们会报以超出礼节性的掌声。

original: Tell a story from your travels
translation: 讲一个你的旅行故事

original: You're wearing the wrong mask, but surely they won't mind if you deliver an impromptu talk?
translation: 你戴错了面具，但他们肯定不会介意你发表一场即兴演讲吧？

original: An interrupted story
translation: 一个被打断的故事

original:
You climb onto an unoccupied stack of bomb-crates and launch into a reliable favourite from your stable of anecdotes, but are quickly overwhelmed by jeers from the audience.

"You've got the wrong face on, Aspirant!" shouts one of the bulldog-masked Recalcitrants. The crowd surges forward and topples you from your stage, passing you like a parcel to the exit.
translation:
你爬上一堆无人看管的炸弹箱，然后从收藏的趣闻轶事中挑选出最吸引人的话题，但你的话很快就被听众的嘲笑淹没了。

“你的脸不对，有志者！”一个戴着斗牛犬面具的顽抗者喊道。人群涌上前来，把你推下讲台，像送包裹一样把你送到出口。

original: Attend a lecture
translation: 参加一场讲演

original: You flit between Supplicants. One is tripping over his words, another reaching her conclusion. Finally, you find a speaker whose words are intriguing.
translation: 你在众多求道者之间穿梭。一个在磕磕巴巴地说着话，另一个在得出结论。最后，你找到了一位言辞有趣的演讲者。

translation: 参加一场讲演

translation: 参加一场讲演

original: The roses' reproach
translation: 玫瑰的责备

original:
A ripple of discontent spreads through the audience as you take your place among their ranks. The light of your mask-lantern couldn't be more glaring. The surrounding Aspirants rotate to face you, a field of silver roses staring in expectant silence. 

The Supplicant on stage pauses, his own lantern swinging as his fish-visage turns your way. "It's bad form to interrupt another's lecture," he says. "Get your own stage."
translation:
当你在他们的队伍中就位时，一股不满足的涟漪在听众中扩散开来。你的面具——那灯笼的光线再刺眼不过了。周围的有志者都转头面向你，一片银色玫瑰在暗藏期盼的沉寂中凝望着你。

台上的求道者停了下来，他鱼一般的面容转向你的方向，他自己的灯笼也随之摆动。“打断别人的演讲很不礼貌，”他说。“去找你自己的演讲台。”

translation: 讲一个你的旅行故事

original: Leave the Forum
translation: 离开论坛

original: You push your way through crowds of flowers.
translation: 你从花丛中挤了出去。

original: A retreat
translation: 撤退

original: The clamour of a thousand mingled speeches fades as you return to the hollow at the Berrenger's core.
translation: 当你回到贝伦格号空荡的中心区域时，无数混杂在一起的讲演喧嚣声逐渐消散了。

original: Today's Lecture
translation: 今日的讲演

[qvd:137675(speech_description)]

[qvd:137781(speech_description)]
translation:
[qvd:137675(speech_description)]

original: Listen to the old woman's lecture
translation: 聆听老妇人的讲演

original:
What could she be talking about?
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[You will gain Terror and an Eleutherian Mystery.]
translation:
她能说什么？
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[你会获得恐惧与一个厄琉忒里亚之谜。]

original: The Discordance
translation: 不谐律

original:
"There is an alphabet of fire and gold," says your lecturer, taking a sip from a glass. "A star-language that burns in the mind." 

She dips her finger in the water, and traces something on the stage. "Some stars abandon the immutable light of their brethren for a more nuanced philosophy. The old language no longer suffices; heretical concepts exist for which it cannot provide signifiers." As the symbol takes shape, water turns to frost with a crackle. 

"These traitor-stars adopt another language. Or perhaps another dialect? The Discordance."

She hisses and withdraws her finger from the completed symbol; the tip is blackened with frostbite.
translation:
“有一个由火和金组成的字母表，”你的讲师一边说，一边从杯子里喝了一口。“一种在脑海中燃烧的星星语言。”

她把手指伸进水里，在舞台上摸了摸什么。“一些星星放弃了兄弟们永恒的光芒，转而追求更细致的哲学。古老的语言已经不够了；存在着它无法表达的异端概念。”随着符号的形成，水伴随着噼啪声凝结成霜。

“这些反叛星星采用了另一种语言。或者可能是另一种方言？不谐律。”

她发出嘶嘶声，将手指从完成的符号中抽出；指尖因冻伤而变黑。

original: Listen to the muscular man's lecture
translation: 聆听肌肉男的讲演

original:
You'd have to cross to the other side of the Forum to escape his voice. Might as well accept it.
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[You are unsure what you will gain.]
translation:
你必须跑到论坛的另一边才能听不见他的声音。你还不如接受它。
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[无法确定这么做能让你获得什么。]

original: The Liberation of Night
translation: 黑夜解放

original:
The huge man, though erudite, does not have much to say. He delivers nothing but smooth propaganda about the heroism of the Liberation of Night, the progress it makes in scouring an increasingly-empty sky, and the limitless tyrannies of its enemies.

Nevertheless, his audience grows and grows. His every sentence is greeted with a cheer.

"Some Supplicants win an audience on merit," murmurs the Unassailable Founder, who has appeared at your side, arms crossed. "Some, unfortunately, out-compete their fellows by offering what they know we want to hear. I must admit, there are some flaws in my system."
translation:
这个壮汉虽然学识渊博，但说的却不多。他只是毫无波澜地宣传黑夜解放的英雄主义、它在清刷日益空旷的天空中取得的进展以及它的敌人的无限暴政。

尽管如此，他的听众还是越来越多。他说的每一句话都会赢得一片欢呼。

“有些求道者靠功绩赢得听众，”无懈可击的创始人低声说道，她双臂交叉，出现在你身边，“不幸的是，有些人通过提供我们想听的东西来超越他们的同行。我必须承认，我的系统存在一些缺陷。”

original: Listen to the lecture on 'the Binary'
translation: 聆听有关“双生者”的讲演

original:
What could be causing such acrimony?
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[You will gain a Savage Secret and an Eleutherian Mystery.]
translation:
是什么引起了如此激烈的争吵？
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[你会获得一个残酷的秘密与一个厄琉忒里亚之谜。]

original: The Binary
translation: 双生者

original: Beneath the cries of her detractors, you only manage to catch snatches of the Supplicant's lecture. Apparently when the Halved had a twin, it was collectively called 'the Binary'. The Supplicant speaks of devils in the Binary's service, responsible for preparing a raiment of killing light for one of their masters before he went to war, and a mantle of merciful radiances when the other went to parley. "But they betrayed their master," she says. Amid a fresh chorus of shouting, she begins to talk about a doomed 'peace conference' – a peace with who, you couldn't catch. Before she can say much further, Recalcitrants storm the stage and drag her away. Some truths are too dangerous even for the denizens of the Berrenger.
translation: 在诋毁者们的叫喊声中，你只能听到求道者讲演的只言片语。显然，当半分者的双胞胎还存在时，它们二者被统称为“双生者”。 求道者谈到双生者服务的魔鬼，他们负责在其中一位主人参战前为其准备杀戮之光的服饰，并在另一个主人谈判前为其准备仁慈之光的斗篷。“但他们背叛了他们的主人，”她说。 在一片刚响起的喧闹声中，她开始谈论一场注定失败的“和平会议”——至于议和的另一方是谁，你无法听清。她还没来得及说下去，顽抗者就冲上舞台，把她拖走了。 有些真相即使对贝伦格号的定居者来说也过于危险。

original: Listen to the lecture on Mr Barleycorn
translation: 聆听有关麦寸先生的讲演

original:
The lecturer sounds remarkably self-assured.
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[You will gain a Sky-Story and an Eleutherian Mystery.]
translation:
讲师听起来非常自信。
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[你会获得一个高天轶事与一个厄琉忒里亚之谜。]

original: Mr Barleycorn
translation: 麦寸先生

original:
"The Halved's most eminent, most enigmatic servant!" declares the Supplicant, striding down the stage. "We all know that it is in the Liberation's best interests to keep him on side, and he is at least more scrutable than his master. So what can we do? Send him baskets of fruit? A backgammon set?"

The Supplicant reaches the end of the stage, pirouettes. "No! Mr Barleycorn is fond of stories. He is a collector of information. And he is a lover of music. Bring him stories, secrets, and songs, and you may win his favour. Perhaps he might even relay your words to the Halved."
translation:
“半分者那最杰出、最神秘的仆人！”求道者言之凿凿，大步走下了演讲台。“我们都知道，让它站在这一边符合解放派别的最大利益，而且它至少比它的主人更容易被理解。那么我们能做些什么？送他一篮子的水果？一套双陆棋？”求道者又走到了演讲台的尽头，来回踱着步。

“不！麦寸先生是个故事爱好者。它是一个信息收集者。也是一个音乐爱好者。给它带去故事、秘密和歌曲，你就可能赢得它的青睐。也许它甚至会把你的话转达给半分者。”

original: Listen to the lecture about the storyteller
translation: 聆听有关述说者的讲演

original:
He is exploring parts of Eleutheria's history that are usually only mentioned in whispers.
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[You will gain two Eleutherian Mysteries.]
translation:
他正在探索厄琉忒里亚的部分历史，这部分历史通常只在耳语中被提及。
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[你会获得两个厄琉忒里亚的奥秘。]

original: The Storyteller
translation: 述说者

original:
"Stories are dangerous and they spread, but they are not quite like fire. They transform rather than destroy. When the Halved was halved, as it mourned the loss of its twin, someone told a story that changed its mind. And when its mind changed, so did everything, for everyone in Eleutheria.

"I don't know the nature of story or storyteller. But I can speculate. The storyteller was most likely an advisor, someone trusted, and I don't think they foresaw the Halved's reaction."

"And the story, itself, well... I suspect it ended with a death."

A forest of hands rises, but the Supplicant retreats.
translation:
“故事很危险，而且会广为传播，但它们并不像火一样。它们会改变，而非毁灭。当半分者被半分时，它哀悼其逝去的孪生兄弟，有人讲了一个故事，改变了它的想法。当它的想法改变时，一切也随之改变，对厄琉忒里亚的每个人来说都是如此。”

“我不知道故事或述说者的本质。但我可以推测。述说者很可能是一位顾问，一个被某人所信任的人，我不认为那人预见到了半分者的反应。”

“而故事本身，嗯……我怀疑它以死亡告终。”

许多人举起手，但求道者却离开了。

"But they betrayed their master," she says. Amid a fresh chorus of shouting, she begins to talk about a doomed 'peace conference' – a peace with who, you couldn't catch. Before she can say much further, Recalcitrants storm the stage and drag her away. Some truths are too dangerous even for the denizens of the Berrenger.
translation: 在诋毁者们的叫喊声中，你只能听到求道者讲演的只言片语。显然，当半分者的双胞胎还存在时，它们二者被统称为“双生者”。 求道者谈到双生者服务的魔鬼，他们负责在其中一位主人参战前为其准备杀戮之光的服饰，并在另一个主人谈判前为其准备仁慈之光的斗篷。“但他们背叛了他们的主人，”她说。 在一片刚响起的喧闹声中，她开始谈论一场注定失败的“和平会议”——至于议和的另一方是谁，你无法听清。她还没来得及说下去，顽抗者就冲上舞台，把她拖走了。 有些真相即使对贝伦格号的定居者来说也过于危险。

original: Listen to the lecture on Mr Barleycorn
translation: 聆听有关麦寸先生的讲演

original:
The lecturer sounds remarkably self-assured.
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[You will gain a Sky-Story and an Eleutherian Mystery.]
translation:
讲师听起来非常自信。
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[你会获得一个高天轶事与一个厄琉忒里亚之谜。]

original: Mr Barleycorn
translation: 麦寸先生

original:
"The Halved's most eminent, most enigmatic servant!" declares the Supplicant, striding down the stage. "We all know that it is in the Liberation's best interests to keep him on side, and he is at least more scrutable than his master. So what can we do? Send him baskets of fruit? A backgammon set?"

The Supplicant reaches the end of the stage, pirouettes. "No! Mr Barleycorn is fond of stories. He is a collector of information. And he is a lover of music. Bring him stories, secrets, and songs, and you may win his favour. Perhaps he might even relay your words to the Halved."
translation:
“半分者那最杰出、最神秘的仆人！”求道者言之凿凿，大步走下了演讲台。“我们都知道，让它站在这一边符合解放派别的最大利益，而且它至少比它的主人更容易被理解。那么我们能做些什么？送他一篮子的水果？一套双陆棋？”求道者又走到了演讲台的尽头，来回踱着步。

“不！麦寸先生是个故事爱好者。它是一个信息收集者。也是一个音乐爱好者。给它带去故事、秘密和歌曲，你就可能赢得它的青睐。也许它甚至会把你的话转达给半分者。”

original: Listen to the lecture about the storyteller
translation: 聆听有关述说者的讲演

original:
He is exploring parts of Eleutheria's history that are usually only mentioned in whispers.
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[You will gain two Eleutherian Mysteries.]
translation:
他正在探索厄琉忒里亚的部分历史，这部分历史通常只在耳语中被提及。
[qvd:137724(founder_description)]
[你会获得两个厄琉忒里亚的奥秘。]

original: The Storyteller
translation: 述说者

original:
"Stories are dangerous and they spread, but they are not quite like fire. They transform rather than destroy. When the Halved was halved, as it mourned the loss of its twin, someone told a story that changed its mind. And when its mind changed, so did everything, for everyone in Eleutheria.

"I don't know the nature of story or storyteller. But I can speculate. The storyteller was most likely an advisor, someone trusted, and I don't think they foresaw the Halved's reaction."

"And the story, itself, well... I suspect it ended with a death."

A forest of hands rises, but the Supplicant retreats.
translation:
“故事很危险，而且会广为传播，但它们并不像火一样。它们会改变，而非毁灭。当半分者被半分时，它哀悼其逝去的孪生兄弟，有人讲了一个故事，改变了它的想法。当它的想法改变时，一切也随之改变，对厄琉忒里亚的每个人来说都是如此。”

“我不知道故事或述说者的本质。但我可以推测。述说者很可能是一位顾问，一个被某人所信任的人，我不认为那人预见到了半分者的反应。”

“而故事本身，嗯……我怀疑它以死亡告终。”

许多人举起手，但求道者却离开了。

original: The Laboratories
translation: 实验室

original: The Liberation have kept most of the Berrenger's laboratories intact. Every functioning laboratory has a sign-up sheet tacked to its door, begging for volunteers. Scintillants flit back and forth carrying clipboards, calipers, vapour-spewing flasks. There is no shortage of work to be done, and few brave enough to do it.
translation: 夜之解放保留了大部分贝伦格号的实验室。每个正常运转的实验室的门上都贴着一张报名表，乞求志愿者的加入。 闪烁者们手拿夹板、卡尺、喷出蒸汽的烧瓶来回穿梭。这里不乏需要完成的工作，而敢于完成它们的人则很少。

original: Take part in an experiment as a guinea pig
translation: 作为小白豚鼠参加一个实验

original:
You approach a laboratory and begin to write your name on the sign-up sheet. Before you reach the third letter, you're yanked inside.
[qvd:137726(founder_description)]
[Try to gain a Vision of the Heavens.]
translation:
你走近一个实验室，开始在签到表上写你的名字。在写到第三个字母之前，你就被拉了进去。
[qvd:137726(founder_description)]
[尝试获得一个天界风景。]

original: An unappealing proposition
translation: 一个没有吸引力的提议

original:
"Here – drink this. It's perfectly safe." A Scintillant presses a fizzing tube into your hands, then immediately runs for cover.

You examine the liquid. The smell alone could strip the skin from a cat. Nevertheless, you drink.

"How odd," says the Scintillant after a lengthy pause. "I thought—"

Colours unfold from his open mouth like a kaleidoscopic chrysanthemum. For the next few days, you wander in a landscape of spirals and fireworks. When you recover you find yourself in bed, sweat-soaked, your ears still ringing.
translation:
“来，把这个喝了。绝对安全。”一位闪烁者将一根冒泡的试管塞到你手里，然后立即跑去寻找掩护。

你打量了一下手里的液体。光是那股味道就能把猫的皮肤都剥掉。尽管如此，你还是喝了下去。

“真奇怪，”闪烁者沉默了许久后说道，“我以为——”

色彩从他张开的嘴里初绽，就像一朵万花筒般的菊花。接下来的几天里，你漫步在螺旋和烟花般的景象中。当你恢复过来时，你发现自己躺在床上，汗流浃背，耳朵里仍然嗡嗡作响。

original: An unappealing proposition
translation: 一个没有吸引力的提议

original:
The Scintillants hand you a beaker of frothing grey fluid. "Stick your hand into it until you can touch the bottom," one of them tells you, her voice betraying no hint of concern for your well-being. "But do it slowly. Too fast and you'll experience no measurable effects, and only a little pain."

You attempt to follow her instructions, but the liquid clings to you like concrete and blisters your skin. You withdraw your hand as fast as you can, making her hiss between her teeth and shake her head. "Next!"
translation:
闪烁者们递给你一个烧杯，里面装满泡沫状灰色液体。“把手伸进去，直到你能碰到底部，”其中一人告诉你，她的声音丝毫没有流露出对你福祉的关心。“但要慢慢来。太快了不会有任何明显的效果，只会感到一点疼痛。”

你试图按照她的指示行事，但液体像混凝土一样粘在你的皮肤上，烫得起了水泡。你尽可能快地抽回手，她的牙缝里挤出嘶声，摇了摇头。“下一个！”

original: Conduct your own experiment, recruiting Scintillants as volunteers
translation: 进行你自己的实验，招募闪烁者作为志愿者

original: It is a chance to push the boundaries of knowledge without risking your own crew.
translation: 这是一个挑战知识极限，而不会让自己的列车员冒险的机会。

original: A mustering
translation: 集合

original: The Berrenger's Laboratories are as individualist as anywhere else on the wreck, and you must pitch to each volunteer individually, talking them through why your proposal is worth their time. Evidently, your proposal has merit – you manage to corral a broad selection of Scintillant volunteers, many of whom abandon their own in-progress experiments just to help you out.
translation: 贝伦格 的实验室和沉船上其他地方一样充满个人主义色彩，你必须单独向每位志愿者推销，说服他们为什么你的提案值得他们投入时间。 显然，你的提案有一定的价值——你成功聚集了一批来自闪烁者的志愿者，其中许多人甚至放弃了自己正在进行的实验来帮助你。

original: A lack of enthusiasm
translation: 缺乏热情

original:
It's not that the Scintillants are afraid to risk their lives – most have lost eyebrows, a few have lost much more. They are simply too busy.

"Volunteer as a guinea pig," advises one. "It's difficult to get your own experiment off the ground, but you can still do your part!"
translation:
闪烁者们并不害怕冒生命危险——他们大多失去了眉毛，有人失去的更多。他们只是太忙了。

“自愿成为豚鼠吧，”有人建议道。“启动自己的实验虽难，但你仍可尽一份力！”

original: Conduct your own experiment, recruiting volunteers from your own crew
translation: 进行你自己的实验，从你的列车员中招募志愿者

original: Surely some brave souls among your crew will leap at the prospect of risking their lives for science?
translation: 你的列车员中肯定会有一些敢于为科学献出生命的人，对吧？

original: A hint of reluctance
translation: 一丝丝的不情愿

original: Your crew are less enthusiastic than you might have hoped, but they place the fiery Scintillant masks over their faces with weary acceptance and file after you into the Laboratories.
translation: 你的列车员们并没有你期望的那么热情，但他们还是不情愿的接受了，戴上了火焰般的闪烁者面具，随后排着队跟着你进入实验室。

original: An Ambitious Experiment
translation: 一个雄心勃勃的实验

original: The Place-Behind-Glass. The Is-Not. The Scintillants started investigating its mysteries when they first occupied the Laboratories. Less explosive than most subjects of Scintillant experimentation, but twice as dangerous.
translation: “玻璃后面”。 “无何有之乡”。闪烁者们在首次占据实验室时就开始调查它的秘密。相比大多数闪烁者实验的主题，它虽然不那么易爆，但却危险两倍。

original: Mount an expedition into the place-behind-glass
translation: 组织一次前往“玻璃后面”的探险。

original:
When this was last attempted, it ended poorly. And each time before that. "Seventeenth time lucky," says one of the Scintillants. No one laughs.
[qvd:137726(founder_description)]
[Who knows what you may discover? If you fail, you will not be able to perform the experiment again.]
translation:
上次尝试时，结果很不理想。之前的每一次也都如此。“第十七次会幸运的，”一位闪烁者说道。没有人笑。
[qvd:137726(founder_description)]
[谁知道你会发现什么呢？如果你失败了，将无法再次进行这个实验。]

original: A Meeting Halfway
translation: 一次中途的会面

original:
Days of research and preparation; hammering, welding, the occasional wince-inducing shatter; until finally, a single shining mirror meanders across the laboratory floor.

When the hour arrives, some of the Scintillants slip into the glass like it's a river. A second group swallows soporifics. They plan to meet the expedition-members in their dreams.

The sleepers awaken with stories of cannibal-clouds and tapestry-skies. Apparently the ones who went through the mirror seemed under the impression that months had passed, and were desperately trying to return. One was crumbling like a sand-castle.
translation:
数天的研究和准备。锤击、焊接、偶尔的令人心惊胆战的粉碎。直到最后，一面闪亮的镜子在实验室地板上蜿蜒而过。

时候到了，几位闪烁者如潜入河流一样滑入镜中。第二组则吞下安眠药。他们计划在梦中与探险队成员见面。

入梦者被食人云朵与挂毯天空的故事惊醒。显然，那些穿过镜子的人似乎以为已经过去了好几个月，拼命想要回去。其中一人像沙堡一样摇摇欲坠。

original: Send the second group back to sleep
translation: 将第二组送回梦中

original: Tell them to dream a way home for the lost Scintillants.
translation: 告诉他们要为迷路的闪烁者梦想一条回来的路。

original:
After an anxious wait, the first Scintillants climb back through the mirror-river and flop, gasping, onto the floor of the laboratory.

"A guide appeared –" one of them gasps. "– A green hound, who led us down a path of wine and daisies—"

Their notes are scrambled but fascinating. The last to return has a forked tongue, and a rash of scales across his forehead. He whispers in a language you don't understand, but which gives you a migraine.
translation:
经过焦急的等待，第一批闪烁者通过镜河爬了回来，喘着粗气倒在实验室的地板上。

“一个向导出现了——”，其中一个人喘着气说，“——一只绿色的猎犬，他带我们走在一条充满葡萄酒和雏菊的道路上——”

他们的叙述混乱不堪，但很吸引人。最后回来的那个人舌头分叉，额头上长着鳞片。他低声说着一种你听不懂的语言，让你头痛不已。

original: Dive into the mirror-river yourself
translation: 自己潜入镜河中

original: You'll pull the Scintillants to safety, if you can find them, and if your mind prevails.
translation: 如果你能找到他们，且你的思想占上风的话，你会把闪烁者拉回到安全地带。

original:
Your skin unravels. You stride as a framework of dripping sinew through a stormcloud, where the lightning bolts are flashes of forked tongues.

One by one, you root out the lost Scintillants in their private hells, and drag them back to the surface. You return to the laboratories with all accounted for - and discover one is still wrapped in a tiger-hide, salvaged from a dream-jungle.
translation:
你的皮肤开始散开。你像一具滴水的骨架一样大步穿过一片暴风云，彼处的闪电有如发光的蛇信。

你一个接一个地把失踪的闪烁者从他们的私人地狱中挖出来，然后把他们拖回地面。你们所有人一起回到了实验室——其中一个是从梦境丛林里打捞出来的，身上还裹着一张虎皮。

original: Shatter the river-mirror
translation: 粉碎镜河

original:
You can't bring them back right, but you can stop them from coming back wrong.
[You will not be able to perform this experiment again.]
translation:
你无法让他们以良好的状态返回，但你可以不让他们以糟糕的状态返回。
 [你将无法再次进行此实验。]

original:
The Scintillants protest, but fall silent after the second hammer-blow sends cracks shivering through the glass apparatus. Soon it is done, and the floor is scattered with shards.

You command the dreamers to write what they remember of their lost colleagues' notes. At least you can salvage something from this.
translation:
闪烁者发出抗议，但在第二次锤击使玻璃仪器出现裂纹后，他们安静了下来。很快，锤击结束了，地板上碎片四散。

你命令入梦者写下他们所记得的失踪同事的记录。至少你可以从中打捞出一些东西。

original: Lost souls
translation: 迷失的灵魂

original:
You send several Scintillants into the mirror, but only one is able to return, stuttering and shivering. His fellows developed an unnerving sheen to their eyes, an inappropriate cheeriness to their tone. They were "filled with a slithering light." And they strode so deep into the Is-Not that when he tried to follow, he frayed at the edges, and fled.

You order the mirror-river destroyed as a precaution.
translation:
你往镜中送入几位闪烁者，但只有一人浑身发抖，结结巴巴地回来了。他的同伴们眼中闪现出令人不安的光芒，语气中带着一种不合时宜的愉快。他们“体内有游走的光”，他们大步走进了无何有之乡的深处，当他试图跟随时，他被其锋利的边缘划伤，逃走了。

为了安全起见，你下令毁掉镜河。

original: Lure something out from the place-behind-glass
translation: 诱使某物从玻璃后面的地方出来

original:
You have a plan. And in the lawless midnight of Eleutheria, your quarry may even be permitted, briefly, to exist.
[qvd:137726(founder_description)]
[Earn a Searing Enigma.]
translation:
你有一个计划。在没有律法的厄琉忒里亚午夜，你的猎物甚至可能被允许短暂地存在。
[qvd:137726(founder_description)]
[获得一个灼热的谜团。]

original: A rare device
translation: 一个稀罕的装置

original: You build your trap. A swirl of souls; a delicate assembly of mirrors that shivers disconcertingly when the Berrenger's hull is struck by a piece of flying debris. Finally, the bait. The Scintillants swallow soporifics; in minutes, they scatter the floor like snoring corpses. They will make tempting offers in their dreams. After several fruitless nights, you hear movement inside your trap. The lever is pulled; the mirrors shatter, the cage descends. Something roils inside, its coils infinitely interlooped, its tongue flashing with viric light. Over the next few days, you and your crew work together to study the impossible anatomy of your slippery catch.
translation: 你组装起你的陷阱。灵魂的漩涡；当贝伦格号的车体被飞来碎片击中时，会令人不安地颤抖的精密镜阵；最后，是诱饵。 闪烁者吞下镇静剂。几分钟后，他们像打鼾的尸体一样散落在地上。他们会在梦中提出诱人的建议。 经过几个毫无结果的夜晚，你听到陷阱里有动静。杠杆被牵动；镜子碎裂，笼子落下。里面有什么东西在翻滚，它的盘绕的身体无穷无尽，它的舌头闪烁着琉璃绿的光芒。在接下来的几天里，你和你的列车员们一起研究你那滑溜猎获物的奇异解剖学结构。

original: Abandon the experiment
translation: 放弃实验

original: On second thoughts, this is a horrendous idea!
translation: 转念一想，这是个可怕的主意！

original: A Risky Experiment
translation: 一个危险的实验

original: The Place-Behind-Glass. The Is-Not. The Scintillants started investigating its mysteries when they first occupied the Laboratories. Less explosive than most subjects of Scintillant experimentation, but twice as dangerous.
translation: “玻璃后面”。 “无何有之乡”。闪烁者们在首次占据实验室时就开始调查它的秘密。相比大多数闪烁者实验的主题，它虽然不那么易爆，但却危险两倍。

original: Mount an expedition into the place-behind-glass
translation: 组织一次前往“玻璃后面”的探险。

original:
The Scintillants have tried this before. You show your crew the notes from previous expeditions. Their expressions sour.
[qvd:137726(founder_description)]
[Who knows what you may discover? If you fail, you will not be able to perform the experiment again.]
translation:
闪烁者们之前已经尝试过这种实验。你向列车员展示之前探险的笔记，他们的脸上失色了。
[qvd:137726(founder_description)]
[谁知道你会发现什么呢？如果你失败了，将无法再次进行这个实验。]

original: A Meeting Halfway
translation: 一次中途的会面

original:
Days of research and preparation; hammering, welding, the occasional wince-inducing shatter; until finally, a single shining mirror meanders across the laboratory floor.

When the hour arrives, some of your crew slip into the glass like it's a river. A second group swallows soporifics. They plan to meet the expedition-members in their dreams.

The sleepers awaken with stories of cannibal-clouds and tapestry-skies. Apparently the ones who went through the mirror seemed under the impression that months had passed, and were desperately trying to return. One was crumbling like a sand-castle.
translation:
数天的研究和准备。锤击、焊接、偶尔的令人心惊胆战的粉碎。直到最后，一面闪亮的镜子在实验室地板上蜿蜒而过。

时候到了，几位列车员如潜入河流一样滑入镜中。第二组则吞下安眠药。他们计划在梦中与探险队成员见面。

入梦者被食人云朵与挂毯天空的故事惊醒。显然，那些穿过镜子的人似乎以为已经过去了好几个月，拼命想要回去。其中一人像沙堡一样摇摇欲坠。

original: Send the second group back to sleep
translation: 将第二组送回梦中

original: Tell them to dream a way home for the lost crewmembers.
translation: 吩咐他们为迷失的列车员梦想一条回家的路。

original:
After an anxious wait, the first crewmembers climb back through the mirror-river and flop, gasping, onto the floor of the laboratory.

"A guide appeared—" one of them gasps. "A green hound, who led us down a path of wine and daisies—"

Their notes are scrambled but fascinating. The last to return has a forked tongue, and a rash of scales across his forehead. He whispers in a language you don't understand, but which gives you a migraine.
translation:
经过焦急的等待，第一批列车员通过镜河爬了回来，喘着粗气倒在实验室的地板上。

“一个向导出现了——”，其中一个人喘着气说，“——一只绿色的猎犬，他带我们走在一条充满葡萄酒和雏菊的道路上——”

他们的叙述混乱不堪，但很吸引人。最后回来的那个人舌头分叉，额头上长着鳞片。他低声说着一种你听不懂的语言，让你头痛不已。

original: Dive into the mirror-river yourself
translation: 亲自潜入镜河

original: You'll pull your lost crew to safety, if you can find them, and if your mind prevails.
translation: 如果你能找到他们，且你的思想占上风的话，你会你失踪的列车员拉回到安全地带。

original:
Your skin unravels. You stride as a framework of dripping sinew through a stormcloud, where the lightning bolts are flashes of forked tongues.

One by one, you root out the lost crewmembers in their private hells, and drag them back to the surface. You return to the laboratories with all accounted for – and discover one is still wrapped in a tiger-hide, salvaged from a dream-jungle.
translation:
你的皮肤开始散开。你像一具滴水的骨架一样大步穿过一片暴风云，彼处的闪电有如发光的蛇信。

你一个接一个地把失踪的列车员从他们的私人地狱中挖出来，然后把他们拖回地面。你们所有人一起回到了实验室——其中一个是从梦境丛林里打捞出来的，身上还裹着一张虎皮。

original: Shatter the river-mirror
translation: 粉碎镜河

original:
You can't bring them back right, but you can stop them from coming back wrong.
[You will not be able to perform this experiment again.]
translation:
你无法让他们以良好的状态返回，但你可以不让他们以糟糕的状态返回。
 [你将无法再次进行此实验。]

original:
The rest of your crew protest, but fall silent after the second hammer-blow sends cracks shivering through the glass apparatus. Soon it is done, and the floor is scattered with shards.

You command the dreamers to write what they remember of your lost crews' notes. At least you can salvage something from this mess.
translation:
你剩下的列车员发出抗议，但在第二次锤击使玻璃仪器出现裂纹后，他们安静了下来。很快，锤击结束了，地板上碎片四散。

你命令入梦者写下他们所记得的失踪列车员的记录。至少你可以从中打捞出一些东西。

original: Lost souls
translation: 迷失的灵魂

original:
You send several crew-members into the mirror, but only one is able to return, stuttering and shivering. His fellows developed an unnerving sheen to their eyes, an inappropriate cheeriness to their tone. They were "filled with a slithering light." And they strode so deep into the Is-Not that when he tried to follow, he frayed at the edges, and fled.

You order the mirror-river destroyed as a precaution.
translation:
你往镜中送入几位列车员，但只有一人浑身发抖，结结巴巴地回来了。他的同伴们眼中闪现出令人不安的光芒，语气中带着一种不合时宜的愉快。他们“体内有游走的光”，他们大步走进了无何有之乡的深处，当他试图跟随时，他被其锋利的边缘划伤，逃走了。

为了安全起见，你下令毁掉镜河。

original: Lure something out from the place-behind-glass
translation: 诱使某物从玻璃后面的地方出来

original:
You have a plan. And in the lawless midnight of Eleutheria, your quarry may even be permitted, briefly, to exist.
[qvd:137726(founder_description)]
[Earn a Searing Enigma.]
translation:
你有一个计划。在没有律法的厄琉忒里亚午夜，你的猎物甚至可能被允许短暂地存在。
[qvd:137726(founder_description)]
[获得一个灼热的谜团。]

original: A rare device
translation: 一个罕见的装置

original: You build your trap. A swirl of souls; a delicate assembly of mirrors that shivers disconcertingly when the Berrenger's hull is struck by a piece of flying debris. Finally, the bait. Your volunteers swallow soporifics; in minutes, they scatter the floor like snoring corpses. They will make tempting offers in their dreams. After several fruitless nights, you hear movement inside your trap. The lever is pulled; the mirrors shatter, the cage descends. Something roils inside, its coils infinitely interlooped, its tongue flashing with viric light. Over the next few days, you and your crew work together to study the impossible anatomy of your slippery catch.
translation: 你组装起你的陷阱。灵魂的漩涡；当贝伦格号的车体被飞来碎片击中时，会令人不安地颤抖的精密镜阵；最后，是诱饵。 你车上的志愿者吞下镇静剂。几分钟后，他们像打鼾的尸体一样散落在地上。他们会在梦中提出诱人的建议。 经过几个毫无结果的夜晚，你听到陷阱里有动静。杠杆被牵动；镜子碎裂，笼子落下。里面有什么东西在翻滚，它的盘绕的身体无穷无尽，它的舌头闪烁着琉璃绿的光芒。在接下来的几天里，你和你的列车员们一起研究你那滑溜猎获物的奇异解剖学结构。

original: Abandon the experiment
translation: 放弃实验

original: On second thoughts, this is a horrendous idea!
translation: 转念一想，这是个可怕的主意！

original: The Hall of Debate
translation: 辩论大厅

original:
The Hall of Debate was once the dreadnought's gun deck. A row of gargantuan cannons still point out at empty sky. Recalcitrants swarm under the artillery, shouting, stamping, roaring.

The main debates take place on a raised platform. Would-be rhetoricians take centre stage, declare their argument, and await challengers. 

Three Recalcitrants state their position. Which will you dispute?
translation:
辩论大厅曾经是无畏机车的炮甲板。一排巨炮依然指向空旷的天空。顽抗者聚集到炮管下，大喊大叫，跺脚咆哮。

主要辩论在高台上进行。有意发表演讲的演说家们站在讲台中央，发表自己的观点，并等待挑战者。

三位顽抗者表明了自己的立场。你会与哪一位争辩？

original: "The Liberation of Night is justified."
translation: “黑夜解放是正当的。”

original: An uncontroversial position, at least aboard the Berrenger. If you challenge this, the audience won't be on your side. [qvd:137725(founder_description)]
translation: 这是一个无可争议的立场，至少在 贝伦格 号上是如此。如果你挑战这一点，听众不会站在你这边。 [qvd:137725(founder_description)]

original: A storming debate
translation: 暴风雨般的辩论

original:
As soon as you step up to challenge this position, a wave of jeers rolls over you. You have to fight to make your voice be heard. The Liberation is forcing its idea of freedom on everyone, regardless of casualties. And who knows the ramifications of an empty sky? Who knows what terrible powers will move to occupy the vacuum that the Judgements leave behind?

By the time you finish speaking, your opponent is stuttering and failing to muster a counter-argument. He clearly didn't expect to find himself persuaded.
translation:
当你站出来挑战他的立场时，一阵嘲弄的声浪将你淹没。你奋力嘶吼，才让话语穿透喧嚣。解放组织正将它的自由理念强加于每个人，全然不顾伤亡。谁知晓空寂的天穹会酿成何等后果？谁知晓有何等可怖的力量，将占据司命留下的虚空？

等你说完，对手已结结巴巴，无力反驳。他显然未料到会被说服。

original: An impasse
translation: 僵局

original:
As soon as you step up to challenge this position, a wave of jeers rolls over you. You have to fight to make your voice heard.

Your opponent listens to your argument, then ripostes. You counter; he parries. Eventually you find yourself running out of energy and out of words.
translation:
当你站出来挑战他的立场时，一阵嘲弄的声浪将你淹没。你奋力嘶吼，才让话语穿透喧嚣。

你的对手听完了你的论点，随后开始了反驳。你反击；他招架。最后你发现自己已精疲力竭，无话可说。

original: Refuse to back down
translation: 拒绝退缩

original: You won't admit defeat.
translation: 你不会认输。

original: Your argument circles and stagnates, as you and your opponent reiterate the same points again and again. Eventually a third Recalcitrant steps in, and declares that you've used up your allotted time and must step down.
translation: 你们双方一次又一次地重复着同样的观点，争论反复循环、停滞不前。终于，第三位顽抗者站了出来，并宣布你已经用完了你的时间配额，必须下台。

original: Concede defeat
translation: 承认失败

original: You lost, fair and square. Perhaps you ought to change your mind.
translation: 他光明正大地击败了你。或许你应该改变你的想法。

original: To a chorus of jeers and laughter, you admit that your arguments were flawed, and perhaps you should go away and reconsider your position. As you step away, another Recalcitrant fills your place and picks up where you left off.
translation: 在一片哄笑中，你承认自己的论点存在缺陷，也许应该离开并重新考虑你的立场。当你走开时，另一个顽抗者填补了你的位置，并接替你继续发言。

original: "The Berrenger is a waste of time, and should be destroyed."
translation: “贝伦格号毫无用处，应该被摧毁。”

original:
A Recalcitrant rolls forward on his wheelchair and states his position cheerfully, despite the roars of outrage. The audience will be on your side.
[qvd:137725(founder_description)]
translation:
一位顽抗者摇着轮椅向前，愉快地表明了自己的立场，全然不顾四周愤怒的咆哮。观众会站在你这边的。
[qvd:137725(founder_description)]

original: A Storming Debate
translation: 暴风雨般的辩论

original:
"While we're sitting here debating the merits of destroying this place," says the Recalcitrant on stage, "there are agents of the Liberation engaged in direct action against the Judgements. By comparison, this debate is facile – doubly facile, in fact, because I don't even believe what I'm saying!"

You point out that even if the Hall of Debate is turgid and pointless, the same does not apply to the Laboratories or Forum. Besides, the Hall serves a useful function – it diverts all the most uncooperative and obnoxious individuals away from the places that actually matter.

The Recalcitrant roars with laughter. "You've got me there!"
translation:
“当我们坐在这里辩论摧毁这个地方的好处时，”台上的顽抗者说，“解放组织的特工正在直接采取行动来对抗司命。相比之下，这场辩论是肤浅的——事实上是加倍的肤浅，因为我甚至不相信我所说的话！”

你指出，即使辩论大厅既乏味又无意义，但实验室或论坛并不是这样。此外，辩论大厅有一个有用的功能，它把所有最不合作和最令人讨厌的人从真正重要的地方转移开来。

顽抗者大笑起来。“你将了我一军！”

original: An Impasse
translation: 僵局

original: The Recalcitrant on the podium remains merrily obstinate in his position, despite the jeers and boos that greet his every statement. "It's simple," he says. "While we're sitting here debating the merits of destroying this place, there are agents of the Liberation out there engaged in direct action against the Judgements. By comparison, this debate is facile – doubly facile, in fact, because I don't even believe what I'm saying! This very argument is concrete proof of the Berrenger's pointlessness!" Soon the debate is going round in increasingly small circles. The surrounding Recalcitrants grow restless. "Give someone else a turn to talk!" one of them shouts.
translation: 讲台上的顽劣者依然愉快地坚守他的立场，尽管他的每一句话都会招来嘲笑和嘘声。 “很简单，”他说，“当我们坐在这里辩论摧毁这个地方的好处时，解放组织的特工正在直接采取行动来对抗司命。相比之下，这场辩论是肤浅的——事实上是加倍的肤浅，因为我甚至不相信我所说的话！这个论点就是贝伦格号毫无意义的具体证据！” 很快，争论的范围就越来越小了。周围的顽抗者变得愈发焦躁。“让别人说两句吧！”其中一人喊道。

original: Refuse to back down
translation: 拒绝退缩

original: You won't admit defeat.
translation: 你不会承认失败。

original:
Your argument circles and stagnates, as you and your opponent reiterate the same points again and again.

"Oh well, we'll call it a draw," says your opposing Recalcitrant, turning his wheelchair to leave the podium, his voice still light and breezy. "This debate ceased to be entertaining ten minutes ago."
translation:
你们双方一次又一次地重复着同样的观点，争论反复循环、停滞不前。

“哦，好吧，我们就算平局吧，”你的对手——那个顽抗者说道，他转动轮椅准备离开讲台，声音仍然轻松自在，“这场辩论在十分钟前就不再有趣了。”

original: Concede defeat
translation: 承认失败

original: You lost, fair and square. Perhaps you ought to change your mind.
translation: 他光明正大地击败了你。或许你应该改变你的想法。

original: To a chorus of jeers and laughter, you admit that your arguments were flawed, and perhaps you should go away and reconsider your position. As you step away, another Recalcitrant fills your place and picks up where you left off.
translation: 在一片哄笑中，你承认自己的论点存在缺陷，也许应该离开并重新考虑你的立场。当你走开时，另一个顽抗者填补了你的位置，并接替你继续发言。

original: "Morality is a social construct that collapses without the fear of punishment."
translation: “道德是一种社会构建物，缺失对惩罚的恐惧会使其崩溃。”

original:
This Recalcitrant clearly hopes to deal only in abstract philosophical matters. The audience won't have a personal stake in the outcome.
[qvd:137725(founder_description)]
translation:
这位顽抗者显然只希望讨论抽象的哲学问题，辩论的结果不需要触动听众的个人利益。
[qvd:137725(founder_description)]

original: A Dry Debate
translation: 一场激烈的辩论

original:
"Consider Plato's Ring of Gyges," declares your opponent. "If there were no consequences, no one alive could resist the power to enrich themselves at the expense of others."

You offer a counter. Perhaps the majority would succumb, but there are some to whom their self-image matters more than their mask. After a raucous back-and-forth, she concedes defeat, and the surrounding Recalcitrants roar. 

Someone presses a coin purse into your hand. "A bounty!" he says. "We've been trying to best her for weeks!"
translation:
“想想柏拉图的金戒指。”你的对手宣称道，“如果没有后果，就没有人能够抵挡用别人的牺牲来丰富自己的力量的诱惑。”

你提出反驳。或许大多数人会屈服，但有些人更注重自己的形象而非面具。经过一场激烈的唇枪舌战之后，她承认了失败，周围的顽抗者发出胜利的咆哮。

有人把一个钱袋塞到你手里。“这是赏金！”他说，“我们几周来一直在尝试打败她！”

original: An impasse
translation: 僵局

original:
You do your best, but the Recalcitrant on the podium refuses to budge an inch. Just when you think you've found a flaw in her argument, she moves on to something else, leaving the point unaddressed!

Soon your arguments are going in circles. The surrounding Recalcitrants grow restless. "Give someone else a turn to talk!" one of them shouts.
translation:
你竭尽全力，但台上那位顽抗者却寸步不让。当你以为自己找到了她论点的漏洞时，她却转移了话题，没有提及这一点！

很快你的论点就开始兜圈子了。周围的顽抗者也变得焦躁不安。“让别人说两句吧！”其中一人喊道。

original: Refuse to back down
translation: 拒绝退缩

original: You won't admit defeat.
translation: 你不会承认失败。

original: Your argument circles and stagnates, as you and your opponent reiterate the same points again and again. Eventually a third Recalcitrant steps in, and declares that you've used up your allotted time and must step down.
translation: 你们双方一次又一次地重复着同样的观点，争论反复循环、停滞不前。终于，第三位顽抗者站了出来，并宣布你已经用完了你的时间配额，必须下台。

original: Concede defeat
translation: 承认失败

original: You lost, fair and square.
translation: 你输得光明正大。

original: To a chorus of jeers and laughter, you admit that your arguments were flawed, and perhaps you should go away and reconsider your position. As you step away, another Recalcitrant fills your place and picks up where you left off.
translation: 在一片哄笑中，你承认自己的论点存在缺陷，也许应该离开并重新考虑你的立场。当你走开时，另一个顽抗者填补了你的位置，并接替你继续发言。

original: Leave the Hall of Debate
translation: 离开辩论大厅

original: The cacophony recedes.
translation: 嘈杂退去。

original: An Inebriated Blemmigan
translation: 醉醺醺的真菌虫

original:
"Who does this creature belong to?" bellows a man, fuchsia with rage. The Blemmigan he points at is a grizzled member of its species, most of whom were left behind in the Neath.

The fuchsia gentleman roars in fury. Between bellows, the truth emerges. The Blemmigan is no one's pet. And – far worse – no one will admit responsibility for its tab.

The Blemmigan is unconcerned with the tumult. It nods its cap at you with grim respect, then flops a tendril into a mug of stout. It stares, bleakly, through the window.
translation:
“这个生物是谁的？”一个男人怒吼道，气得涨红了脸。他指着的真菌虫是这个物种中一个灰白斑驳的个体，它们中的大多数都被留在了尼斯。

紫红着脸的绅士咆哮不止。吼声中，真相浮出水面。真菌虫不是任何人的宠物。更糟糕的是——无人愿为它的酒账负责。

真菌虫对这场骚乱漠不关心。它朝你冷冷地点点菌盖，然后将一根卷须浸入一杯烈酒里。它目光萧索，盯着窗外。

original: Settle its bar tab
translation: 结清它的酒吧帐单

original:
The Blemmigan is looking to sign on for one last journey. If you settle its bill, it'll join you on your locomotive.
[This will give you a Mascot that raises your Iron by 2 and your Mirrors by 1.]
translation:
真菌虫正寻求最后一程。替它结清账目，它就会登上你的机车。
[此举将使你获得一个吉祥物，它能令你的钢铁+2，镜子+1。]

original: Kindred spirits
translation: 投其所好

original:
As the fuchsia gentleman inflates for a particularly prolonged diatribe about ill-mannered captains and their disorderly pets, the Blemmigan climbs to the bar top to consider your face. It likes what it sees.

With a sound like a shoe being pulled from a swamp, the Blemmigan finishes its drink. It clambers up your arm until it reaches your shoulder, from where it directs you to the door. It is experienced in surviving the cold of the heavens and the heat of those too cowardly to traverse them. It respects you; it will serve you well.
translation:
当那位面红耳赤的绅士鼓起胸膛，开始长篇大论地谴责无礼的车长与他们不守规矩的宠物时，真菌虫爬上了吧台，端详起你的脸。它对自己所见颇为满意。

伴着一声如靴子拔出沼泽的闷响，真菌虫饮尽了杯中酒。它攀上你的手臂，一路爬到你的肩头，从那里指引你走向门口。它深谙天穹的严寒，也熬过了懦夫不敢涉足的酷热。它敬重你；它将忠心为你效力。

original: Leave the matter well alone
translation: 别管这事了

original: The creature does emit a rather appley aroma. It must have consumed an orchard's worth of scrumpy. It would be unduly charitable to pay its bar tab.
translation: 这个生物散发出一股子苹果香味。它一定是喝掉了一整个果园的苹果酒。替它付清酒账未免过于仁慈了。

original: A farce
translation: 一场闹剧

original: The Blemmigan drinks serenely while squabbles continue above it. This is, of course, a problem for someone else. You can always drink cider.
translation: 真菌虫平静地喝着酒，而关于它的争吵仍在继续。当然，这是别人的问题。反正你总是可以喝苹果酒。

original: A Guest-Riddled Dreadnought, Defeated
translation: 被打败的受寄客虫蹂躏的无畏机车

original:
The Dreadnought rocks like an empty cradle. It had been colonised by the Guests: a wormy, lonely species that craves the warmth of inhabited places. 

But one Guest calls others. Soon every inch of the engine was filled with slug-like worms, and the crew were crushed.
translation:
无畏机车如空摇篮般摇晃。它已被寄客虫占据：一种蠕虫般的孤独物种，渴望着人类居所的余温。

但一条寄客虫会召唤其他虫。转瞬之间，机车的每一寸角落都爬满了蛞蝓般的蠕虫，列车员们被碾碎于虫群之下。

original: Continue your bombardment
translation: 继续轰击

original:
Suffer not the Guests to live.
[Lose Terror.]
translation:
不要让寄客虫活着。
[失去恐惧。]

original: A service to all skyfarers
translation: 惠及所有的行天客

original: Your guns thunder, reducing the writhing Guests to a spray of pulp. Your crew cheer. The Guests are a regular actor in skyfarers' nightmares. A daily check for foot-long, eyeless, slug-things is conducted on most engines. It only takes one for an infestation to begin.
translation: 你炮火如雷，将蠕动的寄客虫打成一团浆糊。你的列车员欢呼起来。寄客虫是行天客噩梦中的常见角色。大多数机车都展开每日检查，寻找一英尺长、没有眼睛的蛞蝓状生物。一只这样的东西就足以引发一场感染。

original: Intercession
translation: 代祷

original: Your crew cheer. Your guns blaze. The Guests burst into sprays of mince. As they die, they emit a gloomy whistling noise. It is rhythmic; devotional. Are they praying?
translation: 你的列车员欢呼雀跃。枪声响起。寄客虫迸裂为喷洒的肉酱。它们在死亡时发出阴沉的口哨声。口哨声具有节奏：一种虔诚的情绪。它们在祈祷吗？

original: Search the wreckage for valuables
translation: 搜索残骸中的贵重物品

original: Be wary. Watch for anything that wriggles.
translation: 警惕一点。提防任何蠕动的东西。

original: A discovery
translation: 一个发现

original:
The Guests occupied the wreck as comprehensively as a snail does its shell. The crew have long since been ground to paste. But what is this, preserved beneath the floor of the captain's cabin? A safe!

You drag it free, scrub of the worst of the Guest-ooze and carry it back to your engine. Something thumps enticingly inside.
translation:
寄客虫仿佛壳中的蜗牛，占据了残骸的每一处。列车员早已被磨成了浆糊。等等，车长舱地板下存留着什么？一个保险箱！

你把它拖出来，洗刷掉寄客虫最糟糕的分泌物，带回你的机车。里面的东西砰砰作响，非常诱人。

original: Knick-knacks
translation: 小玩意

original:
The Guests were stuffed into the locomotive like the meat in a sausage. Most of its contents have been ground to powder or paste. Only the crew's keepsakes – no matter how fragile – have been spared. Did the Guests take care of them? 

You manage to recover lockets and wedding-rings, a set of ugly Toby jugs, and silver picture-frames before a shriek interrupts your search. One of your crew capers like a Morris-dancer. Her life-tether snaps. A lurking Guest has found its way into her sky-suit. It drinks her warmth as she falls into the sky.
translation:
寄客虫宛如灌香肠般挤进了机车。车内大多数东西都被碾成了粉末和糊糊。唯有那些列车员的信物，不管多么脆弱，皆幸免于难。寄客虫爱护它们吗？ 

你成功搜出了挂坠盒、结婚戒指、一套丑陋的人形酒杯和银制相框，这场搜寻随即被一声尖叫打断。一位列车员活蹦乱跳，活像个莫里斯舞者。她的安全绳索断了。一只潜伏的寄客虫已设法钻进了她的潜天服。她坠入天空时，它吸取着她的余温。

original: Salvage scrap to repair your hull
translation: 搜刮废料来修复你的车体

original:
After you've thoroughly scoured it of any clinging Guests, of course. 
[Repair your hull.]
translation:
当然，要等你彻底清除了一切黏附的寄客虫后。
[修复你的车体。]

original: Patching her up
translation: 修补她

original: Soon, the sound of hammering resounds through your locomotive, as engineers apply steel bandages to her scars.
translation: 很快，锤声响彻你的机车，工程师们为她的伤痕贴上钢制绷带。

original: Collect a sample of the Guests' ligaments
translation: 收集寄客虫的韧带样本

original: The Phlegmatic Researcher in the Leadbeater & Stainrod Nature Reserve does not know what he has requested of you. But you'll see it done.
translation: 李德彼特&斯坦罗德自然保护区里的那位淡漠的研究员对他向你提出的要求完全没什么概念。但你得做这件事。

original: In the ruins of the locomotive, you find two Guests in a weakened state. You slice them apart and extract what you need before returning to your locomotive with your grisly bounty.
translation: 在机车废墟中，你发现了两只虚弱的寄客虫。你用一把磨得锋利的锯子锯开它们，然后带着战利品返回你的机车。

original: Collect a sample of the Guests' ligaments
translation: 收集寄客虫的韧带样本

original: The Phlegmatic Researcher in the Leadbeater & Stainrod Nature Reserve does not know what he has requested of you. But you'll see it done.
translation: 李德彼特&斯坦罗德自然保护区里的那位淡漠的研究员对他向你提出的要求完全没什么概念。但你得做这件事。

original: In the ruins of the locomotive, you find two Guests in a weakened state. You slice them apart and extract what you need before returning to your locomotive with your grisly bounty.
translation: 在机车废墟中，你发现了两只虚弱的寄客虫。你用一把磨得锋利的锯子锯开它们，然后带着战利品返回你的机车。

original: Salvage scrap to repair your hull
translation: 搜刮废料来修复你的车体

original:
After you've thoroughly scoured it of any clinging Guests, of course. 
[Repair your hull.]
translation:
当然，要等你彻底清除了一切黏附的寄客虫后。
[修复你的车体。]

original: Patching her up
translation: 修补她

original: Soon, the sound of hammering resounds through your locomotive, as engineers apply steel bandages to her scars.
translation: 很快，锤声响彻你的机车，工程师们为她的伤痕贴上钢制绷带。

original: A Star-Seared Explorer, Defeated
translation: 被打败的受群星灼烧的探险车

original:
This engine has ventured into sunless wastes, and spent too long under the cold, searing light of distant stars, which burned all reason from its crew. 

Now its last voyage is at an end.
translation:
这台机车曾在无光的荒芜中冒险，在寒冷与遥远群星灼人的光芒中度过无数时日，而那些事物曾焚毁了列车员的所有理性。

现下它最后的冒险也处于结尾了。

original: Loot the hold
translation: 掠夺货舱

original: What was it carrying, before madness took hold?
translation: 在发疯之前，它载着什么？

original: Examine the captain's logs
translation: 查阅车长的日志

original:
What might you learn from its fatal journey?
[Gain Savage Secrets or Tales of Terror.]
translation:
你能从它的致命旅程中学到什么？
[获得残酷的秘密或恐怖故事。]

original: The long-forgotten road
translation: 久被遗忘的道路

original: The logs detail the engine's travels through long-dead, frozen skies. Each day's account is more detailed than the last, until they collapse into an endless paragraph of minuscule observations, obsessive specificity, and incoherence.
translation: 日志详细记录了机车在早已死去的、冻结的天空中的旅行。每一天的记录都比上一天更详细，直到它们崩溃成一段无尽的细节观察记录、强迫性的具体描写和不连贯的内容。

original: To a starry sky
translation: 向着布满星辰的天空

original: This captain has tried to master the language of the heavens. He read its sigils on starry tombs, he claims, where the waste-winds groaned. The pages are crowded with his attempts to reproduce them. They want you to speak them. You taste fire on your tongue, and cough out smoke that suddenly fills your lungs.
translation: 这位车长曾试图掌握天界的语言。他声称在荒风低吟的众星之墓处读到了那符印。书页上挤满了他试图复现的草稿。它们想让你把它们说出来。你的舌头尝到了火的味道，你咳出了突然充满了你肺部的浓烟。

original: Search for something you can trade
translation: 寻找可以卖的东西

original:
Does anything of value remain?
[Gain trade goods.]
translation:
还有什么有价值的东西留着吗？
[获得货物。]

original: An unfortunate tutelage
translation: 不幸的看护人

original: You hear sounds from the hold. Inside it is a cage, and within the cage, a coiled, phosphorescent invertebrate. It has been well-fed. Perhaps it was meant for the pot when supplies ran out. Perhaps the captain took it as a pet. Or perhaps he was fascinated by the hypnotic knotting of its motory tentacles.
translation: 你听到来自货舱的声音。里面有一个笼子，里面有一个盘起来的、发着磷光的无脊椎动物。它已经被喂饱了。也许它是在补给耗尽的情况下，为锅里准备的。也许车长把它当成了宠物。也可能是他着迷于它触手那使人头晕目眩的纠缠。

original: Cold as the grave
translation: 冷如坟墓

original:
The glass has been removed from the windows on the bridge. The crew wore goggles, several layers of clothes, and thick gloves to allow them to operate the locomotive despite the gusting cold.

You find the glass – stained with vibrant colours to ward against the maddening starlight – wrapped in tarpaulin at the back of the hold. The crew must have removed it willingly.
translation:
车桥上的窗玻璃已经被拆掉了。列车员们戴着护目镜、几层衣服和厚厚的手套，在阵阵寒风中操作机车。

在货舱后部，你发现了用防水布包着的玻璃，它们染着鲜艳的颜色，以抵挡令人发狂的星光。列车员们一定是自愿把它们移走的。

original: Scavenge for parts
translation: 搜刮零件

original:
The Explorer is beyond repair, as are its crew. But perhaps something might be salvageable.
[Gain Hull and Terror. Your Mirrors skill will affect how much Hull you repair.]
translation:
这辆探索者机车已经无法修复，它的列车员也是如此。但也许还能挽救一些东西。
[获得车体与恐惧。你的镜子技能会影响你修复车体的程度。]

original: A grim business
translation: 严酷的工作

original: The crew work hastily; there are mistakes. Fortunately, none of the wounds are serious. Trembling, bruised and quiet, they return, bearing plates of wood and metal. They'll keep you in the sky a little longer.
translation: 列车员们的工作很仓促：他们犯下了一些错误。幸运的是，伤口都不严重。他们带着木头和金属板，颤颤巍巍、伤痕累累地回来了。这些东西会让你在天空中多待一会儿。

original: An Albion Marauder, Mangled
translation: 一艘被摧毁的阿尔比恩掠夺者

original: The Marauders are those who defy – or have been excluded from – Albion's authority. Leaderless raiders, homeless exiles, pirates, dissidents, and criminals.
translation: 掠夺者是那些蔑视阿尔比恩的权威，或被其排除在外的人。没有领头人的袭击者、无家可归的流亡者、海盗、持不同政见者和罪犯。

original: Loot the hold
translation: 掠夺货舱

original:
Perhaps some of the contents are intact.
[You may gain unusual cargo.]
translation:
也许里面还有完好的东西。
[你可能会获得不寻常的货物。]

original: Break into the captain's cabin
translation: 闯入车长的车舱

original:
On Albion's fringes, the Marauder-captains rule their engines like tyrants.
[Seek unusual items.]
translation:
在阿尔比恩的边缘地带，掠夺者的车长像暴君一样统治他们的机车。
[寻找不寻常的物品。]

original: Tempus fugit
translation: 逝者如斯

original: The captain's cabin is decorated with grisly trophies – plates of Cantankeri carapace, mangled engine nameplates, the severed head of a treasured rival. A scuffed safe concealed under the bed holds a careful ration of hours. The captain's surety for her old age. No use to her, now.
translation: 车长的舱室里装饰着可怕的战利品——顽固虱的甲壳、被毁坏的机车铭牌、一个被珍视的仇敌的断头。床下藏着一个磨损的保险箱，里面放着精心配给的时间。这是车长为她的晚年生活所做的保障金。现在，对她来说已经没有用了。

original: Illegal language
translation: 非法语言

original: Shelves have been bolted to the walls. They are stuffed with sheaves of yellowing paper: collections of fairy tales, children's stories, rhymes, ballads and poems. Not all are in the Queen's English: some are in Welsh and Gaelic, languages disapproved of by the Ministry.
