translation: 拒绝

original:
The hand encloses your face. A twist, a wrench, and your flesh starts to give away like malleable clay...

No. You can't. You knock the Sequestrator's hand away and push through the crowd, heading back to the surface.

Logoi follow you every step of the way back through the Catafalque, watching you with burning eyeless intensity. Your hesitancy has given yourself away – they've realised you are not actually dead. 

[You are reduced to the status of Invisible once again.]
translation:
一只手围住了你的脸，在你脸上扭了几下，然后用力地拉拽了一会。你的皮肤开始像可塑的粘土一样脱落……

不，你受不了了。你把剥面者的手甩掉，穿过拥挤的幽魂，回到地面。

你离开灵枢的每一步圣言都跟在你身后，用它那燃烧着的光亮的“眼睛”一直盯着你。你的犹豫不决已经暴露了你自己，他们已经意识到你实际上并不是死者。

[你的身份再次降至无形灵。]

original: Bargain for special treatment
translation: 通过讨价还价来获得特殊优待

original:
When you present your Testament of Roses to the Sequestrator, she agrees to be a little more gentle in removing your face.
[You will lose your face, and with it 5 Hearts. Perhaps you will be able to get it back at a later date.]
translation:
将花之证明赠送给剥面者后，她同意在摘除你的脸时更轻柔一点。
[你将失去你的脸，并同时失去5点红心。也许你可以在以后把它找回来。]

original: Faceless
translation: 无面

original:
The Sequestrator teases your face away delicately, like she's peeling a scab. Her hand retreats with something ragged clutched between its fingers. It doesn't hurt at all. A weight has been lifted.

Your new reality becomes apparent only when you touch your face, and feel nothing but an expanse of brute blank flesh. Your vision dims, as though a grey veil has closed over the world. With some effort, you are able to manifest a lipless slit of a mouth, which screams.

You have passed the Test of Substance, and your face is gone. You may move further into the Catafalque.
translation:
剥面者轻轻地把你的脸剥下，就像在剥痂一样。她的手缩了回去，手指间抓着一个粗糙的东西。一点也不疼。重担已经卸下了。

只有当你触摸自己的脸时，才能了解到你现在的样貌，除了一片单调平整的肉体，你什么也没摸到。你的视线变得模糊，仿佛一层灰色的面纱笼罩了整个世界。经过一番努力，你终于能显现出一张发出无声的尖叫的，没有嘴唇的嘴巴。

你通过了本质的检验，你的脸消失了。你可以深入灵柩。

original: The Test of Definition
translation: 定义的检验

original:
Once again, the tunnel opens up and becomes a staircase, descending into a cauldron huge as a lake. 

It brims with a whirling black fluid. Dozens of the Yoked stand stirring at the edges. An endless procession of shades march in without hesitation, and are whipped away by the current.

On a balcony above the cauldron, a vast frog-like spirit carefully oversees the entire affair. "What are you waiting for?" it croaks when you pause.
translation:
隧道再次打开，变成了一个楼梯，向下通往一个像湖泊一样巨大的大锅。

锅里充满了翻涌的黑色液体。数十个缚链灵站在河岸边搅动。无数遗魂毫不犹豫地涌入锅中，然后被水流卷走。

在大锅上方的看台上，一只巨大的青蛙样子的鬼魂仔细地监视着整个过程。当你停下脚步时，它嘶哑地说道：“你还在等什么？”

original: Step into the cauldron and try to keep yourself intact
translation: 踏入大锅，同时试着保持自我的完整

original:
You'll be relying on nothing but sheer force of will. [qvd:138078(Cauldron)]
[You will lose your name, and with it 5 Mirrors. Perhaps you will be able to get it back at a later date. The Nameless Spirit could assist here.]
translation:
你将只依靠意志力。[qvd:138078(Cauldron)]
[你将失去你的名字，并同时失去5点镜子。也许你可以在以后把它找回来。无名之灵可以在这里提供协助。]

original: Nameless
translation: 无名

original:
As you step beneath the surface, foreign memories flood you. Fleeing through long grass. The crunch of bones between your jaws. Swirling, unfamiliar skies. You are coming apart.

Spirits swirl around you, silent shapes with arms outstretched. You are buffeted by memories: sword-fights in a forest, sunken libraries, a city aflame. You cling to your name, but there are a dozen other names you can call to mind, and you no longer know which is yours.

You fight the swirling currents and emerge on the other side mostly intact. Your name is gone. The other gaps in your memory are not too severe. You think.
translation:
当你踏入锅中时，陌生的记忆涌入你的脑海。穿过长长的草丛逃跑。下颌之间骨头嘎吱作响。天空旋转的、陌生的天空。你正在分崩离析。

鬼魂在你周围旋转，无声的身影伸出的他们手臂紧抓住你。回忆冲刷着你的脑海：森林中的剑术格斗，天野上沉没的图书馆，火光冲天的城市。你紧紧抓住属于自己的名字，但十几个你能想起的其他的名字瞬间涌入你的思绪之中，你不再记得哪个是你的本名。

你与漩涡搏斗，几乎完好无损地到达了另一边。你的名字不见了。你记忆中的其他空白并不严重。至少你这么认为。

original: Failure
translation: 失败

original:
As you step beneath the surface, foreign memories flood you. You open your mouth, and the scream is not your own. 

You're coming apart at the seams. Willpower drains away. You simply cannot keep yourself together. You turn and struggle from the cauldron, splashing, thrashing, pushing spirits aside in your desperation to escape. Soaked and shivering, you dash back through the Catafalque.

Logoi pursue you relentlessly, their lashing flames leaving angry welts across your back. Your hesitancy has given yourself away – they know you are not actually dead. 

[You are reduced to the status of Invisible once again.]
translation:
当你踏入锅中时，陌生的记忆涌入你的脑海。你张开嘴，发出了不属于自己的尖叫。

你在水流中开始分崩离析，意志力被耗尽。你根本无法保持自己的状态。你转过身，从大锅里挣扎地爬出，水花四溅，惊慌失措，逃跑的过程中绝望的把鬼魂推开。浑身湿透，瑟瑟发抖。你冲回了灵柩。

圣言无情地追赶你，它们的火焰卷须在你的背上留下了愤怒的伤痕。你的犹豫不决已经暴露了你自己，他们意识到你实际上并不是死者。

[你的身份再次降至无形灵。]

original: Loudly refuse to step into the cauldron
translation: 大声拒绝踏入大锅。

original:
You don't want to lose yourself.
[This will change your Blue Kingdom status to Invisible.]
translation:
你不想失去自我。
[这将使你在蓝色王国的地位变为无形灵。]

original: Refusal
translation: 拒绝

original:
As you turn to leave, you find a log-jam of waiting spirits has clustered behind you. You push your way through, knocking them aside. One of them tumbles into the cauldron with a splash.

Logoi pursue you relentlessly, their lashing flames leaving angry welts across your back. Your hesitancy has given yourself away – they know you are not actually dead. 

[You are reduced to the status of Invisible once again.]
translation:
当你转身离开时，你发现身后已经挤满了等待的鬼魂。你推开他们，把他们撞到一边。其中一个鬼魂扑通一声掉进了大锅里。

圣言无情地追赶你，它们的火焰卷须在你的背上留下了愤怒的伤痕。你的犹豫不决已经暴露了你自己，他们意识到你实际上并不是死者。

[你的身份再次降至无形灵。]

original: Ask the Amphibian Alchemist what awaits you in the cauldron
translation: 询问两栖的炼金术士，大锅里有什么在等着你？

original: Spirits pile up behind you. The Alchemist groans in frustration.
translation: 鬼魂在你身后排着长队，炼金术士不耐烦地呻吟了一声。

original: The Amphibian Alchemist
translation: 两栖的炼金术士

original:
"You will enter the cauldron and mix with the other spirits," croaks the Alchemist. "You will taste each other's memories, know each other's innermost selves. If you are strong enough, you will emerge on the other side, stripped of irrelevancies. Your name, for instance."

And if you are not strong enough? "You will remain in the cauldron, and other spirits will absorb what they need from you. You will still reach Death's Door. They will take you with them, piece by piece."
translation:
“你将进入大锅，与其他鬼魂混合，”炼金术士用阴郁的语气回答道，“你们将品尝彼此的回忆，相互了解对方的内心世界。如果你足够强大，你将能在另一边上岸并剥离一些无关紧要的东西，比如你的名字。”

但如果你不够强大呢？“你将留在大锅里，其他遗魂将从你身上吸收他们需要的东西。你仍然会到达死亡之门。因为它们会带着你——一块一块的。”

original: Slip away without attracting the Logoi's notice
translation: 在不引起圣言注意的情况下溜走。

original: You have no desire to lose your identity, but outright refusal will draw unwelcome attention.
translation: 你并不想失去你的身份，但直接拒绝会引起多余的注意。

original: A successful evasion
translation: 一次成功的躲避

original: You step backwards, mingling among the crowd of shades. You manage to slip back to a safer part of the Catafalque.
translation: 你向后退了一步，混迹在一群遗魂中。你设法溜回灵柩的一个较安全的地方。

original: Failure
translation: 失败

original:
As you step back into the crowd, the Logoi rotate to face you. A dozen blazing sigils burn into your eyes and mind. They've noticed your reluctance, and they advance like a firestorm.

The Logoi pursue you relentlessly, all the way back to the surface, their lashing flames leaving angry welts across your back. 

[You are reduced to the status of Invisible once again.]
translation:
当你退回鬼群中时，圣言转身面对你。许多炽热的符印烙在你的眼睛和头脑里。它们注意到了你的犹豫，它们像风暴一样移动。

圣言无情地追赶你，直到你回到灵枢上方的地面，它们的火焰卷须在你的背上留下了愤怒的伤痕。

[你的身份再次降至无形灵。]

original: Step into the cauldron, focusing on a powerful thought
translation: 踏入大锅，并专注于一个强大的念头

original:
A beacon blazes in your mind. Its light will fill you, keep you whole.
[You will lose your name, and with it 5 Mirrors. Perhaps you will be able to get it back at a later date.]
translation:
一盏明灯在你的心中闪耀。它的光芒会充盈你，让你保持完整。
[你将失去你的名字，并同时失去5点镜子。也许你可以在以后把它找回来。]

original: Nameless
translation: 无名

original:
As you step beneath the surface, foreign memories flood you. Fleeing through long grass. The crunch of bones between your jaws. Swirling, unfamiliar skies. You are coming apart.

Spirits swirl around you, silent shapes with arms outstretched. You are buffeted by memories: sword-fights in a forest, sunken libraries, a city aflame. You cling to your name, but there are a dozen other names you can call to mind, and you no longer know which is yours.

You fight the swirling currents and emerge on the other side mostly intact. Your name is gone. The other gaps in your memory are not too severe. You think.
translation:
当你踏入锅中时，陌生的记忆涌入你的脑海。穿过长长的草丛逃跑。下颌之间骨头嘎吱作响。天空旋转的、陌生的天空。你正在分崩离析。

鬼魂在你周围旋转，无声的身影伸出的他们手臂紧抓住你。回忆冲刷着你的脑海：森林中的剑术格斗，天野上沉没的图书馆，火光冲天的城市。你紧紧抓住属于自己的名字，但十几个你能想起的其他的名字瞬间涌入你的思绪之中，你不再记得哪个是你的本名。

你与漩涡搏斗，几乎完好无损地到达了另一边。你的名字不见了。你记忆中的其他空白并不严重。至少你这么认为。

original: A Spirifer Engine, Stopped
translation: 一辆停止运转的猎魂机车

original:
Spirifage, or the trade in souls, is ceaselessly prohibited in the Blue Kingdom. 

Nevertheless, spirifers flock here, drawn by the quality and abundance of souls available in the Kingdom. They will take lost spirits they can lead astray, or ransack the soul-troves locked in unplundered vaults.

The engine is covered in gaudy pennants, brass gongs and copper bells, in a poorly-grasped imitation of funeral customs intended to hoodwink Kingdom officials.
translation:
在蓝色王国，灵魂走私，或曰灵魂交易，是一贯受到禁止的。

但是，为其中灵魂的数量和质量所吸引的猎魂者们涌至蓝色王国。他们会带走那些误入他们圈套的迷失鬼魂，亦或洗劫那些锁在保险库里的珍贵灵魂宝藏。

他们的机车上挂着华丽的三角旗、铜锣和铜铃，这是一种模仿葬礼习俗的拙劣行为，目的是为了蒙蔽蓝色王国的当地官员。

original: Loot the engine's plundered haul
translation: 黑吃黑

original: It must rattle with stolen souls.
translation: 被盗的灵魂一定在里面嘎嘎作响。

original: Gold stored in lead
translation: 铅中黄金

original:
After a thorough and rapacious search of the engine, you unearth a concealed chamber in the hold. Inside, a battered and unpromising looking trunk. Have they already sold their cargo? 

Opening the trunk, you find a collection of London-made jars, cheaply manufactured, but housing a collection of unparalleled souls. You collect up the souls and depart the engine.
translation:
在对机车进行了一次彻底而贪婪的搜索之后，你在舱里发现了一个隐藏房间。里面是一个破烂不堪、看起来不怎么样的大箱子。他们已经卖掉了他们的货物吗？

打开箱子，你发现了一堆伦敦制造的罐子，虽然这些罐子制造成本低廉，但却里面收藏着无垢的灵魂。你把这些灵魂收集起来，然后离开了机车。

original: A return, thwarted
translation: 失望而返

original:
The captain's cabin is poorly hidden behind an array of funerary hangings. Perhaps they hoped to fool any officials that the engine might have encountered. 

Inside, you discover that he was part way through charting a course back to the transit relay. In his logs, the captain expresses disappointment with his haul. Looking at it, you can't help but agree.
translation:
车长室被可怜地隐藏在一排用于丧葬的挂饰后面。也许他们希望能骗过机车可能遇到的任何官员。

在里面，你发现了车长绘制了一半的返回中继站的路线。在他的日志中，车长表示对这趟旅途的收获感到失望。看着手中的战利品，你不禁感到同意。

original: Scrap the engine
translation: 拆卸机车

original:
Salvage what you can to repair your Hull.
[You will recover up to 20 points of Hull.]
translation:
尽你所能地搜刮废料来修复你的车体。
[你将恢复至多20点车体。]

original: An annoyance
translation: 一件烦人的事情

original: Spirifer Engines disguise themselves when entering the domain of the dead. They bedeck their hulls with clanking bells and tattered pennants and the detritus of scavenged burial customs. This rarely fools the Logoi who scour the Kingdom and mostly serves to frustrate your crew as they search for intact plating.
translation: 进入死者之国时，猎魂机车会伪装自身。他们在车体上悬挂叮当作响的铃铛，披覆破败褪色的幡旗，并点缀捡来的天葬残骸。这些伪装几乎骗不了在王国中巡弋的圣言，反倒让你的列车员在寻找完好的装甲板时徒增烦恼。

original: Invite the survivors to join your crew
translation: 邀请幸存者加入你的车队

original: A light moves at a window on the wreckage. Some still live, despite your barrage.
translation: 一盏灯在残骸上的窗户后面移动。尽管你的火力凶猛，但依然有人存活。

original: Acceptance
translation: 接纳

original:
The bleak-eyed crew consider your offer. The leader (a junior signaller) looks at the burnt jars of souls; the scorched log books; the remains of her superior officers scattered across the bridge.

The decision is unanimous.
translation:
眼神黯淡的列车员们考虑着你的提议。他们的领队（一个初级信号员）开始检查烧坏的装载着灵魂的罐子；焦黑的日志；散落在舰桥上的上级车务官的遗体。

他们的决定是一致的。

original: A cold calculation of odds
translation: 冷酷的概率

original:
The bleak-eyed crew (all lower-deck; your guns have blasted the command of this Engine from the sky) huddle to consider your offer. 

At last, one of their stokers, approaches you for a cigarette. He does not seem inclined to return to the rest; who view him with expressions of alternately contempt and disgust. They will remain with their engine; you leave them to their fate.
translation:
眼神黯淡的列车员们（都在下层甲板工作，你的大炮已经把这个机车的指挥层炸成了碎片）挤在一起考虑你的提议。

最后，他们中的一个司炉向你要了一支烟。他似乎并不愿意回到之前的同伴身边；其他人用蔑视和厌恶的表情看着他。他们将留在损坏的机车旁；你把他们交给命运。

original: Retrieve an Otherworldy Artefact
translation: 取回一个异界文物

original: Canny spirifers know that certain artefacts can open the Vaults of souls found across the Blue Kingdom.
translation: 精明的猎魂者知道，某些文物可以打开遍布蓝色王国的某个灵魂宝库。

original: Amidst the detritus of practical spirifage
translation: 在灵魂走私活动的残骸的包围中

original:
The engine has accumulated an astonishing amount of useless paraphernalia – some to disguise itself as a merchant engine, some to disguise itself as a funerary vessel, some more obscure in purpose. Your engineer dismisses it as the worthless trash it is.

A hidden compartment in the battery contains what you're after: a glistening artefact to unseal a Blue Kingdom vault.
translation:
这台机车积累了数量惊人的无用配件，有些是为了把自己伪装成一个行商的机车，有些是为了把自己伪装成一个用于丧葬的机车，有些则是为了更隐蔽的目的。你的工程师把这些配件当作毫无价值的垃圾来处理。

一个隐藏在火炮组中的隔间里有你要找的东西：一个闪闪发光的文物，用于打开蓝色王国的墓室或者保险库。

original: An Eater of the Dead, Defeated
translation: 被打败的食魂徒

original:
A rancid horror, with the elongated muzzle of a crocodile and the plumage of a peacock corpse conjoined by a knot of bloated hippopotamus with many, many mournful eyes.

The bane of the trespasser and the devourer of the dead. The powers of the Blue Kingdom tolerate them because they thin out the ranks of the unwanted dead.
translation:
一个腐臭的恐怖的生物，有着像鳄鱼一样拉长的大嘴和像由腐烂孔雀尸体上的羽毛组成的羽衣，被一节像河马一样臃肿的骨块连在一起，上面长着很多很多哀伤的眼睛。

这是那些非法入侵的人的麻烦，也是死者或灵魂的吞噬者。蓝色王国的权力机构容忍它们，因为它们可以减少那些不受欢迎的多余的死者的数量。

original: Extract its meat
translation: 收集它的肉

original: There is an abundance of flesh available.
translation: 这里有大量的肉可供取用

original: A grim harvest
translation: 阴沉的收获

original:
With careful application of your cannery, you prise off the most succulent slabs of meat. Your crew shuttle them back to your engine.

Now that the beast's bones are exposed, you can see that they are scored with Correspondence. The sigils are fractured; many of its still-pulsing internal organs are twisted and deliquescent. This doesn't look like damage from your weapons: was it made to be thus?
translation:
你小心翼翼地使用装罐机，把最多汁的肉片撬下来。你的列车员将它们送回你的机车。

现在，野兽的骨头暴露在外，你可以看到上面有信符的刻痕。符印是破碎的：有许多仍在跳动的内部器官扭曲着，并且在不断溶化。看起来不像是你的武器造成的伤害：这是它生理机制的一部分吗？

original: Search its maw
translation: 搜索它的咽喉

original: Its jaw gapes, exposing waterfalls of noxious drool. It may have eaten something valuable; you'll have to climb in to find out.
translation: 它的下颚张开，流出的有毒唾液像瀑布一样倾泻下来。它可能吃了什么有价值的东西。你得爬进去才能确认。

original: A taste for spirifer
translation: 灵贩的味道

original:
Three stokers hold the line of your sky-suit as you plunge in. The smell is abhorrent, drawing your gaze to the rotting church-steeples of its teeth.
 
Between the sharp spindles of the teeth, you find the remnant of the Eater's recent meals. Nestled, unchewed, between two black molars you pry out a number of souls.
translation:
三个司炉拉住你潜天装的连接线，把你放进它的咽喉。口腔里面的味道很难闻，气味把你的目光引到它那像教堂尖顶一般锐利的牙齿上。

在尖锐的牙齿缝隙之间，你发现了食魂徒最近进食的残余物。在两颗黑色的臼齿之间，你撬出了一些残存的灵魂，它们没有被嚼碎。

original: The meals of the Devourer
translation: 食魂徒的饮食

original:
A couple of your crew hold the line of your sky-suit as you plunge in. Even through your helmet, the smell is like a morgue full of gassy cadavers. 

Fishing within the rotting gums, you uncover mottled scraps of hair, splinters of doomed engines, and pools of liquefying flesh. There are a few undigested valuables amidst the gore.
translation:
几个列车员拉住你潜天装的连接线，把你放进去探索。即使你戴着密不透风的头盔，透过来的气味仍像那充满一堆胀气尸体的停尸房所散发出的，令人反胃的味道。

你在腐烂的牙床里翻找，发现了一些染有血斑的头皮碎片、损坏严重的机车碎片和一滩液化的肉。在这些血肉中还有一些未被消化的贵重物品。

original: Claim a trophy
translation: 获取一个战利品

original:
There are very few living who can say they've slain an Eater of the Dead.
[This will give Experience or Reduce Terror.]
translation:
很少有人能杀死一只食魂徒。
[这会给予经验或减少恐惧。]

original: A little night work
translation: 一个小小的夜间工作

original:
Your crew are very taken with the idea, until it comes to the practicalities. 

Inevitably, you find yourself out, alone, on the oozing back of the beast, bone saw in hand. Where to begin? A jagged yellow-black fang? An eye, opal-black and sad as a child's? Or, a clutch of feathers, luminous and bright? 

You return to your engine to a chorus of cheers, a brace of bloody trophies in your hand.
translation:
你的列车员对这个想法很感兴趣，直到它付诸实践。

不可避免地，你离开机车，独自一人站在不断渗出液体的天兽背上，手里拿着一把骨锯。该从哪里开始呢？一个凹凸不平的黄黑色利齿？一只如孩童一样悲伤的蛋白石般的黑色眼睛？或者一束发光的耀眼羽毛？

你在一片欢呼声中回到了你的机车，手里拿着一串血淋淋的战利品。

original: Triumph
translation: 胜利

original:
You go out with bonesaw and malice, and return with a clutch of bloody feathers, brilliant as the dawn, and an oozing eyeball, black as an opal and large as a boiler. 

A chorus of ragged cheers goes up. You have triumphed over something terrible and now dead.
translation:
你带着骨锯和恶意走出机车，然后拎着一束血淋淋的羽毛回来，它们像黎明的太阳一样光亮鲜艳。还有一颗不断渗出液体的眼球，像蛋白石一样黑，像锅炉一样大。

一阵参差不齐而疲惫不堪的欢呼声响起。你已经战胜了孽物，现在它已然灭亡。

original: A Blue Logos, Diminished
translation: 减损的蓝色圣言

original:
A wheel of living flame; a commandment of the Westernmost King's highest Law; an utterance of fire and glory.

This Logos was of the Order of Perfection, appointed to extinguish errors of vitality. The Antedeceased are their prey.

It is not dead, only diminished. It will rekindle in time, at which point it would be advisable to be far away.
translation:
一只由活着的火焰构成的巨轮；它是蓝宝石之王说出的话语，代表着最高真理的戒条：火焰与荣誉的吐露。

这圣言属于“至善律令”，被派去消灭由活力带来的错误。质亡灵便是它的猎物。

它没有死，只是暂时熄灭了。它的火焰终将重燃，到时候最好离它远一点。

original: Claim its embers
translation: 获得它的余烬

original:
Use its living fire to invigorate your engines.
[You will gain Fuel.]
translation:
用它的活火来鼓动你的引擎。
[你会获得燃料。]

original: To become fire, rather than be burned
translation: 为火，而非受灼于火

original:
You send out a complement of stokers to tame the immortal flame. They approach the mangled wheel of fire: specks of shadow before the searing light. 

All hands return. No one burns today. The embers are shovelled into the boiler, which roars like a triumphant tiger. Gouts of steam billow from the smoke-stack.
translation:
你派出一队司炉去驯服那不朽的火焰。他们走近残缺不全的火轮：在炽烈的光芒面前，斑驳的人影不断晃动。

所有出去的人手都回来了。今天没有人被烧死。圣言的余烬被铲入锅炉，后者像一只得胜的老虎一样咆哮着。烟囱里窜出大量蒸汽。

original: To be burned
translation: 受灼于火

original:
You send out a complement of stokers to gather embers from the mangled wheel of fire.

One overreaches and spills the embers they were carrying. You can't hear the screams from behind glass, but you watch shadow after shadow ignite. 

Some return, carrying still smouldering embers. You make use of what you have left.
translation:
你派出一队司炉去收集那残缺不全的火轮上的余烬。

一位司炉不小心摔倒了，打翻了他们携带的余烬。你听不到玻璃后面的尖叫，但你看到一个又一个人影被点燃。

一部分人带着还在冒烟的余烬回来了。你让剩下的东西物尽其用。

original: To be fire
translation: 为火

original:
You send out a complement of stokers to tame the immortal flame. The rest of you watch from the galley window. There is not a sound in the room as your crew near the Logoi; sun spots to the sun. They work with caution, but one leans too close. Were they transfixed by the glaring beauty?

The rest return later with fuel and the ashes of their fellow. They are subdued. They tell you she wept before falling.
translation:
你派出一队司炉去驯服那不朽的火焰。其余的人从厨房的窗口沉默地观看着。当你的列车员靠近圣言时，房间里没有一丝声音；斑驳的人影就像太阳上的黑子。他们小心翼翼地工作，但有一个人离圣言靠得太近。那人是被这耀眼的美景迷住了吗？

其余的人后来带着燃料和他们同伴的灰烬回来了。他们默不作声。他们告诉你，她在倒下之前流泪了。

original: Celebrate your victory
translation: 庆祝你的胜利

original:
You have triumphed over a Prince of Heaven.
[This will reduce Terror.]
translation:
你战胜了一位天界的王侯。
[这将减少恐惧。]

original: Victory, cry victory!
translation: 胜利！高呼胜利！

original: A stoker brings out his fiddle; a signaller her flute.  The galley is raided. The bridge becomes an East-End pub for an evening and several of your crew get blind drunk. The laughter is queasy with the dissipation of terror.
translation: 一位司炉拿出他的小提琴，信号员则吹响他珍藏的长笛。 厨房就像被海关搜查过一样凌乱不堪。车桥在一个晚上变成了伦敦东岸的酒吧，你的几个列车员都喝醉了。恐惧消散，笑声传到了很远的地方。

original: Claim a fragment of a lost sigil
translation: 获得一个遗失的符印碎片

original: Fire becomes ash. But at the Logos' core, angles of fierce, embered light still burn. Can fire have bones?
translation: 火化为灰。但在圣言的核心，暴烈的、琥珀色的光芒仍在燃烧。火有骨头吗？

original: A subdued crew
translation: 压抑的列车员

original: You retrieve the fragments of the Logos' heart-sigil. The engine is quiet when you return. Is it relief, that the battle with the Logos is finally over? Or disappointment – that all you have to show for your bloody triumph is half a sigil? Either way, you'll have to find another Logos.
translation: 你取回了圣言核心符印的碎片。你回来的时候，机车上很安静。是因为与圣言的战斗终于结束而感到解脱吗？还是对你的血腥胜利只有半个符印而感到失望？无论怎样，你都必须找到另一个圣言。

original: Assemble the fragments of the lost sigil
translation: 拼合失落的符印碎片

original: Another Logos, another charred sigil-skeleton. Another partial sigil growth. It is enough.
translation: 又一个圣言，又一个烧焦的符印轮廓。又一部分的符印生长出来。这就够了。

original: Like a winter chestnut, oven hot
translation: 就像冬天的烤板栗，冒着刚出炉的热气

original: The sigil fragments retain their heat. Even many hours later, you still have to wear gloves. Using tongs requisitioned from the galley, you rotate the pieces till they align. Where the sigil breaks off on this one, you can see the pattern on the next. There are enough overlaps between the two that you can trace the whole sigil. Fully formed, the pattern glowers resentfully.
translation: 符印碎片保留了它们的热力。即使过了好几个小时，你在接触它们时仍然要戴上手套。你用从厨房里拿了一个火钳，旋转符印碎片直到它们对齐。在这块符印断裂的地方，你可以看到下一块碎片上的图案。两个符印碎片之间有足够多的重叠部分，你可以勾画出整个完整符印。完整的符印完全临摹出来之后，上面图案闪烁着诡异的光。

original: Ambition: Recover a spark with which to open the Arbiter's vault
translation: 野心：获得用来打开仲裁者金库的火花

original: Her vault requires three colours of language-fire.
translation: 打开她的金库需要三种颜色的语言之火。

original: The Blue Knight
translation: 蓝骑士

original:
The Blue Knight throws his sword to the ground and yields, raising his gauntlets in supplication. He'll give you whatever you want—

No. No. You blink away the visions, and send a team of stokers with long-handled lamps to recover a spark of the Logos's living flame.
translation:
蓝骑士把它的剑扔到地上，投降了，举起他的臂铠向你祈求仁慈。它将给你任何你想要的东西——

不。不。你眨了眨眼，甩掉幻象，并派了一队拿着长柄燃灯的司炉去回收圣言那活着的火焰所迸发的火花。

original: A Red Logos, Diminished
translation: 减损的红色圣言

original:
A wheel of living flame; a commandment of the Westernmost King's highest Law; an utterance of fire and glory.

This Logos was of the Order of Propriety. The Propriety regulate the officials of the eternal bureaucracy.  They visit judgement upon any dead of the Yoked caste – the lowliest of the Kingdom's servitors – who permit themselves to be seen or heard, or who abandon their duties.

It is not dead, only diminished. It will rekindle in time, at which point it would be advisable to be far away.
translation:
一只由活着的火焰构成的巨轮；它是蓝宝石之王说出的话语，代表着最高真理的戒条：火焰与荣誉的吐露。

这圣言属于“通礼律令”。通礼约束着这永恒王国官僚机构中的官员。它们对任何处于缚链灵——王国最低级的仆人——地位的死者进行审判，被审判的缚链灵或是因为放任自己被看到或听到，或是因为放弃了自己的职责。

它没有死，只是暂时熄灭了。它的火焰终将重燃，到时候最好离它远一点。

original: Claim cooling embers
translation: 获得冷却的余烬

original:
Use its living fire to invigorate your engines.
[You will gain Fuel.]
translation:
用它的活火来鼓动你的引擎。
[你会获得燃料。]

translation: 为火，而非受灼于火

一部分人带着还在冒烟的余烬回来了。你让剩下的东西物尽其用。

translation:
你战胜了一位天界的王侯。
[这将减少恐惧。]

translation: 获得一个遗失的符印碎片

original: Fire becomes ash. But at the Logos' core, angles of fierce, embered light still burn. Can fire have bones?
translation: 火化为灰。但在圣言的核心，暴烈的、琥珀色的光芒仍在燃烧。火有骨头吗？

original: A subdued crew
translation: 压抑的列车员

original: You retrieve the fragments of the Logos' heart-sigil. The engine is quiet when you return. Is it relief, that the battle with the Logos is finally over? Or disappointment – that all you have to show for your bloody triumph is half a sigil? Either way, you'll have to find another Logos.
translation: 你取回了圣言核心符印的碎片。你回来的时候，机车上很安静。是因为与圣言的战斗终于结束而感到解脱吗？还是对你的血腥胜利只有半个符印而感到失望？无论怎样，你都必须找到另一个圣言。

original: Assemble the fragments of the lost sigil
translation: 拼合失落的符印碎片

original: Another Logos, another charred sigil-skeleton. Another partial sigil growth. It is enough.
translation: 又一个圣言，又一个烧焦的符印轮廓。又一部分的符印生长出来。这就够了。

original: Like a winter chestnut, oven hot
translation: 就像冬天的烤板栗，冒着刚出炉的热气

original: The sigil fragments retain their heat. Even many hours later, you still have to wear gloves. Using tongs requisitioned from the galley, you rotate the pieces till they align. Where the sigil breaks off on this one, you can see the pattern on the next. There are enough overlaps between the two that you can trace the whole sigil. Fully formed, the pattern glowers resentfully.
translation: 符印碎片保留了它们的热力。即使过了好几个小时，你在接触它们时仍然要戴上手套。你用从厨房里拿了一个火钳，旋转符印碎片直到它们对齐。在这块符印断裂的地方，你可以看到下一块碎片上的图案。两个符印碎片之间有足够多的重叠部分，你可以勾画出整个完整符印。完整的符印完全临摹出来之后，上面图案闪烁着诡异的光。

original: Ambition: Recover a spark with which to open the Arbiter's vault
translation: 野心：获得用来打开仲裁者金库的火花

original: Her vault requires three colours of language-fire.
translation: 打开她的金库需要三种颜色的语言之火。

original: The Red Knight
translation: 红骑士

original:
Blood froths from the Red Knight's visor as he dies. You sheathe your blade—

No. No. You blink away the visions, and send a team of stokers with long-handled lamps to recover a spark of the Logos's living flame.
translation:
红骑士死后，鲜血从他的面罩中汩汩流出。你收剑入鞘——

不。不。你眨了眨眼，甩掉幻象，并派了一队拿着长柄燃灯的司炉去回收圣言那活着的火焰所迸发的火花。

original: An Aureate Logos, Diminished
translation: 减损的金色圣言

original:
A wheel of living flame; a commandment of the Westernmost King's highest Law; an utterance of fire and glory.

This Logos was one of the Visitation, who deliver trials upon the dead pilgrims of the Ephemera caste. 

It is not dead, only diminished. It will rekindle in time, at which point it would be advisable to be far away.
translation:
一只由活着的火焰构成的巨轮；它是蓝宝石之王说出的话语，代表着最高真理的戒条：火焰与荣誉的吐露。

这圣言属于“探寻律令”，为浮生灵种的死亡朝圣者提供试炼。

它没有死，只是暂时熄灭了。它的火焰终将重燃，到时候最好离它远一点。

original: Claim cooling embers
translation: 获得冷却的余烬

original:
Use its living fire to invigorate your engines.
[You will gain Fuel.]
translation:
用它的活火来鼓动你的引擎。
[你会获得燃料。]

original: To become fire, rather than be burned
translation: 为火，而非受灼于火

original:
You send out a complement of stokers to tame the immortal flame. They approach the mangled wheel of fire: specks of shadow before the searing light. 

All hands return. No one burns today. The embers are shovelled into the boiler, which roars like a triumphant tiger. Gouts of steam billow from the smoke-stack.
translation:
你派出一队司炉去驯服那不朽的火焰。他们走近残缺不全的火轮：在炽烈的光芒面前，斑驳的人影不断晃动。

所有出去的人手都回来了。今天没有人被烧死。圣言的余烬被铲入锅炉，后者像一只得胜的老虎一样咆哮着。烟囱里窜出大量蒸汽。

original: To be burned
translation: 受灼于火

original:
You send out a complement of stokers to gather embers from the mangled wheel of fire.

One overreaches and spills the embers they were carrying. You can't hear the screams from behind glass, but you watch shadow after shadow ignite. 

Some return, carrying still smouldering embers. You make use of what you have left.
translation:
你派出一队司炉去收集那残缺不全的火轮上的余烬。

一位司炉不小心摔倒了，打翻了他们携带的余烬。你听不到玻璃后面的尖叫，但你看到一个又一个人影被点燃。

一部分人带着还在冒烟的余烬回来了。你让剩下的东西物尽其用。

original: To be fire
translation: 为火

original:
You send out a complement of stokers to tame the immortal flame. The rest of you watch from the galley window. There is not a sound in the room as your crew near the Logoi; sun spots to the sun. They work with caution, but one leans too close. Were they transfixed by the glaring beauty?

The rest return later with fuel and the ashes of their fellow. They are subdued. They tell you she wept before falling.
translation:
你派出一队司炉去驯服那不朽的火焰。其余的人从厨房的窗口沉默地观看着。当你的列车员靠近圣言时，房间里没有一丝声音；斑驳的人影就像太阳上的黑子。他们小心翼翼地工作，但有一个人离圣言靠得太近。那人是被这耀眼的美景迷住了吗？

其余的人后来带着燃料和他们同伴的灰烬回来了。他们默不作声。他们告诉你，她在倒下之前流泪了。

original: Celebrate your victory
translation: 庆祝你的胜利

original:
You have triumphed over a Prince of Heaven.
[This will reduce Terror.]
translation:
你战胜了一位天界的王侯。
[这将减少恐惧。]

original: Victory, cry victory!
translation: 胜利！高呼胜利！

original: A stoker brings out his fiddle; a signaller her flute.  The galley is raided. The bridge becomes an East-End pub for an evening and several of your crew get blind drunk. The laughter is queasy with the dissipation of terror.
translation: 一位司炉拿出他的小提琴，信号员则吹响他珍藏的长笛。 厨房就像被海关搜查过一样凌乱不堪。车桥在一个晚上变成了伦敦东岸的酒吧，你的几个列车员都喝醉了。恐惧消散，笑声传到了很远的地方。

original: Claim a fragment of a sigil
translation: 获得一个符印碎片

original: Fire becomes ash. But at the Logos' core, angles of fierce, embered light still burn. Can fire have bones?
translation: 火化为灰。但在圣言的核心，暴烈的、琥珀色的光芒仍在燃烧。火有骨头吗？

original: A subdued crew
translation: 压抑的列车员

original: You retrieve the fragments of the Logos' heart-sigil. The engine is quiet when you return. Is it relief, that the battle with the Logos is finally over? Or disappointment – that all you have to show for your bloody triumph is half a sigil? Either way, you'll have to find another Logos.
translation: 你取回了圣言核心符印的碎片。你回来的时候，机车上很安静。是因为与圣言的战斗终于结束而感到解脱吗？还是对你的血腥胜利只有半个符印而感到失望？无论怎样，你都必须找到另一个圣言。

original: Assemble the fragments of the lost sigil
translation: 拼合失落的符印碎片

original: Another Logos, another charred sigil-skeleton. Another partial sigil growth. It is enough.
translation: 又一个圣言，又一个烧焦的符印轮廓。又一部分的符印生长出来。这就够了。

original: Like a winter chestnut, oven hot
translation: 就像冬天的烤板栗，冒着刚出炉的热气

original: The sigil fragments retain their heat. Even many hours later, you still have to wear gloves. Using tongs requisitioned from the galley, you rotate the pieces till they align. Where the sigil breaks off on this one, you can see the pattern on the next. There are enough overlaps between the two that you can trace the whole sigil. Fully formed, the pattern glowers resentfully.
translation: 符印碎片保留了它们的热力。即使过了好几个小时，你在接触它们时仍然要戴上手套。你用从厨房里拿了一个火钳，旋转符印碎片直到它们对齐。在这块符印断裂的地方，你可以看到下一块碎片上的图案。两个符印碎片之间有足够多的重叠部分，你可以勾画出整个完整符印。完整的符印完全临摹出来之后，上面图案闪烁着诡异的光。

original: Ambition: Recover a spark with which to open the Arbiter's vault
translation: 野心：获得用来打开仲裁者金库的火花

original: Her vault requires three colours of language-fire.
translation: 打开她的金库需要三种颜色的语言之火。

original: The Gilded Knight
translation: 金骑士

original:
You stand over the corpse of the Gilded Knight, your blade reflecting moonlight—

No. No. You blink away the visions, and send a team of stokers with long-handled lamps to recover a spark of the Logos's living flame.
translation:
你站在金骑士的尸身旁，剑刃反射着月光——

不。不。你眨了眨眼，甩掉幻象，并派了一队拿着长柄燃灯的司炉去回收圣言那活着的火焰所迸发的火花。

original: Dismissed
translation: 驳回

original:
The Judge peers at you.

"I have seventy-two more spirits to process before the end of the hour if I can hope to meet today's quota," she says. "Do you really think I have time to pore over the records of all the spirits who passed through here and were declared Dead?"
translation:
法官凝视着你。

“如果我希望完成今天的任务定额，我需要在一小时内处理72个甚至更多鬼魂的审核，”她说。“你真的认为我有时间翻阅所有经过这里并被宣布死亡的鬼魂的记录吗？”

original: Offer a tithe
translation: 提供一份捐赠

original: The Judge is always in need of more gemstones.
translation: 法官总是需要更多的宝石。

original: A lead
translation: 一条线索

original:
She examines each gemstone expertly. "This changes everything," she says. "I'll close the courtroom and get to work. Return at the end of the day."

When you return, she is sitting before a book that's easily four times as tall as she is. The pages are cast from brittle clay, and a servile Graven stands atop a precarious stepladder, turning them periodically. She holds up a hand as he finally reaches the correct page.

"The spirit you seek has been judged as Dead," says the Judge. "She has moved on to Death's Door. If you're lucky, you can reach her before she passes on."
translation:
她熟练地检查了每一块宝石。“这改变了一切，”她说。“我会关闭法庭然后开始工作。一天结束后你再回来。”

当你回来时，她正坐在一本书前，你很肯定这本书有她身高的四倍那么厚。书页是由易碎的粘土铸成的，一个卑微的墓族站在一个不稳定的梯子上，周期性的翻动着书页。当终于翻到正确的一页时，她举起一只手。

“你要找的鬼魂已经被判定为死亡，”法官说。“她已经前往了死亡之门。如果你幸运的话，你可以在她步入大门前找到她。”

original: Persuade her of your task's importance
translation: 让她相信你的任务的重要性

original: Somehow, despite the fact that her face is a gem-studded skull, she manages to project a decidedly sceptical air.
translation: 不知道什么原因，尽管她的面貌是一个镶满了宝石的颅骨，但她仍让你觉得她对这件任务持怀疑态度——这还可以商量……

original: A lead
translation: 一条线索

original:
She listens with sympathy as you relay the Industrialist's story. "Oh, fine," she says. "I'll get to work. Come back at the end of the day."

When you return, she is sitting before a book that's easily four times as tall as she is. The pages are cast from brittle clay, and a servile Graven stands atop a precarious stepladder, turning them periodically. She holds up a hand as he finally reaches the correct page.

"The spirit you seek has been judged as Dead," says the Judge. "She has moved on to Death's Door. If you're lucky, you can reach her before she passes on."
translation:
当你转述实业家的故事时，她同情地听着。“哦，好吧，”她说，“我去工作了。一天结束后你再回来。”

当你回来时，她正坐在一本书前，你很肯定这本书有她身高的四倍那么厚。书页是由易碎的粘土铸成的，一个卑微的墓族站在一个不稳定的梯子上，周期性的翻动着书页。当终于翻到正确的一页时，她举起一只手。

“你要找的鬼魂已经被判定为死亡，”法官说。“她已经前往了死亡之门。如果你幸运的话，你可以在她步入大门前找到她。”

original: No dice
translation: 不走运

original: "I can't help you," she says. "I'm sorry. That's the end of it."
translation: “我帮不了你，”她说，“我很抱歉。没什么好说的。”

original: There's nothing you can do
translation: 你无能为力

original: The Judge waves you away without another word.
translation: 法官一言不发地挥手让你离开。

original: Make a demand
translation: 提出要求

original: You can call in a formidable favour.
translation: 你可以使用一个强大的恩惠

original: A lead
translation: 一条线索

original:
On hearing the favour you're owed, she snaps to attention. "That changes everything," she says hastily. "I'll get to work. Come back at the end of the day."

When you return, she is sitting before a book that's easily four times as tall as she is. The pages are cast from brittle clay, and a servile Graven stands atop a precarious stepladder, turning them periodically. She holds up a hand as he finally reaches the correct page.

"The spirit you seek has been judged Dead," says the Judge. "She's moved on to Death's Door. If you're lucky, you can reach her before she passes on."
translation:
当听到你欠的人情时，她立即集中了注意力。“这改变了一切，”她说。“我会开始工作。一天结束后你再回来。”

当你回来时，她正坐在一本书前，你很肯定这本书有她身高的四倍那么厚。书页是由易碎的粘土铸成的，一个卑微的墓族站在一个不稳定的梯子上，周期性的翻动着书页。当终于翻到正确的一页时，她举起一只手。

“你要找的鬼魂已经被判定为死亡，”法官说。“她已经前往了死亡之门。如果你幸运的话，你可以在她步入大门前找到她。”

original: The Lost Love
translation: 失落的爱人

original:
The Lost Love resists your attempts to lead her away from Death's Door. You hand her a stick of chalk, and she scrawls on the wall of the Catafalque.

I LOVE HIM STILL, she writes. BUT I AM READY TO MOVE ON.

She pulls a small clay jar from her robes and thrusts it into your hands.

IT HOLDS MY VOICE, she writes. GIVE IT TO HIM. A MEMENTO.
translation:
失落的爱人拒绝了你带她离开死亡之门的意图。你递给她一根粉笔，她在灵柩的墙上书写。

我 仍 爱 着 他，她写道。但 我 已 经 准 备 好 继 续 前 进 了 。

她从她的袍子里拿出一个小泥罐并把它塞到你的手里。

这 里 面 有 我 的 声 音，她写道。把 它 给 他 。一 个 纪 念 品 。

original: Convince her to return to the world of the living
translation: 说服她回到生者的世界中

original: It won't be difficult. She has little willpower left after the Catafalque's trials. A few more mentions of the Industrialist, and her resolve will crumble.
translation: 这并不困难。经过灵柩的检验，她的意志力已经所剩无几。再多提几句实业家的事情，她的决心就会崩溃。

original: A turning point
translation: 一个转折点

original:
She glances back at Death's Door, and hesitates. It begins to open. The first light blazes forth. She writes a single word on the wall.

YES.

You grab her and pull her away from the Door and its enticing ensnaring light. You wait, clutching each other, until it slams shut once again. 

[qvd:139195(salt_warning)]
translation:
她回头瞥了一眼死亡之门，犹豫不决。大门开始打开。第一道耀眼的光芒喷涌而出。她在墙上写了一个字。

好。

你抓住她，把她从门前和那诱人光芒的照耀下拉开。你们紧紧抓住对方，等待着，直到大门再次关闭。

[qvd:139195(salt_warning)]

original: Accept the jar and let her go
translation: 接受罐子，放她离开

original: It's probably for the best.
translation: 也许这样是最好的

original: The Door opens
translation: 大门打开

original:
Death's Door tilts, opens, and blinding light floods over you. A mass of spirits skid helplessly into the light. The Lost Love is among them. She turns to face you as she descends – perhaps to change her mind, perhaps to see another living thing one last time. Either way, she is too late. The light engulfs her.

You are left with the jar. While it's in your hands, and with the faintest exertion of will, you can think a sentence, and the jar will speak in a female monotone. This is all of her that remains. You can only hope that will be enough.
translation:
死亡之门倾斜、打开，耀眼的光芒淹没了你。一大群鬼魂无助地滑入光中，失落的爱人就在其中。她在下落时转过身来面向你，也许是改变了主意，也许是为了最后一次看到另一个生命。无论怎样，她都来不及后悔了。光吞噬了她。

你只剩下了一个罐子。当它在你手中的时候，只要有最微弱的意愿，你可以想一个句子，罐子就会用一个单调的女性声音把它说出来。这就是她留下的全部。你只能希望这就足够了。

original: The Daughter's Deliberations
translation: 太阳之女的考虑

original:
"If a spirit leaves my father's kingdom without my blessing, she will be rendered to salt. I am pleased with this state of affairs." As she states this, pillars of salt spring up around you like a circle of standing stones.

"Why, then, should I break centuries of tradition and permit her to leave? To allow such a thing goes against everything my father and I strive for."
translation:
“如果一个鬼魂没有得到我的祝福就离开我父亲的国度，她将被变成盐柱。我对这种状况很满意。”当她说出这句话时，盐柱在你周围突然生长涌现出来，就像一圈站立的石头。

“那么，为什么我应该打破几个世纪的传统，允许她离开？允许这样的事情违背了我父亲和我所努力的一切。”

original: Offer a costly tithe
translation: 提供一个昂贵的捐赠

original: Such a request has a momentous cost.
translation: 这样的请求需要付出极其高昂的代价。

original: A tithe is paid
translation: 代价已经付出

original:
"Your offer is enough for me to consider your request. But I must impose a limitation." The Sun's Daughter pauses. "The spirit in question can only return to her lover for a year and a day. 

"If you fail to bring her back within that time limit, the consequences will be severe." With that final word, she seems to grow in stature. Her eyes become shining hurricanes. For a terrible moment she looms over you, huge as a mountain, wide as a sea. "Severe beyond measure or reason, and falling solely on your shoulders, traveller."
translation:
“你的捐赠足以让我考虑你的请求。但我必须施加一个限制，”太阳之女停顿了一下，“那位特赦的鬼魂只能在她的爱人身边待一年零一天，在那之后，她必须回来。”

“如果你不能在这个时限之前把她带回来，后果将很严重。”随着这最后一句话，她的身体似乎在逐渐变大。她的双眼变成了带有闪电的骇人光芒的猛烈飓风。在那可怕的一刻，她笼罩着你，高大如山，宽广如海。“这后果严重到你无法估量，也无法理解而且这一切都会落在你的肩上，旅行者。”

original: On second thoughts...
translation: 再考虑一下……

original: The price is too high. Perhaps you will return later, when you can meet it.
translation: 这价格太高昂了。也许你以后会回来——当你能满足它时。

original: The Sands Run Down
translation: 沙子滑落，时间流逝

original:
It is time.

The Bleak Industrialist refuses to allow you to collect the Lost Love. He brandishes a pistol; he threatens to shoot you on the spot. You'll have to kill him before he lets you take her.

Large shapes loom in the darkness of the hallway. He has hired some large, shadowy men to help him make good on the threat.
translation:
是时候了。

毫无希望的实业家拒绝让你带走失落的爱人。他挥舞着手枪，威胁说要当场射杀你。你必须杀了他——如果他坚持的话。

在走廊的黑暗中，一些健壮的身影隐约可见。他雇佣了一些大块头、阴暗的人，帮他兑现他的威胁。

original: Shoot the Industrialist before he shoots you
translation: 在实业家射杀你之前先对他开枪

original: You'll have to be quick.
translation: 你必须要快。

original: A short, bloody affair
translation: 一件短暂而血腥的事情

original:
Your pistol cracks once, twice. The first gunshot barely registers. The second knocks the Industrialist down, gun tumbling from his hand.

The Industrialist didn't fear death, but his hired thugs certainly do, especially with their paymaster dead on the floor. When you point the pistol in their direction, they retreat.

There's nothing left but to order your crew into the suddenly-quiet mansion to collect the Lost Love from her room.
translation:
你的手枪响了一次，又响了一次。第一声枪响几乎没有人注意到。第二枪把实业家打倒在地，枪从他的手中滑落。

实业家并不害怕死亡，但他雇佣的那些暴徒当然害怕——尤其是他们的老板在地上死去的时候。当你把手枪指向他们的方向，他们逃跑了。

剩下的就是命令你的列车员进入突然安静下来的大宅，从失落爱人的房间里带走她。

original: A short, bloody affair
translation: 一件短暂而血腥的事情

original:
You make a move for your gun, and the Industrialist fires his. You feel a sudden blow to the chest, and when you look down, there is a blossoming red stain.

As you fall to the floor, your alarmed crew burst through the door. The last thing you hear is gunfire.

When you wake up, you find yourself back at the engine, your limbs stiff and bandages shrouding you from head to toe. You've been in a coma for a month. Several crew died recovering your wounded body.
translation:
你摸了一下你的枪准备采取一些行动，但实业家却率先开枪了。你突然的感到胸口受到铁锥般的打击，你低头看去，那里一朵血花绽放。

你倒在地上，你那些惊慌失措的列车员冲进门来。你记忆里最后听到的只剩枪声。

当你醒来时，你发现自己又回到了机车上，四肢僵硬，全身上下都覆盖着绷带。你已经昏迷了一个月。有几名列车员为救回你受伤的身体而牺牲。

original: Try to calm him down
translation: 试着让他平静下来

original: It may not be possible.
translation: 这可能有点困难。

original: Deaf ears
translation: 充耳不闻

original: Your words are useless. The Industrialist cocks his pistol and jabs it alarmingly in your direction. He cannot be reasoned with, not in this state; you will have to try another approach.
translation: 你的话语没有作用。实业家拔出手枪，警觉地指你的方向。在这种情况下，他可能听不进道理，你必须尝试另一种方法。

original: Allow him to keep the Lost Love
translation: 允许他保留失落的爱人

original: The Arbiter of Fates will not be happy, but what is there to do?
translation: 命运仲裁者不会高兴的，但这有什么办法呢？

original: A peaceful end
translation: 一个和平的结局

original:
The Industrialist lowers his pistol. His whole body is shaking, and he is covered in a sheen of sweat.

"I thought I would have to shoot you to protect her," he murmurs. "I'm many things, but I'm not a killer. Thank you for not making me one."

He gestures to one of his men. A clinking purse is dropped at your feet.

"Consider this severance pay," says the Industrialist. "I never want to see you again."
translation:
实业家放下了他的手枪。他的整个身体都在颤抖，浑身是汗。

“我以为我必须向你开枪才能保护她，”他喃喃地说，“我有很多身份，但我不是一个杀手。谢谢你没有让我成为一个杀手。”

他向他的一个手下打了个手势。一个叮当响的钱包掉在你的脚下。

“考虑一下这个遣散费，"实业家说，“我再也不想见到你了。”

original: Pretend to acquiesce, then return in the night with your crew
translation: 假装同意，然后在夜里带着你的列车员回来

original: You'd rather not suffer the consequences of the Arbiter's wrath.
translation: 你不愿承受仲裁者的愤怒所带来的后果。

original: A daring heist
translation: 一次大胆的盗窃

original:
You agree to leave in peace and never return. The Industrialist seems relieved not to have to kill you. His burly hirelings grab you by the scruff of your shirt and haul you out onto the street.

The next evening you return with your crew, a crowbar, a set of lockpicks, a grappling hook, and a fortunately-unnecessary bottle of chloroform. You take the Lost Love from his cellar. She will be returned to the Blue Kingdom where she belongs.
translation:
你同意和平地离开并不再回来。实业家似乎为不用杀你而松了一口气。他那些魁梧的手下抓住你的衣领，把你拖到街上。

第二天晚上，你带着你的列车员、一根撬棍、一套开锁器、一个抓钩和一瓶也许比较幸运无需使用的氯仿。你从他的地窖里带走了失落的爱人。她将被送回属于她的蓝色王国。

original: A bloody conclusion
translation: 一个血腥的结束

original:
You agree to leave in peace and never return. The Industrialist seems relieved not to have to kill you. 

The next evening you return with your crew and break onto the premises with the aid of a crowbar. Everything goes perfectly, right up until you surprise the Industrialist while he's wandering the halls in his nightgown. 

The Industrialist pulls a pistol and begins firing into your crew. Someone falls, groaning. Your crew fire back and the Industrialist falls dead, a red hole in his throat.

You take the Lost Love from his cellar. She will be returned to the Blue Kingdom where she belongs.
translation:
你同意和平地离开并不再回来。实业家似乎为不用杀你而松了一口气。

第二天晚上，你带着你的列车员回来，借助一根撬棍闯入了这个地方。开始一切都很顺利，直到你惊讶的发现在实业家穿着睡衣在大厅里闲逛。

实业家掏出一把手枪，开始向你的手下开火。有些人倒下，呻吟着。你的列车员开枪还击，实业家倒下了，他的喉咙上有一个红色的洞。

你从他的地窖里带走了失落的爱人。她将被送回属于她的蓝色王国。

original: Consequences
translation: 后果

original:
This time your preparations to meet the Sun's Daughter are half-baked. Your tongue is a wisp of smoke; Correspondence symbols flicker weakly across your skin. Her radiance sears you with a terrible, bone-deep pain.

"I told you the consequences would be severe," she says, and her every word is a spear that impales. "Your crew will be slain. And you will suffer."
translation:
这一次，你为会面太阳之女所做的准备是不成熟的。你的舌头仿佛一缕轻烟无法言语：信符在你的皮肤上无力地闪动。她的光芒让你感到可怕的、深入骨髓的痛苦。

“我告诉过你后果会很严重，”她说，她的每一个字都像是刺穿你身体的矛，“你的手下会被屠戮。而你将蒙受痛苦与折磨。”

original: Pay the terrible price
translation: 付出可怕的代价

original: All you can do is writhe, pinned in place by words that flay and scald and seethe through your bones.
translation: 你所能做的就是痛苦的挣扎，被那些如同剥皮般疼痛、烧伤皮肤的和刺痛骨髓的话语钉在原地。

original: The Arbiter's curse
translation: 仲裁者的诅咒

original:
Under her gaze your skin cracks and crumbles. Worms twine themselves through your flesh. When you return you have been transformed into a crawling clod of infested soil.

You slither to the Furrows, inch by decaying inch, and burrow. You linger for a month in the ground, every moment a torture.

After a week, a skeletal arm emerges from the toxic earth. Then a skeleton; it gradually develops muscles, blood vessels, flesh...

Finally, a version of you has grown that is healed and new. You return to the near-empty engine. Your one surviving crewmember cannot (or will not) relay what happened to the rest.
translation:
在她的注视下，你的皮肤出现了裂纹并开始分解。蛆虫像麻绳一样缠绕在你的血肉之中。当你回过神来，你已经变成了一个蠕动着的无数蠕虫寄生在上的肉块。

你爬到沟壑里，血肉一寸一寸地腐烂，然后挖出了一个地洞。你在泥土下苟延残喘了一个月，无时无刻不感到折磨。

一个星期后，一只骨瘦如柴的手臂从有毒的土地上冒了出来。然后是骨架，随后它逐渐长出了肌肉、血管、肉块……

最后，一个新的，仿佛大病初愈的你生长出来。你回到了近乎空无一人的机车。你唯一一个幸存的列车员不能（或不愿意）向你转述期间发生的事情。

original: The Arbiter's Request
translation: 仲裁者的请求

original:
"I can perform miracles, traveller," says the Sun's Daughter, her eyes blossoming like flowers. "There are only two things you can do that I cannot. The first is die. The second is exit the Blue Kingdom. Fortunately for you, I require the latter."

The sky shatters; her mouths sing something similar to laughter. "I have decided to establish a Blue Kingdom embassy in the Reach. Our isolation must end. I have chosen you for this task."
translation:
“我可以行使奇迹，旅行者，”太阳之女说，她的眼睛如花般绽开。“只有两件事你能做到而我不能。第一件是死亡。第二件是离开蓝色王国。你很幸运，我想要的是后者。"

天空碎裂；她的嘴里唱出类似笑的声音。“我已经决定在外野建立一个蓝色王国的大使馆。我们的孤立状态必须结束。我选择由你来完成这项任务。”

original: Agree to help establish the Blue Kingdom embassy
translation: 同意帮助建立蓝色王国的大使馆

original: The Embassy will not just facilitate relations, but also spread the Blue Kingdom's philosophy and influence.
translation: 大使馆不仅要促进与外界的关系，还要传播蓝色王国的理念和扩大其影响力。

original: A pact
translation: 一份契约

original:
The Sun's Daughter accepts your agreement with the unhesitating ingratitude of someone very accustomed to the world reshaping itself in her favour. 

"You will not be alone in this task," she says. "Waiting at the station you will find my other chosen representative: a Yoked spirit who, in life, was famous for his charisma and genius. He has received special dispensations that allow him to venture outside of the Blue Kingdom without being unmade."
translation:
太阳之女毫不犹豫地接受了你的协议———就像一个非常习惯于世界因她喜好而改变的不懂感恩的人一样。

"在这个任务中，你不会独自一人，"她说，"在车站等着你的是我选择的另一个代理人：一个缚链灵，在生前他以他的魅力和天才而闻名。他已经获得了特殊的豁免，允许他在蓝色王国之外冒险而不被解体。"

original: Refuse the Arbiter's request
translation: 拒绝仲裁者的请求

original: You will not help the Blue Kingdom expand its influence.
translation: 你不会帮助蓝色王国扩大其影响力。

original: A violent exile
translation: 一个暴力的流放

original:
"Then I have no use for you." The Arbiter's words crush you beneath them like boulders.

The palace falls away. Your new shape twists, folds, retreats. The flaming symbols that have replaced your flesh extinguish one by one. The stones in your eye-sockets shatter into teardrops and crumble down your cheeks. 

It is excruciating in a dozen different ways. The ache of a still-healing wound, the agony of scourged flesh, the pain of a bitter departure. 

When it is finally over, you find yourself once more confined to the twitching, decaying flesh-wreck that is your body. The Carefree Attendant solemnly helps you to your feet.
translation:
“那么你对我毫无用处。”仲裁者的话像巨石一样把你压倒。

宫殿崩塌。你的新形体不断扭曲、折叠、分解。取代你肉体的火焰符印一个接一个地熄灭。你眼窝里的石头碎成了泪珠，从脸颊上滑落。

这个过程包含着十几种不同的痛苦，包括尚未痊愈的伤口的疼痛、肉体被鞭笞的痛苦、离别的痛苦。

当改变最终结束时，你发现自己再次被困在一个不断抽搐的、会腐烂的、状况不佳的肉体中——这是你的身体。无忧的侍从庄重地帮助你站起来。

original: The Orator's Assignment
translation: 演说家的任务

original: [qvd:138976(assignment_description)]
translation: [qvd:138976(assignment_description)]

original: Accept the assignment
translation: 接受任务

original: You'll do your part to help spread the Philosophy of Culmination throughout Albion and the Reach.
translation: 你将尽你之责，帮助蓝色王国在整个阿尔比恩和外野传播终焉的哲学。

original: The beginning of something
translation: 某些事情的开端

original: The Orator's voice is sunshine breaking through the clouds. "Wonderful! I have every confidence in you, [qvd:131182(SpeechFormal)]."
translation: 演说家的嗓音宛如冲破阴云的阳光。“太好了!我对你有信心，[qvd:131182(SpeechFormal)]。”

original: Refuse the assignment
translation: 拒绝任务

original: Another will be available in a week, if you so choose.
translation: 如果你选择这么做，一周后会有另一份任务。

original: A sigh of disappointment
translation: 一声失望的叹息

original: "Oh, I understand," murmurs the Orator. "Busy, busy busy, of course. But don't lose sight of the value of the work we are accomplishing here. Perhaps later, when it better fits your schedule..."
translation: “哦，我懂，”演讲者嘟囔着，“忙这个，忙那个，忙忙忙，当然了。但也别轻视了我们在这里所做工作的价值。也许下次吧，等你有空的时候……”

original: The Poetic Forged Companion
translation: 诗意的锻造同伴

original: The Poetic Forged Companion has installed themselves in the cabin nearest the hold. They are crouched at a desk, scratching away with a quill. Every now and again, they gaze out of the window to draw inspiration from the stars.
translation: 诗意的锻造同伴已经被安置在离车舱最近的房间里。它蹲在桌子旁，抓着羽毛笔。它不时地凝视窗外，从星星中汲取灵感。

original: Ask them to write you a poem
translation: 请他们为你写一首诗

original: It will reveal whether they have skill as well as inclination.
translation: 这将揭示他们是否有能力和倾向。

original: Magnificent!
translation: 文采飞扬！

original:
The Poetic Forged Companion clicks their quill against the inkwell, scratches something onto a slip of paper, and passes it to you.

[qvd:138893(WriteAPoem)][qvd:138888(WriteAPoem)]
translation:
诗意的锻造同伴用羽毛笔敲击墨池发出咔嗒咔嗒的声音，随后在纸条上划了些东西，然后递给你。

[qvd:138893(WriteAPoem)][qvd:138888(WriteAPoem)]

translation: 你的作品看起来怎么样？

original: A vision indeed
translation: 确实是一个愿景

original: This state of affairs cannot continue
translation: 这种情况不能再继续下去了

original: You have had enough.
translation: 你已经受够了。

original: Ask if they are happy in their post
translation: 询问他们是否对自己的职位感到满意

original: What is happiness, anyway?
translation: 总之，什么是幸福？

original: "I am neither happy nor unhappy," says the Poetic Forged Companion. "But I was created to serve you in the way that you chose, and spend my every moment doing just that. I want for nothing." They continue to stare at you with their [qvd:138894(Happy)][qvd:139010(Happy)] eyes until you turn away.
translation: “我并没有快乐也并没有不快乐，”诗意的锻造同伴说道，“但我生命的意义就是遵照你的心意，每时每刻为你服务。我什么都不想要。”它继续用[qvd:138894(Happy)][qvd:139010(Happy)]的眼睛盯着你，直到你转身离开。

original: That is all, for now
translation: 目前仅此而已

original: The Poetic Forged Companion will be here if you need them.
translation: 如果你需要的话，诗意的锻造同伴会在这里。

translation: 强健的锻造同伴

original: The Pugilistic Forged Companion has hung a punching bag and a weapons rack in their cabin, and is vigorously attacking the former. Despite the speed and power with which their fists are slamming into the bag, the Companion's body shows no signs of strain.
translation: 强健的锻造同伴在他们的小屋里挂了一个拳击袋和一个武器架，并大力攻击前者。尽管他们的拳头猛烈地砸在袋子里，但他们的身体没有任何紧张的迹象。

translation: 就这样吧

original: The Studious Forged Companion will be here if you need them.
translation: 如果你需要，好学的锻造同伴会在这里。

original: The Quartermaster's Office
translation: 司务长的办公室

original: "We don't usually get requests for returns." The Jaded Quartermaster is a shade with an almost spherical body, and a mask whose lips are pursed in frozen contempt. His voice mutters from a clay urn on his desk; you have to stoop to hear him. "The Blue Kingdom doesn't really do returns, as a rule."
translation: “我们通常不会收到关于归还的请求。 ” 疲倦的司务长是一个有着几乎是球形身体的遗魂，以及它戴着一个嘴唇紧闭的面具，面具上的嘴唇散发出冰冷的蔑视。他的声音从他桌子上的一个瓦罐中发出，你必须弯腰才能听到他的声音：“作为一项法则，蓝色王国并不真正做归还。“

original: Reclaim your face
translation: 拿回你的脸

original: The Quartermaster slams a stack of wax tablets on the desk. "Fill these out," he says. "And I'll need a Testament of the Feather too."
translation: 司务长砰的一声把一堆蜡片砸在桌子上。“把这些填了，”他说。“我还需要一份羽之证明。”

original: Saving face
translation: 拿回脸

original:
After peering through your signed and stamped tablets, the Quartermaster sighs. "Wait here," he says, picking up his voice-jar and heading for the door. "I'll need to retrieve your face from the Hall of Stoics."

He returns hours later, clutching something ragged and slight. He presses it onto your blank visage, and it settles like a spiderweb. 

The world regains its colour. Sounds are sharper. Smells, keener. You reach up with both hands and gently, reverently push against your familiar old eyes, nose, lips.

"No more going into the Catafalque unless you don't plan on coming back up," says the Quartermaster. "It's not healthy."
translation:
司务长仔细检查了你的签字和盖章的蜡片后，叹了口气。“在这里等着，”他提高了嗓音，拿起声音罐朝门口走去，“我得去斯多葛大厅把你的脸取回来。”

几个小时后，他回来了，手里紧握着某样破旧而轻薄的东西。他把它按在你的空白面容上，它就像蜘蛛网一样贴合了上去。

世界重新恢复了色彩。声音更加清晰，气味也更加敏锐。你双手举起，温柔而虔诚地抚摸着那些熟悉的老眼睛、鼻子和嘴唇。

“除非你打算再也不回来，否则别再踏进灵柩了，”司务长说道，“那对身体不好。”

original: Reclaim your name
translation: 重新获得你的名字

original: "A name's not as simple as a face," says the Quartermaster. "It can only be returned if you have permission from the Sun's Daughter herself."
translation: “一个名字可不如一张脸那么简单，”司务长说道。“只有当你拥有来自太阳之女自身的许可后，它才能被归还。”

original: A Fair Trade
translation: 一个公平的交易

original:
A name cannot be returned, but it can be exchanged. Or taken.

By order of the highest representatives of the Sapphir'd King himself, you have been granted the name of the Jaded Quartermaster. The nameless thing protests.

"I have many names to trade," the nameless one before you whines. "All the names of all the dead! Famous names! Forbidden names, secret and hideous and profound!"

No, says the Jaded Quartermaster. Only one name will do.

"An exchange, then," mutters the nameless thing. It scribbles a contract on a tablet of wax, and you sign. Your name is returned, and it is the Jaded Quartermaster once more.
translation:
一个名字无法被归还，但可以被交换，或者被夺走。

根据蓝宝石之王最高代表的命令，你已被授予司务长之名。那个没有名字的存在提出了抗议。

“我有很多名字可以交换，”你面前的那个无名之物抱怨道，“所有死者的名字！著名的名字！禁忌的、秘密的、可怕而深奥的名字！”

“不，”疲惫的司务长说道，“只有一个名字才行。”

“那就交换吧，”那个无名之物喃喃自语，它在一块蜡板上匆匆写下了一份契约，你签了字。你的名字被归还了，而它再次成为了疲惫的司务长。

original: Leave the Jaded Quartermaster in peace
translation: 让疲惫的司务长安宁一会儿

original: He mutters something at your retreating back. You escape into the world of mud.
translation: 他对着你离开的背影嘀咕了几句。你逃入了泥泞的世界。

original: Forging a Clay Companion
translation: 锻造粘土同伴

original:
Smoke rises from the chambers of the Forge; the air resounds with hammer upon gemstone. Spirits of air and darkness fly hither and thither, while Ministers in Red and Blue and Indigo labour over moulds and blueprints, written in starshine.

Supervising them all is the White Minister, who sits upon her lofty throne, which circulates the Forge at a stately pace.
translation:
烟雾从铸炉的密室中升起；空气中回荡着铁锤敲击宝石的声音。空气之灵与黑暗之灵四处飞舞，而身着红色、蓝色和靛蓝色的大臣们则辛勤地工作在模具和蓝图旁，这些蓝图是用星光书写的。

监督他们所有人的是白衣牧师，她坐在高高的王座上，以庄严的步伐环绕着铸炉巡视。

original: Consult the White Minister
translation: 请教白衣牧师

original: What is needed to create this companion?
translation: 创造这个锻造同伴需要什么？

original: A person in four parts
translation: 人的四要素

original:
The White Minister tells you that despite what anatomists believe, the essential building blocks of a person are: a body, a heart, a thought, and a voice. The last of those is most important for this task and so will be dealt with at the very end. 

She has a list of requirements for the rest, which she presents to you. The Clay Conductor grinds his teeth in frustration, but nods his head. "We will gather these immediately," he pauses and turns to you, "At the Captain's convenience, of course."
translation:
白衣牧师告诉你，尽管解剖学家们可能持不同观点，但构成一个人的基本要素是：身体、心脏、思想和声音。其中，声音对于这项任务最为重要，因此我们会将其放在最后处理。

对于其他要素，她列出了一系列要求，并向你展示。粘土人列车主管咬牙切齿地表示不满，但还是点了点头。“我们会立刻去收集这些，”他停顿了一下，转向你，“当然，要在车长方便的时候。”

original: Provide a body
translation: 提供一个身体

original: The White Minister has very specific requirements. Unfortunately, they do not naturally exist.
translation: 白衣牧师有着十分具体的要求。遗憾的是，它们并非天然存在。

original: A body reclaimed
translation: 一具尸体的再生

original:
The White Minister bends low, sheathing the silver blades in her forearms. She takes the condemned experiment from you. It rests in her arms like a child in a cradle. She promises she will give it a purpose it was denied.

The Conductor nods in satisfaction. "One step closer. Soon, the air will resound with our voices."
translation:
白衣牧师微微弯下腰，将前臂中的银色利刃收回。她从你手中接过那个违背伦理的实验品。它安详地躺在她的臂弯里，就像一个婴儿躺在摇篮中。她承诺会赋予它一个被否定的存在意义。

粘土人列车主管满意地点点头，“又近了一步。很快，空气中就会回荡起我们的声音。”

original: Provide a heart
translation: 提供一颗心

original: The White Minister asked for something that was once wild but is no longer; that knew freedom but is now trapped.
translation: 白衣牧师要的是曾经野性但如今不再之物；是曾经自由，如今受困之物。

original: A heart taken
translation: 摘出一颗心脏

original:
The White Minister lifts the cage delicately, holding the beast within to see into her eye. With one hand she unlocks the cage, with the other she breaks the beast's neck in a single clean snap. She carries its corpse away in stately procession.

The Clay Conductor watches impassively. "Soon, my companion will have their voice."
translation:
白衣牧师小心翼翼地抬起笼子，笼子里面的野兽看向她的眼睛。一手解锁笼子，另一手则干净利落地扭断了野兽的脖子。她庄重地带走了它的尸体。

粘土人列车主管面无表情地注视着。“很快，我的锻造同伴就会拥有他们的声音。

original: Provide a mind
translation: 提供一个灵感

original: A singer without inspiration might become competent, but never exceptional. The White Minister requires a thought to fill the Companion with fire.
translation: 一位缺乏灵感的歌手或许能够变得称职，但绝不会出类拔萃。白衣牧师需要一种思想来点燃锻造同伴的热情。

original: A mind cleared
translation: 洁净一种思想

original:
The White Minister leads you into one of the slimmest of the towers, and bids you sit over a small furnace for three days and three nights. The air is soon damp with steam and sweat, which the White Minister gathers in a small iron pot.

At last, you are free to go. The Clay Conductor hurries to examine you, and is not satisfied until he is certain you have not been diminished.
translation:
白衣牧师引领你进入塔楼中最纤细的一座，并让你在一个小炉子旁坐上三天三夜。很快，空气中便弥漫着蒸汽与汗水，白衣牧师将这些收集在一个小铁锅里。

最后，你终于可以自由离开了。粘土人列车主管急忙来检查你，直到他确信你没有变瘦才满意。

original: Provide a voice
translation: 提供一个声音

original:
The White Minister tells you that the vessel is ready. It is time for the last component of the Companion.
[This choice is irreversible.]
translation:
白衣牧师告诉你，容器已经准备就绪。是时候安装锻造同伴的最后一部分了。
[此选择不可逆。]

original: Almost born
translation: 即将诞生

original:
The White Minister leads you deeper into the Forge. The Clay Conductor barrels ahead of you, almost running into the Minister until a sense of self preservation stops him short. You emerge into a vault blackened by soot and coal dust. Slivers of gemstones sparkle in the ceiling, like stars in the firmament. Your footsteps echo and echo again.

In the middle of the vault is a slab of crystal. Upon the slab is a body. The Companion.
translation:
白衣牧师引领你深入铸炉。粘土人列车主管莽撞地跑在你前面，差点撞到白衣牧师，直到自我保护的本能让他猛然停下。你走进一个被烟灰和煤尘熏黑的地下室。天花板上镶嵌的宝石碎片闪闪发光，宛如夜空中的星辰。你的脚步声在里面回荡，一遍又一遍。

在地下室中央，有一块水晶石板。石板上躺着一具躯体。锻造同伴。

original: Leave this
translation: 离开这里

original: For the moment. The Clay Conductor might grumble; but you have business elsewhere.
translation: 目前来说，粘土人列车主管或许会抱怨；但你还有别的事要处理。

original: The Inhabitor of the Threshold
translation: 门槛住民

original:
The Inhabitor is one (or two) of the dead, and so forbidden to speak. Instead, it keeps the voice of a departed spirit in a clay jar, which speaks on its behalf.

"I have been appointed to conduct the Rites of Departure," the voice-jar says, in gravelly tones. "You have enjoyed the King's hospitality, for this span of the sky is His house, and you have eaten  bread from His table."

There is an expectant pause.

[qvd:139045(Metatext)]
translation:
门槛住民是亡者之一（或之二）。它们被禁止说话，而是将逝者之魂的声音封存于陶罐之中，由其代为发声。

“我已受命主持离魂仪式，”声音罐以沙哑的语调说道，“你们曾受国王款待，因为这片苍穹之下便是他的居所，你们也曾享用过来自他餐桌上的面包。”

随后是一片满怀期待的静默。

[qvd:139045(Metatext)]

original: Return to the relay
translation: 返回中继站

original: You leave the solemn shadows of the Inhabitor's hall, and climb back up the stairs.
translation: 你离开了门槛住民大厅庄严的阴影，重新爬上了楼梯。

original: Offer a gift of old fires
translation: 献上余火的礼物

original:
In the form of Navaratine gemstones, bright as sparks.
[Reduce Dining with the Dead by 3.]
translation:
以璀璨如火花的曩缚咤宝石。
[将与死者共餐减少3。]

original: Render under Caesar
translation: 凯撒的归凯撒（Render under Caesar）

original:
You pour the gems at the feet of the Inhabitor, covering first one pair, then the other. It gives a gracious gesture of gratitude with one elegant hand.

[qvd:139003(Debt)]
translation:
你将宝石倾倒在门槛住民的脚边，先覆盖了一对脚，然后又覆盖了另一对。它用一只优雅的手做出了一个优雅而感激的手势。

[qvd:139003(Debt)]

original: Leave behind a Vision of the Heavens
translation: 留下天界风景

original:
You have seen rare sights in the Kingdom. Perhaps it is fitting that they remain here.
[Reduce Dining with the Dead by 2.]
translation:
你已在这个王国见识过罕见的景象。也许把它们留在这里才最合适。
[将与死者共餐减少2。]

original: The mote in your eye
translation: 眼中的尘埃

original: "So be it," the Inhabitor says. "Wash the glory of His kingdom from your eyes with salt-water and ash. A bowl will be brought." Indeed, a bowl is brought, in the clamped jaws of a jackal-spirit. The ritual stings, but soon the dazzle is scrubbed from your sight. [qvd:139003(Debt)]
translation: “就这样吧，”门槛住民说道，“用盐水和灰烬洗净你眼中他那王国的荣光。会有人端来一个碗。”果然有一只豺狼鬼魂叼来了一个盛满了水的碗。仪式令人刺痛，但很快你眼前的炫目光芒就被擦去了。 [qvd:139003(Debt)]

original: Leave behind a Moment of Inspiration
translation: 留下一个瞬间的灵感

original:
It will remain in the lands that gave birth to it.
[Reduce Dining with the Dead by 7.]
translation:
它将留在孕育它的土地上。
[将与死者共餐减少7。]

original: Called home
translation: 回家

original:
What might that idea have become, if you had carried it with you? A poem? An invention? A grand scheme? What might it have changed? A mind? A heart? A future?

At a word from the Inhabitor it crawls from your skull and slithers across the floor, to coil about the servitor's feet.

[qvd:139003(Debt)]
translation:
如果你一直怀揣着那个灵感，它可能会变成什么呢？一首诗？一项发明？一个宏伟的计划？它可能会改变什么呢？一个人的思维？一颗心？一个未来？

只需门槛住民的一句话，它就会从你的脑海中爬出，沿着地面蜿蜒前行，缠绕在侍者的脚边。

[qvd:139003(Debt)]

original: Speak a Word of Parting
translation: 诉说出一个分别的言辞

original:
Deliver a word of farewell in the language of suns.
[Reduce Dining with the Dead to 0.]
translation:
以太阳的语言传达一句告别之语。
[与死者共餐的次数减少至0。]

original: Au revoir
translation: 永别（Au revoir）

original:
Fire roars from your mouth like a maned lion. Its blaze scorches the shadows from the chamber. The Inhabitor turns one of its heads away; the other is forced to shield its eyes with its arms. The jackals cower, frantically.

[qvd:139003(Debt)] Its voice shakes.
translation:
火焰从你口中喷出，像一头鬃毛狮子的咆哮。这火烧焦了房间中的幽魂。门槛住民转过头去，另一位用手臂遮住自己的眼睛。幽魂畏缩不前，惊慌失措。

[qvd:139003(Debt)]它的声音颤抖。

original: Offer a Testament of Salt
translation: 提供盐之证明

original:
The testament states that you have made indelible progress towards Death's Door. That the lands of the living hold no allure for you.
[Reduce Dining with the Dead by 7.]
translation:
证明你在通往死亡之门的道路上取得了不可磨灭的进展。生者的土地对你没有吸引力。
[与死者共餐的次数减少7。]

original: The promise
translation: 承诺

original:
The Inhabitor is satisfied. The Testament is a promise that you will return, sooner or later, to resume the pilgrimage of the dead. 

[qvd:139003(Debt)]
translation:
门槛住民很满意。盐之证明是一个承诺——你迟早会回来，重新开始死者的朝圣之旅。

[qvd:139003(Debt)]

original: Sacrifice an Indulgence
translation: 牺牲恩惠

original:
An Indulgence allows exemption from any law, any custom.
[Reduce Dining with the Dead to 0.]
translation:
恩惠可以免除任何法律、任何习俗的约束。
[与死者共餐的次数减少至0。]

original: Carte blanche
translation: 一张空白的写有署名的文件

original:
Your Indulgence carries the authority of the Westernmost King himself. The Inhabitor bows; an awkward endeavour. 

"I will arrange passage for you immediately. Please return to your conveyance."
translation:
你的恩惠本身就承载着蓝宝石之王的权威。门槛住民向你鞠躬：它们尴尬地努力着。

“我会立即为您安排通道。请回到您的机车上。”

original: Leave your heart in trust, as surety you will return
translation: 遗留你的心，作为你会回来的保证

original:
The spirit has seven parts. The heart is one. If you give it up, you will be lessened until you reclaim it.
[You will be permitted to leave, but your obligation (and your heart) will be waiting for you on your return.]
translation:
魂分七部。心为其一。如果你放弃了它，你会被削弱，直到你收回它。
[你将被允许离开，但你的义务（和你的心）会等你回来。]

original: A deposit
translation: 押金

original:
The Inhabitor crooks a finger. Your heart flutters like a thrilled bird, then gives a panicked palpitation. You feel a pain, followed by the needle-pricks of numerous legs climbing the inside of your ribs, and a lurching sensation as something shoves its way past your lungs.

A beetle, blood-red, crawls from your throat into your mouth. You spit it to the floor. It is the size of your fist. The Inhabitor picks it up. "I will keep it safe," it says, producing a wooden board and silver needle. With practised grace, the Inhabitor pins the beetle to the board alongside a half-dozen others. You feel a pierce of cold silver, deep in your breast.

"You may reclaim it on your return."
translation:
门槛住民弯了一根手指。你的心像受惊的小鸟般扑棱棱直跳，随后又慌乱地悸动起来。你感到一阵疼痛，紧接着，无数条腿像针扎一样在你肋骨内侧攀爬，还有某种东西挤过你的肺部时带来的颠簸感。

一只血红色的甲虫从你的喉咙爬到你的嘴里。你把它吐到地上。它有你拳头那么大。门槛住民把它捡起来。“我会帮你好好保管。”它说着，拿出一块木板和一根银针。门槛住民以娴熟而优雅的手法，将这只甲虫与其他五六只甲虫一起钉在了木板上。你感到胸口深处有一缕冰冷的银光穿透而过。

“等你回来时，你可以把它取回去。”

original: Enquire about the Rites of Departure
translation: 询问关于离别的仪式。

original: Claim ignorance regarding the customs of this realm.
translation: 声称对这个领域的习俗一无所知。

original: Xenia
translation: 待客之道

original: "Yes," the Inhabitor says, solemnly. "I understand that elsewhere the laws of hospitality have eroded beyond recognition. "A host has three obligations to his guest. The first is protection. The Westernmost King – with His sword of sunlight – shields us from the lawless miseries of other quarters of the sky. Here, you have seen the heavens as they are meant to be. "The second is sustenance. Thus He provides petrichor to nourish all who linger here. "The third is courtesy. For He has asked you no questions as to your nature or presence. You have been permitted, here. "In return, the guest has only two responsibilities: to be no burden, and to offer gifts unto their host before departure."
translation: “好的，”门槛住民庄重地说道，“我明白在其他地方，招待客人的礼仪已荡然无存。 “主人对客人有三项义务。 第一项是保护。蓝宝石之王——以他那柄阳光之剑——保护我们免受天空其他区域无序苦难的侵扰。在这里，你们看到了天空应有的模样。 “第二项是供养。因此，他提供了石之血来滋养所有在此逗留的人。 “第三项是礼貌。因为他没有询问你们的身份或来意。你们被允许留在这里。 “作为回报，客人只有两项责任：一是不给主人添麻烦，二是在离开前向主人赠送礼物。”

original: Ridding Yourself of your Companion
translation: 摆脱你的锻造同伴

original: [qvd:138886(Ridding)][qvd:138891(Ridding)][qvd:138890(Ridding)][qvd:138892(Ridding)] This episode must end. But how?
translation: [qvd:138886(Ridding)][qvd:138891(Ridding)][qvd:138890(Ridding)][qvd:138892(Ridding)]这个插曲必须结束。但如何结束呢？

original: Ask them to leave your vessel immediately
translation: 请此物立即离开你的机车

original:
You wish this to be over quickly.
[This choice is irreversible.]
translation:
你希望这一切能尽快结束。
[这个选择是不可逆的。]

original: A graceful departure
translation: 一个优雅的离开

original:
The [qvd:138886(Name)][qvd:138891(Name)][qvd:138890(Name)][qvd:138892(Name)] Forged Companion blithely makes their way to the hatch. "It is best if I open it myself," they remark as you reach for the fastenings. "If you do it, you will put yourself at risk of frostbite."

You stand aside, and the Companion opens the hatch just wide enough to slip out, pulling it closed behind them. You watch through the window as they drift off into the Wilderness. A patina of frost spreads over their leathery skin. It twinkles delightfully as they spin away from your engine. 

At last, you are free! The possibilities of a life without them stretch out before you. You might even forge a new companion.
translation:
[qvd:138886(Name)][qvd:138891(Name)][qvd:138890(Name)][qvd:138892(Name)]锻造同伴愉快地走向舱门。“最好由我自己来打开它，”这东西在你伸手抓安全带时说，“如果你来开门，可能会被冻伤。”

你站在一旁，同伴把舱门打开一个刚好够它钻出去的缝，离开后关上了舱门。透过窗户，你看着这东西慢慢飘入天野。霜冻的光泽在此物皮革般的皮肤上蔓延。当离开你的机车时，它闪烁着令人愉悦的光芒。

终于，你自由了！没有了这东西，生活的可能性在你眼前铺展。你甚至可以铸造一位新同伴。

original: Take your Companion apart, piece by piece
translation: 一块一块地拆掉你的同伴

original:
It is the only way you can be certain never to see them again.
[This choice is irreversible.]
translation:
这是确保你永远不会再见到这东西的唯一方法。
[这个选择是不可逆的。]

original: At least there is no struggle
translation: 至少没有挣扎

[qvd:138886(Destroy)][qvd:138891(Destroy)][qvd:138890(Destroy)][qvd:138892(Destroy)]

[qvd:138893(Destroy)][qvd:138888(Destroy)][qvd:138894(Destroy)][qvd:139010(Destroy)]

"I have heard the crew speak of it – it is an establishment at Port Avon, in possession of a fine collection of literature. The clientele must be cultured; perhaps they would appreciate an author in residence. If you wish to end our association, I will alight there. translation: 代理人上车

original: "Excellent! Go gather your things, now, and board the engine post-haste." Your new passenger – who you suppose could be loosely described as a spy – hurries from the office. The Orator's intoxicating voice drops in both pitch and volume. Suddenly, he is conspiratorial. "We are establishing a network across the stars, my friend," he says. "Because you are my friend. And so are all the fantastic people who have come to Hybras, all the artists, all the writers, all the impassioned new adherents of our great Philosophy. I have so many friends. A lesser man wouldn't know what to do with them all."
translation: “好极了！去收拾你的东西，现在就去，然后赶快上车。”你的新乘客——你认为可以宽泛地把他认定为一个间谍——匆匆忙忙地离开了办公室。 演说家那令人陶醉的声音在音调和音量上都有所下降。突然间，他变得诡异起来。 “我们正在建立一个跨越群星的网络，我的朋友，”他说，“因为你是我的朋友。所有来到海波拉的人都是如此，所有的艺术家，所有的作家，所有对我们那伟大的理念充满激情的新信徒。我有如此之多的朋友。一个小人物是应付不来他们所有人的。”

original: Refuse to take the passenger

original: "Oh, I understand," murmurs the Orator. "Busy, busy busy, of course. But don't lose sight of the value of the work we are accomplishing here. Perhaps later, when it better fits your schedule..."
translation: “哦，我懂，”演讲者嘟囔着，“忙这个，忙那个，忙忙忙，当然了。但也别轻视了我们在这里所做工作的价值。也许下次吧，等你有空的时候……”

original: A Voice for the Forge
translation: 铸炉之声

original:
The body on the slab is identical to the Clay Conductor, except in three details. Firstly, it is made of copper.  ("For its resonance," the White Minister tells you). Secondly, it looks less abraded than the Clay Conductor, with long copper eyelashes and smooth, metal skin. Thirdly, it is smiling.

[qvd:138988(Forge)]
translation:
板坯的身体与粘土人列车主管几乎一模一样，只有三个细节例外。首先，它是铜制的。 （“为了共鸣效果，”白衣牧师告诉你。）其次，它的磨损不像粘土人列车主管那样严重，还保有着长长的铜睫毛和光滑的金属皮肤。第三，它在微笑。

[qvd:138988(Forge)]

original: Offer your voice
translation: 献出你的声音

original: The point of this endeavour was to give the Conductor a singing partner. To take his voice would be counterproductive.
translation: 这样做是为了给粘土人列车主管一个唱歌的搭档。用他的声音会适得其反。

original: A sacrifice
translation: 献祭

original:
The Clay Conductor looks up, once, from the body of his new companion. "Thank you." His expression is  wistful, almost lost. 

The White Minister fetches her silver spindle. She catches your voice, and draws it out like a fisher pulling a salmon from a river. Your gorge rises; you feel like you are choking up everything that you have ever eaten. 

And then it is over. The White Minister shuts your voice in a small box and places it in the hollow of the companion's chest. She fetches a new voice from her collection: a battered, rasping thing – yours, now.
translation:
粘土人列车主管从他的新同伴的身上抬起头来。“谢谢你。”他的表情充满渴望，几乎迷失了自我。

白衣牧师拿出她的银纺锤。她捕捉到你的声音，把它画出来，就像一个渔夫从河里拉鲑鱼一样。你的喉咙变得难受：你觉得自己就像同时噎住了所有吃过的东西。

然后一切都结束了。白衣牧师把你的声音关在一个小盒子里，放在同伴的胸腔里。她从自己的收藏中拿了一个新的声音：破旧、刺耳——现在是你的了。

original: Allow the Clay Conductor to give up his voice
translation: 允许粘土人列车主管放弃他的声音

original: He wanted someone who could sing as well as he. There are sacrifices for every ambition.
translation: 他想要一个能唱得和他一样好的人。每一个野心都伴随着牺牲。

original: A sacrifice
translation: 献祭

original:
The Clay Companion looks at the body of the Companion. "They are beautiful. They need a voice to match." He nods, slowly. "Do it. I'd rather hear a song than sing again." He hasn't looked up. "Just make it fast."

The White Minister draws out a silver spindle from her sleeve. The last words the Clay Conductor says in his own voice are his request that you don't watch. 

Minutes later, there is a snap. The Minister has closed the Conductor's voice into a small box. She opens a hatch in the Companion and places the box in its chest. The voice she has fetched for the Conductor is nothing like his own one. It is ragged and plain, worn through overuse and suffering.
translation:
粘土人列车主管凝视着锻造同伴的身体。“这东西很美，需要一个与之匹配的声音。”他缓慢地点点头，“动手吧。我不愿再歌唱，宁愿聆听。”他没有抬头，“快一点。”

白衣牧师从袖子里抽出一根银纺锤。粘土人列车主管用自己的声音说的最后一句话是要求你不要看。

几分钟后，传来一声脆响。牧师把列车主管的声音关进一个小盒子里。她打开了同伴身上的一个小门，把盒子放进胸口。她为指挥家取来的声音与他原来的声音完全不同。它褴褛而朴素，因过度使用和痛苦而变得嘶哑。

original: Offer your voice
translation: 献出你的声音

original: The point of this endeavour was to give the Conductor a singing partner. To take his voice would be counterproductive.
translation: 这样做是为了给粘土人列车主管一个唱歌的搭档。用他的声音会适得其反。

original: A sudden change of heart
translation: 突然改变主意

original:
The Clay Conductor looks up, once, from the body of his new companion. "Thank you." His expression is  wistful, almost lost. 

The White Minister fetches her silver spindle, and advances upon you. She is about to hook the thread about your tongue, when the Clay Conductor cries out. "No! D__n you, Captain. Stop." 

The White Minister lowers her spindle and steps back. 

"This was a mistake—" His gaze falls a final time upon his companion. "Cover that up, please."
translation:
粘土人列车主管从他的新同伴的身上抬起头来。“谢谢你。”他的表情充满渴望，几乎迷失了自己。

白衣牧师拿起她的银纺锤，向你走来。她正准备用线勾住你的舌头，这时，粘土人列车主管喊道：“不！__的！不！别这样，车长。停下吧。”

白衣牧师放下她的银纺锤，向后退了一步。

“这是个错误。”他最后一次凝视着他的同伴，“请把它盖上吧。”

original: Assist the Copper Companion
translation: 协助铜伴

original: With a melodic groan, it lumbers to its feet.
translation: 随着一声长长的呻吟，它蹒跚地站了起来。

original: A Clay Choir
translation: 粘土合唱团

original:
When the Companion speaks, their voice does not sound like it had when it was yours. But there is an echo of you about it – it's you when you were tired, or bored, or unwilling. "I can manage."

The Clay Conductor doesn't appear to notice. "Of course. Come, we must get back to our engine." The Companion nods. "Then we can practice together." They walk away, the Companion trailing slightly behind. 

The White Minister fetches a long silver trumpet with which to inspect your voice, which she measures in the octaves of the Blue Kingdom. When she is finally satisfied, she dismisses you.
translation:
当锻造同伴开口说话时，发出的声音听起来不像是曾经的你。但你还是从中辩认出一些——那是你在疲惫、无聊或不情愿时发出的声音。“我可以自己站起来。”

粘土人列车主管似乎没有注意到这个问题。“当然了。来吧，我们必须回到机车上。”同伴点点头，“然后我们可以一起练习和声。”他们走了，同伴在后面紧紧地跟着。

白衣牧师取来一支长长的银色号角，用来检验你的嗓音，她用蓝色王国的八度音阶来衡量你的音准。当她最终满意后，便让你离开了。

original: Assist the Copper Companion
translation: 协助铜伴

original: With a melodic groan, it lumbers to its feet.
translation: 随着一声长长的呻吟，它蹒跚地站了起来。

original: A Clay Chorister
translation: 一个粘土合唱家

original:
The Clay Conductor rushes to support the Companion, who gazes at the Conductor blankly. When they speak, their voice has a resonant echo of the Conductor, though in a more pleasing register. "I can manage."

The Clay Conductor doesn't appear to notice, hurrying to support the Companion. "Of course. Come, we must get back to our engine." 

The Companion nods. "Good," they say, in the Conductor's voice. "Then we can begin to practice together." 

The Conductor smiles, but weakly. They walk away, together, out of the Forge, leaving you to follow behind.
translation:
粘土人列车主管连忙去搀扶他的锻造同伴，后者茫然地望着列车主管。当那东西说话时，声音有着列车主管一样的嘹亮回响——尽管是在一个更悦耳的音域。“我可以自己站起来。”

粘土人列车主管搀扶着同伴，似乎没有注意到这句话。“当然了。来吧，我们必须回到机车上。”

同伴点点头。“好，”它用列车主管曾经的声音说道，“然后我们可以开始一起练习。”

列车主管虚弱的笑了笑。他们走了，一起离开了铸炉，留下你在后面跟着。

original: Speak to the Clay Conductor
translation: 和粘土人列车主管谈谈

original: The White Minister is covering up the hollow copper shell with blue cloth, and summoning spirits to convey it away.
translation: 白衣牧师正用蓝布盖住空心的铜壳，并召唤鬼魂将其运走。

original: A lonely wish
translation: 孤独的愿望

original:
The Clay Conductor turns to face you, but his eyes are unseeing. His voice cracks. "We can – we can talk on your engine. I'll be along shortly." He looks back at the body on the slab, now shrouded in blue cloth. "Go, before I say something I'll regret. Besides what I've already said today." 

The White Minister bows, briefly, as you pass by.
translation:
粘土人列车主管转身向你，但他的眼睛之中没有神采。他的声音仿佛受到了打击。“我们可以离开了，我们可以在你的机车上谈谈。我很快就会过来。”他回头看了看蜡版上被蓝布笼罩着的身体，“走吧，在我说一些让我后悔的话之前——除了那些我今天已经说过的话。” 

当你经过时，白衣牧师简短地鞠了一躬。

original: A Definitive Work
translation: 权威著作

original: [qvd:138978(art_description)]
translation: [qvd:138978(art_description)]

original: Agree to help disseminate the artwork
translation: 同意帮助传播艺术品

original: The style of the Blue Kingdom, and specifically the tenets of the Philosophy, have become something of a sensation in the contemporary art world.
translation: 蓝色王国的风格，特别是其理念的信条，已经在当代艺术界引起了一定的轰动。

original: Ready for delivery
translation: 准备运输

original: "Capital!" says the Orator. "When you return to your engine, you shall find the artwork already waiting in your hold. I took the liberty of arranging matters ahead of time."
translation: “车长！”煽惑人心的演说家说。“当你回到机车的时候，你就会发现艺术品已经在货舱里等着了。我冒昧地把这一切都提前安排好了。”

original: Refuse to deliver the artwork
translation: 拒绝派送艺术作品

original: Another will be available in a week, if you so choose.
translation: 如果你选择这么做，一周后会有另一份任务。

original: A sigh of disappointment
translation: 一声失望的叹息

original: "Oh, I understand," murmurs the Orator. "Busy, busy busy, of course. But don't lose sight of the value of the work we are accomplishing here. Perhaps later, when it better fits your schedule..."
translation: “哦，我懂，”演讲者嘟囔着，“忙这个，忙那个，忙忙忙，当然了。但也别轻视了我们在这里所做工作的价值。也许下次吧，等你有空的时候……”

original: Beyond Death's Door
translation: 死亡之门的里侧

original:
Logoi hound your locomotive, circling like comets, spitting fire-invective and flame-oaths, the weight of their anger so potent it buckles metal and cracks glass. But they can't keep up. You instruct your navigator to hold steady.

Ponderously vast, the golden Door opens. A cold, surgical light spills out. The daily tithe of spirits go rushing in.

And, far above the throng, your engine barrels screaming through. For a moment, the light subsumes you.
translation:
圣言像彗星一样盘旋在后，追赶着你的机车，如同咒骂一般向四周喷吐着火焰。它们的愤怒如此强烈，以至于让机车的金属弯曲、玻璃破碎。但它们无法跟上你的速度。你命令领航员保持稳定。

金色的大门缓缓开启，浩瀚无垠。一道冰冷的、手术般的光线从外面刺入。每天都有鬼魂自死亡之门涌入。

同时，在这群鬼魂的上空，你的机车呼啸着驶过。有那么一瞬间，光芒淹没了你。

original: Turn back
translation: 回头

original: Death's Door has not yet closed.
translation: 死亡之门还没有关闭。

original: Madness averted
translation: 避免狂行

original:
When you turn to your crew, they quail. Ever since you first ordered them to travel through the Door, something in your eye has left them as terrified as the death-light pouring through the windows.

You issue the order. Turn back.

Howls and sobs of relief. They work with the determined desperation of the reprieved. Your locomotive retreats back through the Door, slipping through moments before it thunders shut.

The Logoi chase you far from Death's Door, swollen with righteous fury. Your crew vow to never mention this day again; a vow which some will break, in whispers, on their deathbeds.
translation:
当你看向你的列车员时，他们畏缩着，拒绝与你对视。自从你第一次命令他们穿过这扇门之后，你眼睛中的某些东西已经让他们感到恐惧，就像窗外那倾泻的死亡之光一样。

你下达了命令。掉头。

机车上爆发出欣喜的狂笑和解脱的啜泣声。他们就像被判了死刑的人突然获救一般充满了坚定的信念在奋力工作着。你的机车从门里离开，在大门砰然关闭前的那一刻溜走了。

圣言追逐着你远离死亡之门，仿佛充满了某种正义的怒火。你的列车员们发誓再也不会提及这一天——也许他们会在临终前悄然打破这个誓言。

original: Rage against the light of dying
translation: 怒斥消逝的光明

original:
You will not go gently. On all mortality's behalf, you will mount a (certainly futile) attack on death itself.
[This will kill you more thoroughly, perhaps, than anyone has ever been killed.]
translation:
你不会温和地走入。你将代表所有的凡人，对死亡本身发起（当然是徒劳的）攻击。
[这将会更彻底地杀死你，也许比任何人死得都要彻底。]

original: Rage, rage
translation: 怒斥吧，怒斥吧

original:
You are now in the heart of the Sapphir'd King's power. An ocean of kaleidoscopic machinery. Wheels taller than mountains, turning, vanishing. Rivers of torrential architecture. Songs in cages. 

After a moment to appreciate the spectacle, you order your crew to ready the cannons.

Thunderclaps echo across the Blue Kingdom. Celestial machinery crumbles beneath the fury of your artillery. You punch holes through language. Pillars tumble. Chains shatter.
